Flavor additives commonly found in electronic cigarettes used by millions of Americans can damage joint health – even without any nicotine, according to a study published Wednesday.

Cinnamon and menthol flavors proved especially harmful, causing ATDC5 cartilage cells to die, researchers at New Jersey’s Seton Hall University said.

And the chemical flavors were also shown to disrupt the cells’ ability to build and maintain healthy tissue, triggering inflammation in the cells and turning on changes in the body that lead to tissue breakdown and cause swelling.

"Our findings show that e-cigarette flavor additives are far from benign additives," Jessica Cottrell, an associate professor at the school, said in a statement.

"Even without nicotine, these chemical agents alter metabolism, gene expression and inflammatory pathways, which underscores an urgent need to examine how vaping impacts broader musculoskeletal and tissue health."

open image in gallery Additives found in e-cigarettes have been found trigger inflammation and cause cell death, New Jersey researchers say ( AFP via Getty Images )

Other research has shown that cinnamaldehyde – a main compound in cinnamon flavorings – is tied to death in lung and respiratory cells, Cottrell and her co-authors noted.

And other studies published by Rutgers University and University of Hawai’i researchers showed other negative effects of menthol in e-cigarettes.

The researchers chose five flavors based on popularity in the U.S., including tobacco, strawberry kiwi and flavorless additives.

Some 7 percent of American adults reported using e-cigarettes in 2024, according to the latest federal data released in March. And 8 percent said they had used one in the past week in a 2025 Gallup poll.

open image in gallery E-cigarettes aren’t considered safe but have been found to contain heavy metals and cancer-causing chemicals ( Getty Images )

E-cigarettes aren’t considered safe, but experts generally say they’re less risky than smoking tobacco because they don’t burn material. Smoking tobacco is what causes about 20 percent of all cancers, according to the American Cancer Society.

Still, e-cigarettes contain addictive nicotine, a chemical stimulant that creates addiction.

The battery-powered devices have also been found to contain heavy metals, volatile organic compounds and cancer-causing chemicals, the American Heart Association warns.

“The liquid used in e-cigarettes can be dangerous, even apart from its intended use. Children and adults have been poisoned by swallowing, breathing or absorbing the liquid through their skin or eyes,” the association wrote.

Jos Buttler misses out through injury and Jofra Archer is rested for England’s upcoming ODI tri-series against Pakistan and Sri Lanka.

From 18 October, England will play two matches against each side in Pakistan, before the tri-series final on 31 October in Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore, as Brendon McCullum’s side look to build on the recent home white-ball success against Sri Lanka.

England beat Sri Lanka 3-0 in the T20 series and 2-1 in the ODI series last month but two stars from those matches won’t be travelling to Asia, with Buttler missing out due to the hamstring injury he sustained during the recent series and Archer rested as they continue to manage the fast bowler’s workload.

open image in gallery Jos Buttler was injured against Sri Lanka last month ( PA )

In better news, Adil Rashid is fit again after a hand injury ruled him out of the Sri Lanka wins, while Sam Curran returns from a groin injury.

On pitches that should spin plenty, Glamorgan leggie Mason Crane – who is uncapped in the ODI format – is called into the squad eight years after making his previous England appearance in the fifth Test of the 2018 Ashes in Sydney.

Sussex pair James Coles and Henry Crocombe, who were both part of white-ball squads this summer but are yet to make their debuts, are also included, while Joe Root continues his busy year by being included in a squad captained by Harry Brook.

England selector Marcus North said: “The tri-series in Pakistan provides another valuable opportunity for our ODI squad to test themselves against quality opposition in different conditions.

“Adil Rashid and Sam Curran return to the squad following their respective injuries while Jofra Archer has been rested to manage his workload following a busy summer.

“Mason Crane has been performing consistently for Glamorgan across both formats during the summer. He’s an experienced, high-class leg-spinner who thoroughly deserves another opportunity at international level.”

open image in gallery Mason Crane has played for England Lions recently ( Getty )

Kevin Pietersen is not part of McCullum’s coaching staff for this series, which was always expected but the former England batter will resume his mentor role for the winter series against Australia and South Africa.

After Marcus Trescothick was placed in interim charge for the 3-0 Test series win at home to Pakistan, he is given this series off and Mike Yardy will step up as batting coach after time coaching in England’s youth set-up.

News.title: Chewing tobacco killed 250,000 people in one year, study shows
News.content:
Chewing tobacco killed around a quarter of a million people in 2023, with use of the product remaining stubbornly high, according to research.

The smokeless tobacco is particularly popular in south Asia that is placed between the cheek and lower gum. It is flavoured and sometimes sweetened, and users often spit out unwanted juices while chewing. It is often viewed as safer than smoking but it is a major cause of stroke, as well as head and neck cancer.

Chewing tobacco is different to white snus or nicotine pouches, which contain no tobacco. These white pouches are also made up of flavourings and sometimes sweeteners, and deliver a hit of nicotine through the lining of the mouth.

Despite a successful fight against smoking over the last few decades, rates of chewing tobacco use have fallen little and it has often been overlooked in tobacco control efforts, researchers point out. In a study published in the Lancet Global Health, researchers from the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation in the US estimate that 241 million people aged 15 years and older used chewing tobacco in 2023.

Researchers looked at data on use in 204 countries between 1990 and 2023 and found that there was no significant decrease in the number of users of chewing tobacco over that period. And in 24 countries there was a significant uptick in the number of people using the product. Researchers estimate that about one in five men and one in 10 women in south Asia chewed tobacco in 2023.

Bangladesh has seen the biggest increase in the number of people using the product with 15 million new users between 1990 and 2023. Nepal, Madagascar and Yemen also saw increases in the number of users.

In India 105 million people chew tobacco regularly, accounting for just over two thirds of users globally. Historically, Indians would chew paan, tobacco in its raw form which was mixed with betel leaf and areca nut, a mild stimulant. But the use of chewing tobacco exploded in the 1980s when manufacturers began grinding these into a powder and selling them in packets known as gutkha. This was banned in 2012 but is still widely available. Chewing tobacco is also popular in Pakistan, China and Vietnam.

News.title: Esther Rantzen dies aged 86
News.content:
Dame Esther was a vocal supporter of the Assisted Dying Bill, claiming in March that most people “want and need” the right to end their own lives.

When the bill was defeated in the House of Commons in September, as MPs voted 286 to 270 against the legislation, she called it a “tragic day”. The bill would have allowed those with less than six months to live to seek medical assistance to end their lives.

In 2024, she said that she had joined the Dignitas assisted-dying clinic in Switzerland.

Writing for The Telegraph at the beginning of September, Rebecca Wilcox, Dame Esther’s daughter, said her mother was “too ill now to travel to Dignitas as she had planned and paid for”.

Earlier this month, Dame Esther said in a statement that it was too late for her to “buzz off” to the clinic in Switzerland and said Britain’s current laws on assisted dying are “messy and cruel”.

In a final message shared by her family, the presenter said she had been “immensely lucky” for the support she had received from the public, which she said had enabled her “to live such a long and happy life”.

She added: “Sadly, all good things come to an end, as they say. So I particularly wanted to say goodbye and thank you so very, very much. Perhaps I will see you eventually, on the other side. I do hope so. With very good wishes, as ever, Esther.”

News.title: Laptop running slowly? These tips will improve performance (and save your sanity)
News.content:
MacBooks and Windows laptops both have modes intended to maximise battery life. Low Power Mode (Mac) and Power Saver (Windows) should be avoided if you want peak performance.

On a Mac, you’ll find the Low Power Mode switch in Settings > Battery. For the best experience, set this to Never, but remember to change it back if you need your MacBook to last longer.

On a Windows laptop, there are two controls you need to consider. Both are found in Settings > System > Power & Battery.

Energy Saver mode uses multiple tactics to reduce battery consumption, including lowering maximum power. Switch this off, and you have access to Power Mode controls.

Your options are Best Power Efficiency, Balanced and Best Performance. While Balanced is the default, I was able to unlock up to 33 per cent more power by playing around with these settings using my own laptop.

To make matters more complicated, some laptops have their own performance modes. Many Asus laptops have MyAsus or Armory Crate, for example. Lenovo has the Vantage app, Dell has MyDell, and MSI laptops have MSI Center.

3. Stop applications from opening on start-up

If your laptop is slow when it first starts up, it may be because a whole bunch of apps have been given the green light to wake up with it.

Some applications such as antivirus software are critical, but most can be toggled off. As an example, I make sure apps such as Spotify, Steam and WhatsApp don’t open on startup; I only launch them when I need them.

On a MacBook, you can see which apps have this permission in Settings > General, under Open at Login. Select an app entry and click the “minus” button to remove it.

On a Windows laptop, you’ll find the list of start-up apps in Settings > Apps > Startup. Each entry has a little on/off slider.

News.title: Why the UK medicine supply chain is dangerously exposed to global shocks
News.content:
The UK’s medicine supply chain is dangerously exposed to global shocks, experts have warned, with the NHS dependent on a system where much of the world relies on a handful of countries for its drug supplies.

India and China are the backbone of the global medicines market, manufacturing around two-thirds of the world’s active pharmaceutical ingredients. This leaves countries exposed to factory shutdowns, natural disasters, geopolitical tensions, shipping disruption and sudden changes in the price or availability of raw materials, experts told The Telegraph.

“We rely now more than ever on other countries to make sure we can get access to the medicines that the vast majority of people take,” said Dr James Davies, director of research and insights at Community Pharmacy England.

Nearly all the active ingredients in the UK’s most widely used medicines are made overseas, around 80 per cent of them in China and India, leaving the NHS exposed to shocks thousands of miles beyond its control.

The resilience of Britain’s medicine supply has eroded gradually in recent years, as global instability has placed growing strain on the supply chains it depends on.

“We’ve seen more global turbulence in general,” said Dr Davies. “It’s not unique to the UK, but it’s affecting countries across Europe, across the Western world, with the Iran war, with difficulties flying things over Ukraine and Russia, and challenges with shipping in the Red Sea.”

In the UK, shortages have been reported across a wide range of products, including antibiotics, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder medicines, epilepsy treatments, hormone replacement therapy, and some diabetes medicines.

The drugs most at risk are the cheapest and most widely used – statins, blood pressure pills and antibiotics – taken by millions of people and manufactured in China and India at huge scale and minimal cost.

“Some antibiotics are almost exclusively made in China,” said Dr Davies. “For some of the blood pressure medicines, they’re more likely to be made in India. But across the board, those two are where most of the raw ingredients for those active pharmaceutical ingredients come from.”

News.title: Fraudster jailed for 41 years over Pakistani nurse scam in Saudi
News.content:
A fraudster who sent 92 Pakistani nurses to Saudi Arabia on fake documents in an elaborate scam to provide workers for short-staffed Gulf hospitals has been jailed for 41 years.

Ghulam Zulfiqar Ali used forged experience certificates, created fake verification QR codes and phoney employment platform IDs.

Ali was being paid by the Saudi authorities to find staff, but also charged genuine Pakistani nurses who wanted a job overseas, in a racket that has caused major embarrassment to the Pakistan’s authorities.

Gulf nations including Saudi Arabia are experiencing a severe shortage of nurses, compounded by rapid population growth, a rising burden of chronic diseases, and heavy dependence on nurses from abroad.

The World Health Organization (WHO) forecasts a global shortfall of 4.5 million nurses by 2030, and recruiting nurses for developed countries is a lucrative trade.

The 91 women were all genuine nurses, but did not meet the criteria for the “Nurse Highly Qualified” visa category under which they were sent.

When the Saudi authorities realised the fraud they deported all the nurses.

Syed Shehzad Nadeem Bukhari, director of Pakistan’s Federal Investigation Agency, told the Telegraph: “They lost both their money and their employment, and the incident caused serious embarrassment to Pakistan internationally.”

Investigators found that between October 2022 and September 2023, a Pakistani employment firm called M/S Sahou Manpower obtained permissions for the recruitment of 108 nurses for a Saudi-based manpower company, to work in hospitals under the visa category “Nurse Highly Qualified”.

The investigation found the Saudi employer bore all recruitment costs, including visa processing fees and air tickets.

It paid the Pakistani recruiting firm between $800 (GBP 600) and $1,100 (GBP 830) per candidate. However, Ali was also demanding between $800 (GBP 600) and $1,000 (GBP 750) from each nurse.

Investigators found the candidates were genuine nurses, but did not meet experience requirements and were given fake certificates.

Meanwhile Ali had not uploaded their details to Saudi systems designed to verify and check qualifications and give each applicant a QR code. Instead he provided them with faked QR codes and verification platform IDs.

Ali was convicted of cheating, two counts of forgery and emigration offences.

He was given 41 years imprisonment by the special court in Rawalpindi. He was also fined £1,904 and ordered to pay £25,031 compensation – £272 to each of the 92 nurses.

His accomplice, Ghulam Fareed, was given three years’ imprisonment and a £544 penalty.

Nasreen Begum, one of nurses, told the Telegraph: “We are thankful to FIA for compensation. Most of us have genuine qualifications as nurse-midwives, licenced practical nurses, clinical nursing assistants and a lady health visitor but our documents weren’t verified and that landed us in a difficult situation.”

Zeenat Khan, another victim of the fraud, said she had opted to take a job in Saudi Arabia because she was jobless despite having nursing qualifications.

She said: “I have three kids and wanted to give them a good education. Now, I hope to get back my money,” she said.

Swera Ali said she had been working in a private hospital in her native Lahore, Punjab province, but received only £50 a month and performed 16 hours duty.

She said: “My parents took a loan from relatives to facilitate me, but my hope of making money from an overseas job was short-lived when they deported us after less than a month.”

Mr Bukhari added: “The investigation established that their nursing diplomas were genuine. The fake QR codes and fake [employment platform] IDs were created by the accused, and the experience certificates were forged by the visa agent without the knowledge of the nurses.”

News.title: How vaccines and antibiotics can beat some cancers
News.content:
At least one in eight cancers worldwide are caused by viruses and bacteria, according to a new study published in The Lancet.

An estimated 2.3 million new cancer cases in 2024 – out of a total of 20 million recorded worldwide – were caused by common infections, almost all of which could have been prevented with treatments such as antibiotics or vaccines.

Almost half of infection-linked cancers, around 760,000 cases, were caused by H. pylori, a bacterium that infects the stomach, researchers from the International Agency for Research on Cancer found.

The pathogen, which is typically ingested through contaminated food and water and is carried by around 60 per cent of the world’s population at any given time, can remain relatively undetected in the gut for between 20 and 40 years without causing any symptoms.

If left untreated, it can trigger chronic inflammation in the stomach and cellular mutations that, in some cases, lead to gastric cancer.

Cases of stomach cancer linked to H. pylori are particularly common in East Asia, where roughly 80 per cent of the population carries the bacterium. This is due in part to the prevalence of a more aggressive strain of the pathogen, known as CagA, which is endemic to the region.

East Asian diets – which typically include salty, pickled or smoked foods – can also damage the stomach’s protective lining and accelerate the inflammatory processes that can contribute to stomach cancer, researchers have found.

While H. pylori infection is treatable with a course of antibiotics, its symptoms often mimic those of other digestive problems and can be difficult to distinguish without testing.

This means the infection can remain undetected for years, allowing inflammation and damage to progress.

News.title: ‘Pooled’ TB testing could save money and improve diagnosis, study finds
News.content:
Mixing phlegm samples from multiple patients in “pooled tests” for tuberculosis could halve costs and help find millions of missing cases, according to a major new study.

While most advances in fighting TB come with a large price tag, the shift in strategy could dramatically boost access to diagnosis and save money, experts said.

TB is the deadliest single infection globally, killing around 1.3m people every year, despite being both preventable and curable.

The gold standard in diagnosis is rapid molecular testing, which detects genetic material from the bacteria causing TB in patient sputum samples within hours. But each sample needs a specialist diagnostic cartridge that costs around US$8, beyond the budget of many poorer countries even before recent aid cuts.

In a pooled test, samples from multiple individuals are tested in one cartridge. If the result is negative then all of them are reported to be negative, but if the result is positive each is re-tested individually.

Results published in The Lancet Global Health found the strategy, with up to four patients in each pool, used half as many cartridges as individual testing – 7,028 compared to 14,362. It detected 84.9 per cent of people with TB compared with 88 per cent for individual testing.

The study involved more than 14,000 people whose symptoms suggested TB in Bangladesh, Brazil, Cameroon, Kenya, Malawi, Nigeria and Vietnam.

Sports.title: Man City could face legal action over tax evasion after secret payments to Roberto Mancini are exposed
Sports.content:
Next

ROBERTO MANCINI’s secret side contract while he was Manchester City manager has put the club in danger of legal action by the taxman.

Italy boss Mancini has denied any wrongdoing in relation to the consultancy agreement with a UAE club owned by City chief Sheikh Mansour.



But some tax experts believe City and its executive team could face a massive financial penalty and even criminal proceedings.

An independent disciplinary commission described as a “sham” the arrangement to pay Mancini a tax-free £1.75m a year for four days per annum of coaching at the Al Jazira Sports and Social Club.



That sum was LESS than the £1.45m per year after tax City were officially paying him for his main job as head coach.

The three-person panel found the Al Jazira payments were funded by City owners, the Abu Dhabi United Group, and were in fact extra remuneration for Mancini.

In that case, the thinktank Tax Policy Associates claims the total payments of £8.87m should have been subject to income tax and National Insurance contributions, with the onus on City to make sure they were paid.

Financial journalist Dan Neidle reckons City could owe up to £24m for the Mancini agreement alone, once interest and penalty fees are added to unpaid tax.

HMRC and the courts made a similar judgement about Rangers after the Glasgow giants paid players and other employees £47m in tax-free loans through Employee Benefit Trusts.

Tax debts drove Rangers into liquidation in 2012 and the current club is considered a new entity.



What are Man City charged with? THE Premier League claim Man City hid £900m in 'sham' deals across a nine-year period. They were found guilty on 114 of the initial 115 charges – with the number now up to 130 charges – which fit into six categories… Failing to give accurate financial information over sponsorship revenue, related parties and operating costs between 2009-10 and 2017/18. Total charges: 50

Failing to provide full details of managerial remuneration between 2009/10 and 2012/13. Total charges 8

Failing to provide full details of player remuneration between 2010/11 and 2015/16. Total charges 12

Failing to comply with Uefa Licencing and Financial Fair Play regulations between 2013/14 and 2017/18. Total charges 5

Breaching Premier League Profitability and Sustainability rules between 2015/16 and 2017/18. Total charges 25

Failing to co-operate with the Premier League investigation between 2018/19 and 2022/23. Total charges 30

Total charges: 130

In addition to the Mancini agreement, the PL commission highlighted two other sham arrangements with other unnamed individuals, which could also have tax implications.

Even an honest mistake in such matters could incur a fine on top of unpaid tax.

But deliberate evasion is a criminal offence which is punishable by up to seven years in jail.

HMRC are likely to also be interested in the “sham” image rights agreements City had with players, paid through a company called Fordham but also funded by ADUG.



The commission found the payments to players were inflated above the actual value of the image rights and were therefore a way of artificially increasing their remuneration without paying the correct tax.

HMRC went after Portsmouth for a similar scheme when the club collapsed into administration for the first time in 2010.

The taxman decided image rights payments to players including Sol Campbell were higher than their value – and even used the same legal term “sham” to describe the arrangements.

City’s offences appear much more serious and it would be a major surprise to many if HMRC did not take action.

The Etihad club strongly deny all claims and plan to appeal their guilty verdict.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s five biggest tantrums after quitting Portugal duty including Spurs storm-off & referee meltdown
Sports.content:
Next

CRISTIANO RONALDO has sensationally left Portugal’s squad for their Nations League clashes this week after suffering a falling out with manager Jorge Jesus.

The legendary footballer was left on the bench for the side’s 2-1 victory over Norway in Oslo on Sunday, and things have since escalated to the point that the 41-year-old decided to leave the camp.



He claimed in a statement: “In due time, I will tell the truth to all Portuguese people about the reasons that motivated my departure from the national team, to which I have always devoted myself.”

But the Portuguese icon has a habit of losing his cool when things don’t go his way – and he does not appreciate being left on the bench.



Manchester United vs Tottenham Hotspur 2022

Erik ten Hag can attest to that fact, with the Dutch tactician struggling to get a tune out of Ronaldo after taking over from Ralf Rangnick at Manchester United in 2022.

The Red Devils walked out 2-0 winners while hosting Tottenham Hotspur in October, but Ronaldo was not impressed as he watched on from the sidelines.

The star had been left on the bench in favour of Marcus Rashford in the No9 role, and he was so frustrated by the situation that he walked down the tunnel early and was even reportedly out of the stadium before the match wrapped up.

An icy Ten Hag later praised his “11 players who defend, 11 players who attack” and said of the incident: “We will deal with that on Thursday. I saw him leaving but I didn’t speak to him after.”

Piers Morgan interview 2022

Not content keeping his issues with the club under wraps, Ronaldo told all in a bombshell interview with Piers Morgan just weeks after the tense fixture against Spurs – an interview that was so explosive it prompted the termination of his contract.

He laid bare his issues with the hierarchy at the club, and slammed both Rangnick and Ten Hag, saying of the former: “If you’re not even a coach, how are you going to be the boss of Manchester United? I’d never even heard of him.”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

And he was just as damning of Ten Hag, who was still his coach at the time, saying: “I don’t have respect for him because he doesn’t show respect for me. If you don’t have respect for me, I’m never gonna have respect for you.”

He also took some unexpected jabs at former team-mate Wayne Rooney, saying: “I don’t know why he criticises me so badly… probably because he finished his career and I’m still playing at a high level. I’m not going to say that I’m looking better than him. Which is true…”

Al Nassr vs Al Hilal 2024

One of Ronaldo‘s most heated confrontations with an official came during his current spell with Al Nassr, when he very nearly lashed out after being show a red card against Al Hilal.



The star appeared to elbow opposition defender Ali Al-Bulayhi in the chest during their Saudi Super Cup clash, prompting a major brawl and a red card.

But unable to take the punishment with grace, Ronaldo momentarily looked as though he was about to punch the ball at the referee’s back, before thinking better of it and lowering his arms.

He then tapped the official’s shoulder and gave him a sarcastic thumbs up as he trudged off the field to chants of “Messi”.



Portugal vs Serbia 2021

As we and the entire nation of Portugal have seen recently, it is not just at club level that Ronaldo is willing to test the limits of his professionalism.

That was clear at the end of Portugal’s World Cup qualifier clash with Serbia in 2021, when the then-Juventus star’s apparent late winner was booted off the line by Stefan Mitrovic – with the linesman controversially agreeing that the ball had not yet crossed the line.

Ronaldo furiously shook his head in disbelief, and began trudging off the field while waving his hands in the air disapprovingly, before finally taking off his captains armband and throwing it to the floor behind him on the pitch.



Some fans saw the gesture as disrespectful to his nation, though he released a statement shortly after that read: “There are difficult times to deal with, especially when we feel that an entire nation is being harmed. Lift your head and face the next challenge now! Strength, Portugal.”

World Cup 2022 strop

Portugal did eventually qualify for the 2022 World Cup, but things did not get much smoother there, as Ronaldo struggled to impress early in the tournament.

He was not pleased to see himself hooked for Andre Silva against South Korea, with his obvious display of frustration rubbing manager Fernando Santos the wrong way.

Santos refused to rule out dropping the captain after slamming his conduct, saying: “Have I seen the images? Yes, I didn’t like it, not at all. I didn’t like it.”

He followed through on the threat and dropped Ronaldo for their Round of 16 clash with Switzerland, in which a hat-trick from his replacement Goncalo Ramos helped fire the side to a 6-1 win.

Sports.title: Rashid, Curran return from injury as England rest Archer for ODI tri-series
Sports.content:
Adil Rashid and Sam Curran have been recalled to England's ODI squad after recovering from injury, but Jofra Archer will be rested for the tri-series against Pakistan and Sri Lanka.

Three uncapped players are included in the 16-player squad for the series in Pakistan, which will see Harry Brook's side play each opponent twice. Spinner Mason Crane is included eight years on from making his last international appearance, which came in the final Test of England's 2017/18 Ashes tour.

Sussex duo James Coles and Henry Crocombe could also make their ODI debuts having been included after being part of England's white-ball squads earlier this summer.

Rashid featured as England beat Sri Lanka in a home T20 series in September but the spinner then missed the ODI matches that followed because of a hand injury.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sam Curran took three wickets in the space of six balls, including the huge scalp of Virat Kohli, as England beat India in the series-deciding third ODI at Lord's.

Curran had appeared to be in contention for a first Test appearance since 2021 before his summer was ended by groin surgery in August, but the all-rounder is on track to be ready to play in Pakistan.

Archer came through a summer playing across formats for England and in The Hundred, but with tours of Australia and South Africa to come during a busy winter, national selector Marcus North has decided to rest the fast bowler.

England are also without Jos Buttler after the former skipper was ruled out of the tour with a hamstring injury suffered against Sri Lanka last month.

North said: "The tri-series in Pakistan provides another valuable opportunity for our ODI squad to test themselves against quality opposition in different conditions.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jofra Archer flattens the middle stump to help wrap up Sri Lanka's innings.

"Adil Rashid and Sam Curran return to the squad following their respective injuries while Jofra Archer has been rested to manage his workload following a busy summer.

"Mason Crane has been performing consistently for Glamorgan across both formats during the summer. He's an experienced, high-class leg-spinner who thoroughly deserves another opportunity at international level."

Pietersen not part of coaching staff

Having been relieved of his Test duties earlier in the summer, Brendon McCullum oversees a rotated coaching staff that does not feature Kevin Pietersen.

The former England star was appointed last month as a specialist mentor for the white-ball sides and began his role during the two series against Sri Lanka.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kevin Pietersen speaks to Nasser Hussain about his new role as an England white-ball mentor and how his relationship with Brendon McCullum has developed.

As was planned, Pietersen is not set to be with the side for this tour, but will resume his role during November's tour of Australia.

McCullum will be supported by Jeetan Patel, Mike Yardy, David Saker and Carl Hopkinson.

There is expected to be continued rotation of McCullum's staff as England continue a congested schedule building up to the 50-over Cricket World Cup next year.

Sports.title: Russell reveals his Mercedes upgrade hope in Antonelli title chase
Sports.content:
George Russell is hopeful Mercedes' long-awaited car upgrade at the Bahrain Grand Prix will further help his performances as he bids to build on his return to winning ways from Azerbaijan last week.

Russell dominated the Baku event to not only secure his first win in seven races but also claim the maiden 'Grand Slam' of his Formula 1 career, meaning he led every lap from pole position and set the fastest lap.

The Briton had been happier with his performances in Mercedes' W17 since the August summer break, yet he had still finished behind title-leading team-mate Kimi Antonelli in each of the previous three races, with Antonelli extending his championship advantage to 81 points after victory in Madrid.

But after reducing that deficit by 15 points last Saturday on a weekend that Antonelli finished only fifth after crashing in qualifying, Russell is feeling optimistic as he goes in search of the first back-to-back wins of his F1 career on the sport's return to Malaysia's Sepang International Circuit - a track neither of the title contenders have driven on before.

"As I've really said this whole season, firstly I never really felt in a position to fight for the victories because I didn't feel that the performances were strong enough," replied Russell when asked if another win could sow some doubts in Antonelli's mind.

"But now, finally, I feel I'm in a place where I can fight for victory week in week out.

"Of course, there is a big deficit in the championship but we're only two thirds of the way through. There's a third of the season to go and still so much can happen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Anthony Davidson takes us through Lewis Hamilton's 2017 pole lap around the Sepang International Circuit.

"So I'm just going to go race by race. I'm enjoying it more than I have done recently, just because I feel more at one with the car, and hopefully this new upgrade with a few characteristic changes are also going to play into my favour a bit more. So, bring it on."

Discussing what had changed for him, Russell said that "I don't really feel lost anymore" and that his "confidence is back and growing again".

"It's definitely been a conscious adjustment of my driving," he explained.

"I think I went through a few races when I was having to think how to make those adjustment, whereas now it's all a bit more intuitive and natural.

"What I set out to achieve in terms of getting the car in a slightly better window, I'm now achieving without having to think about it as much, so I can just focus on driving fast."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater gives his verdict after the Azerbaijan GP, where George Russell pipped Max Verstappen to victory.

Russell reiterated that all the pressure was on Antonelli in the chase for the Drivers' Championship over the closing two months of the season.

"For sure there's a lot of pressure in his position," added Russell.

"For any driver fighting for your world championship there's a lot of pressure. At this point of the season it is his to lose so, from my side, I'm just going to go out there and enjoy every race."

'My grandmother went back home!' - Antonelli hopes to learn from Baku lessons

Despite finishing only fifth at the last race, Antonelli remains in firm control of the world championship with his 66-point lead still the joint-second highest he has held this season.

But the 20-year-old Italian said that the events of last week had taught him some valuable lessons.

"Last weekend was probably the worst weekend from me, from my side, of the season," said Antonelli.

"But still very good learning from the weekend. It was also a very strange race for me in Baku [from 16th on the grid] because it was one of those races where I consciously tried not to take any risk and just drive under the limit, which was very weird but it was a good and what I needed. I needed a clean result after a very disrupted weekend.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli hits the wall during qualifying at the Azerbaijan GP.

"But after the race I wasn't happy with the result but I learned many things and the most important learning is I need to always be 100 per cent and I really do my best to achieve the best result.

"If I don't try to do everything right in my power than nothing is going to come my way."

And having joked that he had driven like his grandmother, Antonelli quipped on Thursday: "My grandmother went back home! I booked her a flight and she's back in Italy!"

On Russell, Antonelli added: "He did an incredible weekend in Baku and he's got the momentum.

George has been doing great, especially last weekend, so it's going to be a tough challenge but I'm looking forward to it."

What are Mercedes expecting from Malaysia car upgrade?

Russell and Antonelli's prospects of winning on Sunday are set to be boosted by the introduction of an upgrade package for the W17, Mercedes' first significant update since the Canadian Grand Prix in late May.

"It's a good step," said Russell. "We think it's a good step purely because it's been so long since we last brought some upgrades.

"It's quite abnormal to have an upgrade back in May and then only again in October.

"So, as an individual upgrade step it's large, but in a normal season it's just the normal trajectory you would expect from a May to October upgrade package.

"Hoping it's going to propel us back to the front on these types of circuits, which have been more challenging for us in the past six races."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Mercedes have won the last three races to extend their lead over Ferrari at the top of the Constructors' Championship to 160 points. However, two of those tracks - Monza and Baku - played to the strengths of their engine, while Antonelli was fortunate to win on the streets of Madrid after a Virtual Safety Car helped him and hindered McLaren's Lando Norris.

"I think we have a very efficient car on the circuits that are lower drag, so in Azerbaijan, Monza we were very competitive. Red Bull were also on the podium in Monza as well as in Azerbaijan," added Russell.

"I expect Malaysia to be slightly more closer to the circuits of Madrid, Budapest, Zandvoort, where we saw likes of Ferrari and McLaren competing strongly, so that's going to be an interesting one."

Antonelli is also keen to see how the aerodynamic changes will help the team on a track where medium-high-speed cornering is a crucial part of the lap.

"I think this weekend is the right one to bring it," he said.

"Our car is very efficient. It's not draggy, especially on tracks like Monza, Baku, where we were very quick because it's new tarmac, short corners.

"Whilst I think in these type of tracks without the upgrade we would struggle. For example, Zandvoort McLaren was very quick and Zandvoort has very open tarmac. So I think this race was the right one to bring the upgrades and see if we can improve on these kind of tracks with long corners and very old tarmac."

Sports.title: Alcaraz, Dart, Kartal win in Japan and China but Brits Norrie, Fery knocked out
Sports.content:
A bumper day of action on the ATP and WTA Tours at the China Open and Japan Open saw Carlos Alcaraz and Brits Harriet Dart and Sonay Kartal win. But there were defeats for Cam Norrie and Arthur Fery.

Alcaraz saved three set points before clinching a see-sawing opening set against American Alex Michelsen with a ​strong display in the tiebreak but continued to experiment with his new sped-up service motion and was broken twice early in the next set.

The ​23-year-old Spaniard, who had shown glimpses of his best form en ‌route to the US Open quarter-finals last month after his long injury layoff, recovered to move ahead but a ​double fault in the seventh game handed Michelsen a route back.

Michelsen capitalised and kept his composure in a tense finish to the second set where a fortunate netcord winner ​left Alcaraz stranded at the baseline and helped the 22-year-old American force ⁠a decider.

Alcaraz, who led Team Europe to a ⁠Laver Cup triumph over Team World on indoor courts in London last weekend, said the relentless rain in Tokyo limited his practice.

"It was really important to have ⁠this feeling for the next round, to know what I have ​to do for the next matches."

A couple of breathtaking points gave ​Alcaraz a 2-0 lead in the final set and the seven-times Grand Slam ​champion used the launch pad to close out a comfortable victory on a day ⁠of big upsets in the ATP 500 tournament.

The top seed's win came after third seed Taylor Fritz fell to qualifier Jaume Munar 6-7 (7-9) 6-4 6-3, sixth seed Casper Ruud lost to Luciano ⁠Darderi 7-6 (7-3) 6-3 and seventh seed Tommy Paul suffered ​a 6-1 6-2 defeat by Alejandro Tabilo.

Holger Rune, the former world No 4 ​who is stepping up his comeback from an Achilles injury, also crashed out in a 6-3 6-1 loss to Kyrian Jacquet.

Exits for Norrie and Fery as Dart, Kartal progress

Norrie was beaten 7-6 (7-1) 6-4 by newly-crowned US Open champion Alexander Zverev in the first round of the China Open in Beijing.

The Briton blew a set point opportunity then collapsed in the subsequent tie-break after taking the first point.

Zverev, who is intent on closing in on world No 1 Jannik Sinner, who is not playing in China, grabbed the crucial break in the ninth game of the second set before sealing his victory.

It was Zverev's ninth consecutive main tour victory over Norrie, who was playing his first match since his disappointing early exit at Flushing Meadows.

Sports.title: 'A lot of noise' - Norris explains why he made public apology to Colapinto
Sports.content:
Lando Norris has explained why he felt compelled to add a public apology to the private one he offered Franco Colapinto after strongly criticising the Alpine driver for causing a collision that took the Brit out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Lando Norris has explained why he felt compelled to issue a public apology to Franco Colapinto after already apologising privately to the Alpine driver for strongly criticising him over the collision that ended the Briton's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Colapinto locked up at a Safety Car restart and crashed into his Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly, who was then sent into Norris. All three drivers were forced to retire from the race, with Colapinto subsequently handed a five-place grid penalty for this weekend's Malaysian Grand Prix.

"It [the apology] was more for the wider audience, I would say. I said what I wanted to, to Franco, and he's the only one really that I need to share my opinion and share my apology with," said Norris.

"I don't need to do it on social media, and I don't think you need to use social media to make an apology. But at the same time, there was a lot of noise in the background, so I thought it was sensible to show publicly that I had apologised.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player There was carnage on the safety car restart after contact between Alpine team-mates resulted in Lando Norris crashing out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

"I accepted that I was wrong. I'm generally the same with my driving, to accept when I've done something wrong or accept something I've not.

"But because it was something I said on TV, I thought it was fair that I shared it with everyone, because they all saw it. I didn't think it was a true value of how I hold myself. At the same time, I still see social media at times and saw some bits, some not so good, some better."

Colapinto also apologised to Gasly and Norris for his mistake but says it's "tricky" to control social media backlash which he feels comes from "every fan base".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Norris was critical of Colapinto in the immediate aftermath of the Azerbaijan GP.

But Norris, who has previously been outspoken about online abuse, stated "some people can deal with it much better than others".

He added: "Sadly that's what we have to deal with - a lot of sports deal with it, which some of it is down to passion, which you have in sport and you see more of it because on social media it's easy to share your opinions.

"And to a certain extend I respect it [passion] but to the extent of online abuse, death threats - all those things are far beyond being a fan of a sport or a driver or a person.

"There's a line. It's not new. It's something that has been around every sport for a long time and highlights that social media platforms and sports need to do more to stop this kind of stuff from happening."

'I always trust him' - Colapinto to face no Alpine consequences

Colapinto says he does not expect to face any consequences from Alpine and insisted that he trusts Flavio Briatore after the team boss stated he would take time "reflect on what course of action should be taken" after the "very poor" error.

"There are times in the team when everyone is angry and it's tricky to move forward. But you always find a way," Colapinto said on Thursday.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Franco Colapinto shares the response of Pierre Gasly and Flavio Briatore to his Azerbaijan GP crash.

"Flavio is a great team leader. He's probably one of the best I've had in the sport since I started, and has a lot of experience, so he's very good at these situations, knowing how to manage them and knowing how to make the team better.

"I always trust him with kind of stuff. It's probably not the best when you are the one in the wrong and when you make a mistake.

"But it's great to have him and learn from it. I think it was a difficult situation for the team. He's a team leader, the one trying to make the team win again and making the team better."

On whether he expected to face any internal punishment, Colapinto added: "Not really. I think as a team, we keep focusing on the same thing.

"We review everything we learn from it. It's in the past for all of us already and we keep looking forward."

Sports.title: 'Point fingers somewhere else!' - Hamilton backs Vasseur but calls for Ferrari change
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has launched an impassioned defence of Frederic Vasseur as Ferrari's team principal and suggested he would like to instead see other structural changes at the team.

Hamilton was speaking two days after Ferrari took the unusual step of arranging a media briefing for journalists in which a spokesperson said the company's management retained "full confidence" in Vasseur in the wake of growing speculation around the Frenchman's position in the team principal role amid a run of five races without a podium.

Speaking ahead of this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Hamilton welcomed Ferrari's public move to silence the recent noise around the team - external criticism and speculation which the Briton said was "trying to break our spirit" but "not succeeding".

"I think it's good that they did it," said Hamilton of Ferrari's support of Vasseur.

"In terms of how it unifies the team, I think we already were unified. Honestly, outside sources seem to be so negative towards us as a team and be trying to break our spirit but they are not succeeding.

"So people can continue with the negative narrative but inside everyone is working really hard.

"Fred is the guy to lead us. He's doing a fantastic job. If you look at the history how many people they're swapping out that role and I feel like it's in a better place than it's been before, but ultimately it's not a one-man situation.

"It's lots and lots of people coming together and if you want to point fingers, point it somewhere else.There's people above that are also are a part of it as well. It's a lot of people.

"I feel like if you take things away from this message, Fred is in his position, he's not going anywhere and I'm here to stay with him and I still believe fully in where we're going."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton reflects on his Azerbaijan Grand Prix, which saw him finish sixth.

Former Renault and Sauber chief Vasseur is in his fourth season in charge of the Maranello F1 outfit since replacing Mattia Binotto in the role from 2023. The 58-year-old first worked with Hamilton in what is now F3 and F2 in 2005-2006 before reuniting when the seven-time world champion joined from Mercedes in a blockbuster transfer last year.

"I am happy with my treatment [by the team]. Fred has been fantastic working with me and I think our relationship as a whole, even with the bosses, is in a much better place than it ever was," added Hamilton.

"Of course, people making comments have absolutely no clue what they are talking about, ultimately, because they are not inside the team.

"What's happening in the team or how it's structured, where the weaknesses are, obviously I am in the team and I know all those - I'm not going to speak on them, but will I continue to try and work with those people that are in power to make the changes.

"Making changes is not a quick thing, people aren't always willing to do so very early on, but Fred has done a lot of the changes that I've asked for already and there are more for us to do."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jacques Villeneuve comments on the likelihood of Christian Horner joining Ferrari following his comments the team would be a 'dream role'.

Speaking to the written media, Hamilton added: "Fred is a fantastic leader. He really is the guy to take this team in the right direction. However, there is a structure that's there for some time. Whether or not that needs looking at moving forwards, there are also people above Fred, and it's not about one person.

"Fred has led the team, helped make changes in this past year. He's helped us get to the second Constructors' Championship. That's a huge step from last year. The deficit we have is simply just on engine, and that's something we're not we don't shy away from. We know that.

"Every weekend we carry a 0.4s deficit, if not sometimes 0.6s, just in straight-line power, and we're aware of it, and that's something we need to try to work on. They're working extremely hard to try and fix that for next year."

At Ferrari Vasseur is team principal and general manager of the F1 team and ultimately reports in to the heads of the whole company, which includes its road-car division, chief executive Benedetto Vigna and executive chairman John Elkann.

Image: Lewis Hamilton is third in the Drivers' Championship, with Ferrari second to Mercedes in the Constructors'

Asked about the comparison to his former team Mercedes, where Toto Wolff is the Brackley F1 outfit's team principal, chief executive and one-third co-owner with the German manufacturer and Ineos, Hamilton said: "There are changes that I would make but I'm not going to talk about what those are.

"Toto's in a different position to Fred.

"The structures are a lot different.

"That's all I can say on it really."

'It's not an easy time for Fred'

Image: Frederic Vasseur and Lewis Hamilton have known each other for over 20 years

Vasseur has overseen Ferrari's return to race-winning ways this year after a poor 2025 but their world championship challenge to Mercedes has faded in recent months with their last podium finish coming six races ago in Belgium.

The Frenchman signed a multi-year contract extension last year but there had recently been speculation in the Italian media about his job security beyond this season.

The focus on him was heightened last week by an interview published in The Times with former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner, who described Ferrari as "the dream" in Formula 1 and said it would be the only team he would consider coming back to the sport for without an equity stake.

Vasseur described the noise around him as "frustrating" after last Saturday's race in Baku.

Hamilton said he reiterated his own support to the Frenchman directly and believes changing team principal would only be "detrimental".

"I think it's not an easy time for Fred so it's good that the team came out with something earlier this week," added Hamilton.

"Not that it really changes much but at least gives him a little bit more confidence.

"I've also just let him know that I support him 100 per cent. I wouldn't be here without Fred and I really do believe Fred is the person to take us [forward].

"Swapping him out and putting [someone else in] it won't change how the team's moving forwards, if anything it will be detrimental to it.

"I think consistency with Fred, he knows the team, he helped the team build the best… I think we have had the best car this year, it's unfortunate we just have been down like four tenths every weekend on power, and that's just unfortunately something that is difficult to overcome. But we're working on that for next year."

Sports.title: 'A risk not worth taking' - PL execs not expecting clubs to vote for Man City expulsion
Sports.content:
Two senior executives at different top-level Premier League clubs have told Sky Sports News they would be "staggered" and "amazed" if 15 clubs were prepared to vote to expel Manchester City from the league, with such a move akin to a "self-inflicted commercial disaster".

Expulsion is one of several punishments available to the independent commission, which earlier this week found Man City guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought against them over alleged financial mismanagement. Other potential sanctions include a fine, a points deduction and/or a transfer embargo.

Man City remain adamant they are innocent and have vowed to fight the judgement.

Sky Sports News has been told discussions remain ongoing within, and between, the bosses of other clubs in the Premier League about how they might react to developments, with a number of them considering their own legal positions in terms of a possible financial claim against Man City.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Barristers and lawyers across the country are working with Premier League clubs over the prospect of bringing further litigation against Manchester City. City continue to deny all the charges and will appeal by Friday's deadline.

But in a new and surprising development, we have been told that many rival clubs consider Man City such a key part of the commercial attraction of the Premier League, both in the UK and globally, that if rival clubs voted to expel them, it would be as if those clubs were "cutting off their noses to spite their faces".

"If Man City were expelled, that would have massive commercial consequences for everyone in the league, and ultimately it would cost the other clubs an awful lot of money," one executive, who didn't want to be named, told Sky Sports News.

He went on to explain that, should such a decision come during this or next season, it would mean only 19 clubs playing the remaining fixtures, with broadcasters in the UK and abroad likely to seek refunds due to the reduction in the number and attractiveness of the games they had paid to televise.

Sponsorship and other corporate sources of funding might well be reduced across the board if the most dominant club in English football in the last two decades were no longer playing in the Premier League.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher believes stripping Manchester City of their titles should be part of their punishment after they were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of financial rules. The club continue to deny the breaches.

Similarly, expulsion would bring the futures of stars like Erling Haaland, Phil Foden and more into question, which would further risk the commercial attractiveness of the Premier League and, according to one source, would make expulsion "a risk not worth taking".

A further issue could be the uncertainty created by top clubs deciding to go against the recommended sanction laid out by the independent commission.

It's thought there is a counter-feeling among some top clubs that Manchester City remaining in the Premier League would be damaging to the brand and integrity of the competition, and that an extended period outside the top flight for City, even though it would lead to short-term financial pain, is necessary to maintain the league's global image for the future.

The differences of opinion within Premier League clubs will not affect the independent commission's decision, but it could be a factor if the clubs are forced to vote on City's possible expulsion.

If that commission were to recommend City be expelled, and then the Premier League clubs voted against such a move, it is unprecedented and unknown what - if any - punishment could then be brought against City.

Championship directors averse to Man City joining league

Latest from Sky Sports News' Lyall Thomas and Anthony Joseph:

Sky Sports News has sought out some of the current sentiment in the Championship about Man City potentially joining their league.

If there was an expulsion from the Premier League, Man City's future would then reside in the hands of the FA and EFL. A vote would have to take place involving all 72 clubs and a majority decision would be needed to determine where - and if - they enter into the EFL.

However, another possibility is a points deduction and one that could be severe enough to see Man City relegated to the Championship.

One top Championship club director believes Man City dropping into the Championship has "absolutely no" benefit for the league whatsoever and would prevent another club being promoted.

They said: "What benefit has the Championship got with Man City dropping into it? Absolutely none.

"The finances are so big they'll just blow the Championship away and go straight back up. So it kills a promotion spot for the other clubs. There isn't another club in the Championship that could handle that level of wealth."

Another Championship director told Sky Sports News: "Whoever is making the decision on any sanctions has to uphold the integrity of the whole English football pyramid - and not only be thinking of the Premier League.

"It shouldn't be the case that if they are expelled from the Premier League that they can just join the Championship. That should be for us to decide. They should have to earn their way back up English football."

Another Championship club source said: "It's not for us to comment on this process. There is a lot of uncertainty and speculation at the moment. But really no-one knows what's going to happen. I just hope that our [EFL clubs'] interests are considered and treated fairly."

Sports.title: Former Wallaby hooker Charles confirms MND diagnosis
Sports.content:
Nathan Charles has revealed his motor neurone disease (MND) diagnosis; the 37-year-old made four appearances for Australia across 2014 and 2015; Charles overcame cystic fibrosis to produce a decorated career in professional rugby

Former Australia rugby international Nathan Charles, who overcame cystic fibrosis to forge a professional career in a contact sport, has been diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND).

The 37-year-old Charles, who made his Test debut in 2014 and earned four caps for the Wallabies, including a 12-12 draw against New Zealand, revealed he has been diagnosed with the same illness as recently retired National Rugby League star Jai Arrow.

MND is an umbrella term for a group of progressive neurological conditions where the motor neurones degenerate. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is the most common form, and ALS is often called Lou Gehrig's disease.

During an interview with former Wallabies lock and now commentator Justin Harrison on Stan Sport this week, Charles revealed he had only recently been diagnosed.

"For a long period there I just didn't know what it was," Charles, who retired from professional rugby in 2018 said."I've had many tests and seen many doctors, but we just weren't getting any answers. My health just kept declining."

"And then recently, in the last few weeks, I was actually diagnosed with motor neurone disease, which has been extremely challenging and overwhelming. I know there's no cure and … your physicality, your body deteriorates and, yeah, your life cuts short."

Charles played Super Rugby for the Perth-based Western Force and Melbourne Rebels, as well as in England with Gloucester, Bath and Wasps. Since retiring, he has served as chief executive of Rugby Western Australia and been involved with Sydney University Rugby Club.

Former England rugby captain and 2003 World Cup winner Lewis Moody was diagnosed with MND last year.

Other high-profile rugby players to have died from the disease in recent years include Rob Burrow and Scottish rugby union great Doddie Weir.

Charles, on his personal website, said he was diagnosed with cystic fibrosis, which primarily affects the lungs and digestive system, when he was three months old and was told he might not live past the age of 10.

"I am constantly pushing the boundaries and am living proof that anything is possible," he said in a post raising awareness of the condition. "It is my personal mission to truly exceed the life expectancy of 37 years [which is the life expectancy of people with CF]."

Now, he said he is trying to deal with a medical setback for which there is currently no cure.

"I was born with a life-threatening illness. I've given that a red-hot crack. Now this other thing comes along," he said. "I find it quite ironic that something else will strike me down rather than what I've been dealing with for my whole life."

The Australian team, who are preparing for Bledisloe Cup Tests against the New Zealand All Blacks this month, posted a message of support on social media.

Wallabies captain Harry Wilson said: "We know you have a tough time ahead, but we're with you on every step of the way."

Sports.title: United States lined up to host first Women’s Club World Cup
Sports.content:
The United States is poised to host the first Women’s Club World Cup in January 2028, becoming the latest in a series of major Fifa tournaments staged in North America. Discussions to take the competition to the US are at an advanced stage, with Los Angeles and San Diego among the favoured host cities.

It will follow the men’s tournament, whose expanded version debuted last year, in being staged by a country that also hosted the men’s World Cup this summer.

While a deal is yet to be confirmed, the path has cleared for America to hold the 19-team event without going through a formal bidding process, even though Qatar was in talks with Fifa about hosting.

The winter scheduling will avoid a clash with the men’s Copa America, which the US is the frontrunner to host in June and July 2028, but raises the prospect of a hectic year-round calendar for the world’s top players. The Club World Cup is placed squarely between the 2027 Women’s World Cup and the 2028 Olympics, which will demand full-strength squads. A number of top clubs are in favour of a rule change limiting players to one international tournament per year, whether for club or country.

Fifa is keen to use the Club World Cup as a dry run for the 2031 Women’s World Cup, which the US will host in conjunction with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica in a decision to be formally approved at an Extraordinary Fifa Congress on 23 November.

Football’s global body is eager to assess the stadium venues, pricing and demand for tickets at the smaller 19-team Club World Cup before the 48-team World Cup three years later. Time to organise and market the Club World Cup is tight, given it will start on 5 January 2028.

Sources have cited the chaos engulfing Fifa’s leadership since the emergence of Gianni Infantino’s ill-fated FFE scheme as a significant reason for the backlog of hosting decisions still to be taken. In July, Europe’s top clubs threatened not to participate in future Club World Cups unless the FFE project was shelved. They also warned the threat would hold unless a joint venture between European Football Clubs and Fifa, agreed in outline form, but yet to be signed off, was completed before television rights could be sold for the women’s Club World Cup.

Another tournament awaiting a venue is the 2029 men’s Club World Cup. The US has expressed interest in hosting that competition, but should the women’s event be confirmed it appears more likely to be co-hosted by Morocco, Spain and Portugal before they jointly host the men’s World Cup the following year.
