Sports.title: Who is Rui Pinto? Man City whistleblower no longer a protected witness
Sports.content:
Rui Pinto is a name that has become as synonymous with Manchester City as Sheikh Mansour, Pep Guardiola and Sergio Aguero.

The whistleblower was behind the leaks of private documents that triggered the Premier League investigation into the Etihad outfit.



6 Local journalist Miguel Dantas claimed only his lawyer William Bourdon (R) and maybe his father have direct communication with Rui Pinto right now Credit: AFP

Over a decade after he created the Football Leaks website, Man City have now been found guilty on all charges of financial breaches.

Enzo Maresca's side continue to protest their innocence but, despite this, Pinto has called the decision ‘historic for English football’.

City's rivals are demanding that any sanctions come into effect this season, and they also face being sued for damages by other clubs.



All of this started with Pinto, who published a cache of confidential club documents on his Football Leaks website a decade ago.

He shared information with German magazine Der Spiegel, which included internal emails about sponsorship deals that have since been called 'sham' in the Premier League's verdict this week.



Who is Rui Pinto?

He's been called 'a great European whistleblower' by his lawyers, but to others he's been accused of harbouring more sinister intentions, having been convicted of attempted extortion in Portugal.

The 37-year-old, who is from Vila Nova de Gaia, near Porto, with FC Porto being the team Pinto supported as he grew up.



His ex-Geography teacher, Mario Falcao, explained to BBC Sport: "Rui was a perfectly normal pupil. He was nice, with his spiky hair; he was quite sociable but not extroverted.

"He had a good relationship with the teachers, although he did miss these classes quite often. His father was always on top of things, so in the end he passed quite easily."

6 Man City continue to plead their innocence with CEO Ferran Soriano (right) claiming the charges are a 'Premier League conspiracy theory' Credit: Getty

Pinto's father, Francisco, worked in a shoe factory and as an antiques dealer, while his mother sadly died when he was 11.



He undertook a history degree at his hometown university; however, he never finished the degree — and had no formal IT qualifications.

Pinto set up Football Leaks in 2015 to expose 'the hidden side of football' (his words) and was initially known by the pseudonym 'John'.

Portuguese journalist Antonio Varela was the first person contacted by Pinto, under the cover of his online identity, while he was working at the Portuguese sports newspaper Record that September.

"We realised that [Football Leaks] got the information illegally. But since the moment they publish the information on the site, that's public information," said Varela to the Beeb.



"You can't ignore that. Ethically, it's complicated, but the public interest is more relevant than the ethical issue. That was the conclusion."

6 City won three Premier League titles during the nine-year period in which their offences took place Credit: Getty

How did Football Leaks target Man City?

Pinto's early work on the website targeted two of the biggest clubs in his home country, Benfica, and his own beloved team, Porto.

Tales then emerged of bizarre clauses in players’ contracts - from Liverpool's anti-Arsenal proviso that was inserted in Roberto Firmino’s first deal, to Real Madrid playing down the figures behind Gareth Bale's move from Tottenham to preserve Cristiano Ronaldo’s status as the world’s most expensive player.



Football Leaks were also at the centre of Ronaldo's £16.5million fine and suspended jail sentence due to a tax fraud case in Spain.

The revelations soon became even more shocking once Pinto agreed to meet journalist Rafael Buschmann from Der Spiegel.

He supplied the German magazine and its partners in the European Investigative Collaborations group with more than 70million documents relating to football business.

In 2018, stories emerged of Bayern Munich's plot to start a breakaway European Super League; of City and Paris Saint-Germain’s failure to comply with financial fair play; and of a rape allegation against Ronaldo - who has always denied the claims and had a civil case against him thrown out of court in 2022.



UEFA launched an investigation into City following the release of Pinto's documents and initially banned the club from European competitions for two years.

6 Ronaldo denied Kathryn Mayorga's allegations, which were publicised by Der Spiegel, and has never been charged by police Credit: Getty

That ruling was overturned on appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport in 2020, as much of the case was 'time-barred'.

The Premier League had started its own investigation into possible rule-breaking in December 2018, and their independent charges were confirmed three years ago.



Rui Pinto no longer a protected witness

Miguel Dantas joined talkSPORT to react to the news that Pinto will no longer be protected as a witness by the Portuguese authorities.

On whether his compatriot is viewed as a hero or criminal, the local journalist told White & Jordan: "Rui is a divisive figure because a lot of people see him as a criminal, but then some other factions of people see him as a whistleblower.

"And I think it's important for us to realise that there wouldn't be a Manchester City financial scandal if he hadn't leaked the documents.

"I think it's important also to state that the timing behind this decision made by the Portuguese authorities is a little unbelievable because Rui Pinto has had witness protection for the past six years.



"But now, in the midst of the scandal that's now blowing up, that's when they decide to take the witness protection away from Rui.

"And he was assaulted in April, just a couple of months ago in Lisbon.

"He was punched, and the Portuguese police say that there's no security risk for Rui, which I can't really comprehend."

6 Pinto has been told to 'exercise caution with family contacts' and to stay off social media after losing his status as a protected witness Credit: AFP



Rui Pinto's legal issues Arrested in Hungary in March 2019 and extradited to Portugal Faced 147 charges, which included computer fraud, attempted extortion and violating the privacy of correspondence. Ahead of his criminal trial in Lisbon, Pinto spent more than a year in custody before going under house arrest In September 2023, he was convicted on five counts of 'illegitimate access' to IT systems, three counts of 'correspondence violations', and attempted extortion against the investment fund Doyen Sports. He received a four-year suspended jail sentence and was living under police witness protection until September 2026 In April 2026, Pinto was acquitted of all charges following a second trial on 241 alleged counts of illegally accessing email accounts belonging to Portuguese sports bodies (including Benfica).

Dantas, who covered both of Pinto's court cases in Portugal, has confirmed the hacktivist's location remains a secret.

"In six years, there were two times he was seen in public," he added on talkSPORT.

"Once in a supermarket, surrounded by Portuguese officers, the police officers. And another time when he went for a night out."

"Access to him is really, really hard to obtain," Dantas continued. "Impossible for me, I'll tell you. But only his lawyer and maybe his father have direct communication with him."



'His contributions far outweigh the errors of his past'

What Pinto said in court was that, as a football fan, he wanted other supporters to be aware of what was happening behind closed doors.

Asked whether he believes in that motivation, Dantas replied: "Well, I think that, and he said it himself, in the first couple of months, there was a window of opportunity that he could make money with some of those leaked documents that he hacked. And he tried.

6 Pinto, who wore a bulletproof jacket to and from hearings, was given a four-year suspended sentence in September 2023 Credit: AFP

"He admitted that he tried to do it, but then after a certain thing, there was a switch that lit up, and after that, I am sure that he became a full-on whistleblower.



"He made some errors in the past; there's no denying it. He admitted them. He never made one euro out of the leaked documents.

"There was never any money that he received. But you have to look at what he brought to the world - all the PSG, Manchester City, in Portugal there were a lot of investigations as well - tax evasion from the biggest football players in the world.

"I think that if you weigh the two things, I think that his contributions far outweigh the errors of his past."

Sports.title: Portugal manager Jorge Jesus doubles down on Cristiano Ronaldo decision in new update
Sports.content:
Portugal manager Jorge Jesus doubles down on Cristiano Ronaldo decision in new update

Portugal manager Jorge Jesus has refused to back down over his decision to leave Cristiano Ronaldo on the bench.

Ronaldo was an unused substitute in their 2-1 win over Norway and it was the first time in 18 years that he had not played a single minute despite being in the squad.

3 Ronaldo said no player would be happy with what happened with Jesus Credit: AFP

He played in their clash against Wales but endured a tough night, missing some big chances.

The decision by new head coach Jesus left the five-time Ballon d'Or winner furious, prompting an emergency meeting with the Portuguese Football Federation.

Following the talks, the 41-year-old released a statement promising that he 'will tell the truth' about why he departed the camp over his lack of minutes.

Additionally, his sister Elma Aveiro, also lashed out on social media claiming her brother had been treated with a lack of respect.

While Jesus insisted there was no rift and claimed Ronaldo was fully aware he might not feature in Oslo, talkSPORT revealed that the Al-Nassr striker felt misled by his manager regarding expected minutes.

Jesus has now doubled down on his decision on not bringing the ex-Manchester United forward on against Norway. He said: "I can promise whatever I want. I'm the coach, right?

"I'm the coach who told the player, 'You weren't going to play. I'll put you on the bench. If I need you for 30 minutes, then you'll play. If I don't need you, then you won't play.'

"Cristiano isn't going to, and no player will ever change my ideas as a coach. Never. Right?

"Not him, not anyone in football. Not him. Not anyone. Not any president. Never. Zero."

Facing a potential ban

It's not the first time Ronaldo has had a rift between him and a manager - others include Jose Mourinho, Rafa Benitez, Ralf Rangnick, and Erik ten Hag.

3 Ronaldo and Jesus have won silverware together at club level this year Credit: Getty

Additionally, Ronaldo is under threat of receiving a six-month ban and fine following his exit from the international team's camp.

The Portuguese Federation’s rulebook says a player who leaves a training camp, game or any activity related to the national team can be hit with a six-month ban.

The 41-year-old could also potentially be forced to pay a fine with his £488,000-a-day salary.

The rule states: "The player who, regularly called up, abandons or does not unjustifiably attend training, game or activity of the national teams or related to the sports representation of the FPF or Portugal,

"Is sanctioned with a suspension of one to six months and, incidentally and if he is a professional player, with a fine between 500 and 1,000 euros.

Ronaldo noted he would offer his full perspective in due course, but insisted he did not want to create a distraction for his teammates ahead of Thursday night's clash against Denmark.

3 Ronaldo's international career could be over - 23 years after making his debut Credit: Getty

The quest for 1000 goals

While many anticipated the Euro 2016 winner might follow Lionel Messi into international retirement after this summer's World Cup, Ronaldo has pressed on.

Since making his Portugal debut in 2003, Ronaldo has gone on to score 146 goals in 234 games. No player in history has ever scored more goals or registered as many caps in international football.

Additionally, Ronaldo is 21 goals away from reaching the historic 1,000 official career goals milestone and may want to reach the feat with the national team.

Sports.title: Sean Dyche gives update on managerial future eight months after Nottingham Forest exit
Sports.content:
Sean Dyche gives update on managerial future eight months after Nottingham Forest exit

Sean Dyche has admitted he is not desperate to return to football management and is currently enjoying working for talkSPORT.

The 55-year-old was sacked from Nottingham Forest in February after only four months in charge, and was more recently linked with Tottenham during their relegation scrap last season.

3 Dyche was one of four different managers in the City Ground dugout last season Credit: Getty

That was a job Dyche admitted he would have taken, but he was never approached by Spurs for the role.

He has been out of managerial work for five months now, as the former Burnley boss has become a regular pundit on talkSPORT.

The ex-Premier League manager has admitted he's currently enjoying his life without football.

He told talkSPORT: "We'll see. First thing's first, it's not easy to get any jobs in football. So you've got to first of all, get a job.

"But it's also got to be one that you want. The last few have been tough going. It's been heavy lifting when you're at clubs that need almost bailing out, and sort of stripping back and getting going again.

"It's enjoyable. Very enjoyable in one way, but it is heavy lifting. So we'll see. But at the moment, I'm quite enjoying doing all kinds of different things.

"That includes talkSPORT. There's so much out there now involving football, not just Premier League football."

The ex-Everton boss admitted to miss sitting in the dugout, and added: "Yeah, but I've done it for a long time.

" I still keep myself active. I mean, I'm still watching my son when I can and watching a few games when I can. I'm going down to Merthyr Tiddell with [fellow talkSPORT regular] Jonny Owen.

"We're going to do a sort of talk to raise some funds for them. So there's all sorts I'm getting involved with. I'm quite enjoying that side of it.

3 Dyche has been enjoying the media side of football during his time out of management Credit: talkSPORT

"But you know what it's like, never say never in football. The phone rings and you might just go, yep, come on and let's go."

Dyche has had an impressive career, and has mostly been successful working with teams that a small budget.

Most famously, he led Burnley to a seventh-place finish in the Premier League and a European spot during his incredible ten-year spell.

The Toffees brought in Dyche to replace Frank Lampard in January 2023 as the club was in turmoil.

As manager of the Merseyside-base club, he had the rug pulled beneath him as the club received an unprecedented ten point deduction

However, he pulled off survival on the final day of the season after a narrow 1-0 win against Bournemouth which featured a strike from Abdoulaye Doucoure.

3 Dyche has previously expressed that keeping Everton in the Premier League was one of his greatest achievements as a manager Credit: Getty

But at Nottingham Forest, things didn't go as planned, as after just 25 matches in the dugout he was let go in earlier this year.

The 55-year-old was brought in to replace the sacked Ange Postecoglou and to stabilize the team after dropping into the relegation zone.

Dyche won ten of his 25 games at Forest before being dismissed, despite losing just one of his final five matches.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel tipped to drop 91-cap England star in changing of the guard
Sports.content:
Jordan Pickford has been warned his time as England's No.1 will soon be up after James Trafford's impressive start to the season.

The Everton goalkeeper has been sat on the bench for the Three Lions' last two Nations League, as the youngster has stood in his place - even against world champions Spain.



3 Trafford kept a clean sheet on Tuesday to a 10-man Czechia Credit: AFP

The 32-year-old has been the undisputed first-choice for his country since he replaced Joe Hart in 2017, and has never been truly tested throughout his tenure.

Tuchel has been vocal that he saw this international break as an opportunity to start the Leeds keeper after he had an impressive start to his Premier League campaign.

Additionally, the England manager has already explained that both 'keepers will have the chance to start two games each in the four-match run.



Tuchel admitted: "I felt James deserved to get the two matches, that's why we gave him two matches. He started the Premier League season well and is getting minutes as No1 at Leeds.

"Jordan [Pickford] did absolutely nothing wrong, but we wanted to use this competition to see how far actually James is."



Pickford out, Trafford in?

On talkSPORT's Inside England, they discussed that after Trafford's first two games in the Nations League campaign, he may be England's No1 going forwards.

talkSPORT pundit and content creator Flex, said: "We’ve never seen Pickford properly challenged, there’s been guys where you say ‘let’s see how this goes’ like with Pope, then we realised.



"Ramsdale was getting in at Arsenal, went on a couple of loans and didn’t work out. Dean Henderson, did well at Crystal Palace after he needed to move away from Manchester United.

"He achieved historic things with Palace, but did you feel he was big or good enough to replace Jordan Pickford.

"He has never been truly challenged, and then there’s this emergence of this young kid who was outstanding for the under-21s, so he’s done it at youth level for the country.

3 The Everton stopper has remained the Three Lions' No.1 since Tuchel took charge in January 2025 Credit: Getty



"Then he plays really well at Burnley and gets a huge move to Man City but then they get Donnarumma - he’s stuck in limbo.

"But then he moved to Leeds. He’s starting to show there’s a lot of talent there, he is young, but he does believe in himself.

"He’s got a bit of a personality, like Pickford does so he fits the bill. I definitely think there could be a changing of the guards. I think it’s a very well-timed experiment."

The 23-year-old showed his quality by making an impressive save to deny Ferran Torres in the first half, and the goals they conceded were not particularly down to the Leeds goalie.



Notably, this marked the fifth occasion the Three Lions have conceded three or more goals in a fixture since 2022 - with Pickford failing to feature in any of those matches.

3 Pickford has 91 England caps, while Trafford has four Credit: Getty

Pickford has kept 46 clean sheets in his 91 appearances for England and has been a huge part of the Three Lions' recent success at major tournaments.

Meanwhile, Trafford's form this season has helped place Leeds in fifth position in the Premier League and the youngster has kept two clean sheets in the process.



However, Pickford is showing no signs of slowing down for the Toffees either and has kept five clean sheets in seven games this season.

The 32-year-old has also recently won the August Save of the Month award for a record-extending fifth time following his incredible stop against Crystal Palace.

Sports.title: Second Hull City star crashes on his way to training - in almost the EXACT same spot as team-mate who flipped his £160,000 Land Rover Defender three weeks ago
Sports.content:
Second Hull City star crashes on his way to training - in almost the EXACT same spot as team-mate who flipped his £160,000 Land Rover Defender three weeks ago

A second Hull City player has crashed their car on the way to training, just three weeks after their team-mate Sorba Thomas flipped his vehicle.

A Mercedes was pictured on its side on a residential road close to the Premier League club's training ground.

The identity of the player remains unknown, but midfielder Lucas Gourna-Douath posed for a photograph with the car in question in an Instagram post on Wednesday.

In a statement, the club said: 'Hull City is aware of images circulating on social media following a road traffic accident near the club’s training ground and can confirm that no one was harmed in the incident.'

Humberside Police have confirmed emergency services responded to an incident and that no-one was injured.

'Officers and emergency services were called to reports of a single vehicle road traffic collision on Millhouse Woods Lane in Cottingham at around 8.30am this morning (Thursday, 1 October 2026).

'Thankfully, no one was injured as a result of the collision.'

A second Hull City player has crashed their car close to the Premier League club's training ground

The identity of the player remains unknown, but midfielder Lucas Gourna-Douath posed for a photograph with the car in question in an Instagram post on Wednesday

Gourna-Douath, who signed for the Tigers in a £3million move from RB Salzburg in the summer, had recently received the new vehicle.

'Another one! 2026 GLC 53 sourced for Lucas Gourna,' the post read. 'Thank you for your order.'

The incident comes three weeks after Thomas flipped his Land Rover on the way to training.

The 27-year-old walked away from the crash, which happened on Millhouse Woods Lane in Cottingham at around 8.30am.

His vehicle, a grey Land Rover Defender with a personalised number plate, was pictured on its roof, with broken windows.

Residents had looked on stunned at the crash on the narrow road, where locals say speeds typically only hit 15mph.

Thomas escaped injury in the crash and came off the bench for Hull the following day in their 2-2 draw against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge.

Sports.title: Manchester City should face criminal probe over estimated £12m in unpaid tax, experts claim
Sports.content:
Manchester City should face a criminal investigation into an estimated £12 million of unpaid taxes, according to a report.

The report by Tax Policy Associates (TPA) finds Abu Dhabi-owned City could end up facing a bill of up to £24million to settle the amount, once interest and penalties are added.

Its conclusions, centring on the payment of former manager Roberto Mancini, add to the club’s woes after it was found guilty by an independent commission of financial cheating in a major scandal that has rocked the Premier League.

TPA founder Dan Neidle said: ‘We've examined the decision and leaked Mancini documents. We think City likely failed to pay £12 million in tax. There should be a criminal investigation.’

The TPA's report looks at findings by the commission that a key individual – identified via separate leaked documents as then-manager Roberto Mancini – was paid through a ‘sham’ consultancy.

In reality, the contract represented Mr Mancini’s employment by City and the club ‘should therefore have applied UK PAYE income tax in the usual way’, the report said.

The report centres on payments to then-manager Roberto Mancini

But the evidence suggests the club ‘unlawfully failed to do so’, it added.

It was not known whether HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) has launched an investigation or whether one has been resolved – but there has been no sign of any settlement payments in Manchester City’s accounts, the report said.

TPA continued: ‘The highly irregular nature of the arrangement, and the commission’s findings of sham and intentional concealment, suggest to us that there should be a criminal investigation into whether tax evasion offences were committed.’

The report added that the commission’s findings about City filing false accounts also suggested that ‘criminal offences may have been committed’.

At the heart of the report's claims are payments of £1.75 million a year to Mr Mancini said to cover coaching services in Abu Dhabi. That was on top of a £1.45 million a season salary to manage Manchester City.

The report said: ‘Mr Mancini was, we assume, fully taxed on his income under his main contract with Manchester City.

‘The club will have applied PAYE to deduct income tax and employee National Insurance from his wages, and paid employer National Insurance on his gross wages.

‘The position for Mr Mancini’s consultancy agreement should have been the same.

‘You can’t magically make a salary untaxed by calling it a consultancy fee. If the payments were really for Mr Mancini’s work at Manchester City, they were employment earnings and should have been taxed accordingly.’

The report adds: ‘We are not suggesting that any specific individuals at Manchester City, or indeed Mr Mancini, committed an offence. We do not know.’

HMRC declined to comment.

Manchester City had yet to respond to a request for comment at the time of publication.

Sports.title: England call up Mason Crane almost NINE YEARS after he picked up his last cap - following leg-spinner's reinvention as a star batter in domestic cricket
Sports.content:
Leg-spinner Mason Crane has been called up for England’s one-day tri-series in Pakistan later this month – nearly nine years after he last played international cricket.

Crane, who won his lone Test cap at Sydney in January 2018 a few months after playing his only two T20 internationals, has returned to England’s radar this summer, taking 15 wickets at an average of 20 for Glamorgan in the T20 Blast, and 34 at 35 in division one of the championship. Not yet 30, his batting has also gone to a new level, with the first two hundreds of his career, plus a 99.

‘Mason Crane has been performing consistently for Glamorgan across both formats during the summer,’ said national selector Marcus North. ‘He’s an experienced, high-class leg-spinner who thoroughly deserves another opportunity at international level.’

Also included in England’s 16-man squad for the series in Rawalpindi and Lahore, which starts on October 18 and also involves Sri Lanka, are the uncapped Sussex duo of spin-bowling all-rounder James Coles and seamer Henry Crocombe, who has spent the summer on the fringes of the international set-up.

Mason Crane has excelled with the bat this season, having made his name as a spinner

ENGLAND'S 16-MAN SQUAD AND FIXTURES

Harry Brook (capt), Gus Atkinson, Sonny Baker, Tom Banton, James Coles, Jordan Cox, Mason Crane, Henry Crocombe, Sam Curran, Liam Dawson, Ben Duckett, Will Jacks, Jamie Overton, Adil Rashid, Joe Root, Josh Tongue. Oct 18: Pakistan v Sri Lanka, Rawalpindi Oct 20: Pakistan v ENGLAND, Rawalpindi Oct 22: Sri Lanka v ENGLAND, Rawalpindi Oct 25: Pakistan v ENGLAND, Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore Oct 27: Pakistan v Sri Lanka, Lahore Oct 29: Sri Lanka v ENGLAND, Lahore Oct 31: Tri-series final, Lahore

Adil Rashid returns from the hand injury that ruled him out of the recent ODI series against Sri Lanka, and Sam Curran from the groin problem that cut short his summer. Jofra Archer will be rested, while Jos Buttler misses out after injuring a hamstring last week.

Hampshire fast bowler Sonny Baker, who bowled impressively against Sri Lanka, is also in the squad, and hoping to hone his reverse-swinging skills on the dry pitches of Pakistan.

‘I’m trying to break things down into segments,’ he said after being named as the young player of the year at the annual Professional Cricketers’ Association awards. ‘So for Pakistan it would be reverse-swing, and trying to bang my yorkers and learn about executing skills in those conditions.

‘It’s not somewhere I’ve been before, but I’m sure that’ll be a very transferable skill to playing in other areas of Asia. I’m really looking forward to it.’

England will play two games each against Pakistan and Sri Lanka, with the final taking place at Lahore on October 31.

Sports.title: Andy Burnham slammed for 'tone deaf' Man City statement after Prime Minister shared 'concern' at losing Abu Dhabi owners who have 'been a huge partner in building modern Manchester'
Sports.content:
Andy Burnham slammed for 'tone deaf' Man City statement after Prime Minister shared 'concern' at losing Abu Dhabi owners who have 'been a huge partner in building modern Manchester'

Andy Burnham's claim that he would be 'really concerned' if Manchester City's owners were to sell the club after it was found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations has been hit by widespread criticism.

The Prime Minister made the comments following confirmation from the league that Man City had been found to have created a slew of 'sham' deals and contracts which misled the Premier League over £900million-plus in sponsorship deals over a nine-year period.

The Premier League's chief executive Richard Masters stated that the club had 'systematically broken' the rules for nearly a decade and called the decision by the Independent Commission who heard the case 'the most significant in Premier League history'.

Since confirmation of the decision broke on Tuesday evening, there have been calls for Man City to face relegation, fines, and even expulsion from the top flight, as well as arguments that the Abu Dhabi ownership group should move on - but former mayor of Manchester Burnham took a more hesitant tone and lingered on the investment they had made into both the club and the city.

Those on social media were quick to suggest that his comments could likely interfere with the process of both Man City's appeal and potential future sanctions if the charges are upheld.

Stan Collymore suggested that Burnham's 'concern' was 'tone deaf', highlighting the 'clunky' comments as an example of the power of sports-washing.

Andy Burnham (with Man City chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak in 2019) has been criticised for comments made on his 'concern' that the club's ownership might sell

'For a PM, the day after a judgement by a respected panel to say 'we can't afford to lose City Group, they've put a lot into Manchester' is missing the point so widely that he's now going to be tagged as taking a side or grossly naïve,' he wrote in a lengthy post on X. 'Neither things people will readily vote for.'

Rio Ferdinand added that he thought Burnham was 'on the back foot referencing Manchester City', but other commenters on the site were more critical.

'This is political interference,' one wrote. 'Already stating that he sees them as a positive influence and not wanting them gone. Unacceptable interference by influencing the (government's Football) Regulator.'

Another added: 'Absolutely disgusting statement from the PM. He's basically saying you can cheat the system all you want if you pay enough. Just shows what sort of morals he really has'.

Green Party deputy leader Mothin Ali also weighed in, saying: 'Andy Burnham's comments are staggering, just one day after saying people should come before profit, he sides with big money over the integrity of a sport that belongs to the people.

'It's a shame the prime minister appears to agree there should be one rule for the rich and one for everyone else.'

Conservative MP Louie French, who serves as Shadow Minister for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport warned: 'Burnham’s clumsy comments haven’t just undermined the ongoing legal process and Premier League. He’s left the IFR Chief, who is a Labour donor and will determine the fit and proper owner test, exposed to future legal challenges, as we warned would happen.'

Burnham's comments did attract praise from one corner of social media, with Man City supporter and Oasis frontman Liam Gallagher writing: 'There's only 1 ANDY BURNHAM'.

Burnham, whose mayoral tenure in Greater Manchester began three years after the 2014 deal struck between Manchester Council and the Abu Dhabi United Group worth £1billion promising a regeneration of city centre districts New Islington and Ancoats, had stressed in his remarks that he was unable to 'intervene' in the ongoing case.

Speaking at the home of his side Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, he said: 'I would be really concerned to lose (Man City's Abu Dhabi owners).

'They've been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester and obviously the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is.

'I can't intervene more in the process. It would be wrong for me to do that. It would be wrong, I think, to jump to a conclusion before having really studied all of the detail, but obviously it's ongoing, and because it's still contested by Manchester City, then I think it's right that I don't say much more.'

'I do actually thank the City Football Group and the wider ownership for the money that they didn't just put into the Etihad (Stadium) and the campus around it but also into the city'.

In 2023 when charges were first brought against Man City, Abu Dhabi warned the United Kingdom that a negative outcome might damage relations with the country.

Man City have until October 2 to appeal the verdict, and Evertonian Burnham added that he did not want to assume guilt, as some had done in the wake of the Toffees' own sanctions in 2023.

Burnham was speaking one day on from his appearance at the Labour Party Conference

'Everton was in this position a few years ago and you might remember that I fought for Everton in that situation because I still hold the view very firmly that they weren't fairly treated in that process,' he continued.

'I remember people proclaiming Everton guilty at the time and with hindsight I think more people would say that wasn't fair, the way that was handled.

'So it would be wrong of me to leap to one side given the experience that I'd had before becoming prime minister.'

Everton had fallen foul of the Premier League's financial regulations and were charged and deducted 10 points, later reduced to six on appeal. But this was the scenario Man City seem to have been looking to avoid during the 2009-18 period scrutinised by the Independent Commission.

David Kogan, chairman of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR), stated that he had the powers to 'assess the suitability of owners, directors and executive' and that the body would look to use their powers to protect 'the sustainability, honesty and integrity of English football.'

The IFR and the FA will assess the findings once the sanctioning and appeals process has been completed.

Man City continues to deny any wrongdoing, with chief executive Ferran Soriano stating in a video shared with the club's staff that they were in possession of 'irrefutable evidence' of their innocence that could dispel the Premier League's 'conspiracy theory' on appeal.

Sports.title: England World Cup star Ivan Toney pleads NOT guilty to assault as court hears footballer allegedly 'headbutted and punched' reveller at upmarket London nightclub
Sports.content:
England striker Ivan Toney has denied assaulting a man at a Soho nightclub as he appeared in court to face the charge for the first time.

The 30-year-old footballer, from Northampton, is accused of attacking Saber Da Silva at a nightclub in Wardour Street, central London, on December 6.

Toney stood in the dock at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Thursday morning to confirm his name and age, and pleaded not guilty to a charge of assault occasioning actual bodily harm.

The court was told that during the 'confrontation' that took place at the end of last year, Toney and Da Silva had 'squared up to each other' before the England star was alleged to have 'lunged forward and headbutted the complainant, followed by a few punches.'

Toney, wearing a black top over a shirt and tie, was accompanied by three members of his entourage as he arrived at court shortly after 9.30am.

He was freed on unconditional bail by District Judge Briony Clark ahead of his next hearing at Southwark Crown Court on October 29.

Ivan Toney arrived at court on Thursday to face allegations that he assaulted a man at a London nightclub last year

The England striker is alleged to have attacked Saber Da Silva at a venue in the capital's Soho

The criminal case came after a Metropolitan Police investigation and the charge was announced in late July.

In a statement, his spokesperson said: 'Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court.'

The fracas is alleged by witnesses to have occurred on the heels of a fan asking for a selfie on the evening in question with the former Brentford star.

Following the 'confrontation', police seized Toney at the venue and after three people were assessed by the London Ambulance Service in situ, one was later taken to hospital.

Toney represented England at this summer's World Cup and has 10 international appearances and one goal.

He missed out on the latest squad for the country's Nations League ties.

Toney started his football career with Northampton Town and played for teams including Wigan Athletic and Peterborough United before signing for Brentford in 2020.

He scored 72 goals during four years with the Bees before making a surprise switch in 2024 to Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli.

Sports.title: Finally, Portugal have found the guts to stand up to Cristiano Ronaldo, writes OLIVER HOLT - he is a faded star living on past glories and only playing for himself
Sports.content:
Finally, Portugal have found the guts to stand up to Cristiano Ronaldo, writes OLIVER HOLT - he is a faded star living on past glories and only playing for himself

Lionel Messi will make his final appearance for Argentina in Buenos Aires next week. The match, a friendly against Benin, has been dubbed ‘The Last Tango’. It has been scripted for him. It is an opportunity for a nation to pay homage to one of the greatest players who has ever lived.

Whether Cristiano Ronaldo is ever afforded the same kind of farewell from the international game he has graced for 23 years remains to be seen. If Messi seems at peace with his decision and aware of the limitations age has foisted upon him, Ronaldo is raging and raging against the dying of the light.

It was hard not to feel sad at the sight of Ronaldo, who is 41 and had started the country’s previous game against Wales, walking out of the Portugal camp after manager Jorge Jesus chose not to bring him off the bench in the team’s Nations League victory over Norway in Oslo on Sunday. It was the first time in 18 years that Ronaldo had been an unused substitute for his country.

Ronaldo subsequently missed training on Tuesday before having dinner with Jesus to try to resolve their differences. He has played 234 times for Portugal, scoring 146 goals. Flouncing out of the squad in this way, at this stage of his international career, suggests that this may be the end.

The truth is that it is the strength of leadership Portugal has been crying out for. Many believe that Ronaldo has not deserved a place in the starting eleven of the national team for at least five years. He has become an example of a faded star living on his image and the memory of past glories.

It feels as if he is playing now only for himself. He has scored 979 career goals and he wants to be the first officially to reach 1000. Pele, Romario and others claimed to have reached the same landmark but their totals relied heavily on unofficial appearances in matches that included exhibitions.

Cristiano Ronaldo walked out of the Portugal camp after manager Jorge Jesus chose not to bring him off the bench in the team’s Nations League against Norway

Ronaldo subsequently missed training on Tuesday before having dinner with Jesus to try to resolve their differences, but subsequently appears to have ended his international career

It is unclear as to whether Ronaldo will be afforded the farewell Argentina are preparing to give Lionel Messi, who will make a final appearance for his nation in a friendly next week

Ronaldo has become the epitome of a sportsman who cannot let go and is damaging his legacy by refusing to leave the arena

It is beginning to look as if Ronaldo may have to get those goals playing for Al Nassr in the Saudi Pro League, which has propped up his ego since he joined the club in December 2022. He had left Manchester United shortly before that, claiming he had been betrayed by the club with whom he had made his name in his first spell in English football.

The previous Portugal manager Roberto Martinez did not have the courage or the stomach for the fight. He was in thrall to Ronaldo’s power and persisted with him both at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar and, again, in the USA, Mexico and Canada in the summer that has just passed.

Portugal had a lavishly talented squad at both tournaments but both times, the selection of Ronaldo proved highly controversial and divisive. He was a player playing on his reputation. At both tournaments, Portugal were undermined. In the USA, they were among the favourites to win. After an unconvincing start, they were knocked out by Spain in the Round of 16.

Ronaldo said then that he was considering retirement from the international game but he decided to play on. He was a magnificent player in his prime, second only to Messi in his generation of superstars, but he has been a shadow of that player for a long time and now it appears even his past reputation cannot save him.

He has become the epitome of a sportsman who cannot let go and is damaging his legacy by refusing to leave the arena. Watching him play now is like watching a fighter who has taken too many blows. Those who have his best interests at heart want him to call an end to it all but Ronaldo cannot do it.

He has been an exemplary professional his whole career, a man who has dedicated himself to the game he has graced, and now he cannot let go. He is addicted to the game and to the spotlight and he cannot handle it when a manager says ‘no’. No sooner did Jesus do that than Ronaldo left the camp.

This moment had been coming. Many were astonished that former PSG forward Goncalo Ramos, who now plays for AC Milan, was not the first choice forward for Portugal at this year’s World Cup but Jesus started him against Norway and Ramos rewarded that decision by scoring the winner.

Jesus had let it be known that Ramos, not Ronaldo, would also start tonight’s Nations League tie against Denmark in Copenhagen. That appeared to be too much for Ronaldo. Time catches up with everyone, however great they are. Messi admitted it had caught up with him in the World Cup final. It is to be hoped that, from somewhere, Ronaldo can find the same acceptance before he tarnishes his legacy further.

Sports.title: Gary Neville says Man City verdict has 'dragged Premier League through the MUD' and warns England's top flight could suffer same fate as Italy's Serie A
Sports.content:
The Premier League is being 'dragged through the mud', with Man City's guilty verdict damaging the top flight's image around the world, says Gary Neville. This week's bombshell verdict finding City guilty on almost all charges, benefiting from £900million sham deals and revealing the extraordinary scale of their cheating has sent shockwaves through the sport and wider society. Neville thinks the reputational damage to what he calls the 'country's biggest export' could be long-lasting. He fears a similar decline experienced by Serie A in the wake of the Calciopoli scandal – the 2006 saga exposing how Italian clubs influenced referees, leading to Juventus being stripped of titles and relegated to Serie B. Speaking on the latest Stick to Football podcast, he reflected: 'I'm chilled, this is chilling not celebratory. I support Manchester United, you support Liverpool, you were Arsenal. It is chilling to listen to this. 'The Italian game has suffered immeasurably in the last 25 years. We played against Juventus, we've alluded to this before, we felt at the time this wasn't right and the Italian... I'm not saying that's going to happen to the Premier League but we always think that we've got an enormous integrity the Premier League, that we are the sort of league that sets the standard and it's other leagues that have got corruption, fraud, doping scandals, match fixing, referee scandals. Gary Neville fears long-term damage to the Premier League after Man City's guilty verdict 'This is now coming to our country, this is now coming to our league. This is the greatest export that we have in our country in the world,' he went on. Neville added: 'If you go around the world and talk about Liverpool, Manchester United, Arsenal, you talk about the Premier League. 'People talk about the Premier League more than anything when you tell them where you're from. At the moment, we're being dragged through the mud.' Despite the mountain of evidence against them and comprehensive verdict from an independent commission, City remain intent on appealing. With that process and the highly-anticipated sanctions still to come, the scandal shows no sign of ending any time soon and threatens to overshadow this season, in addition to the last decade. That could further plunge the Premier League into the mire reputationally around the world as the fallout continues. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has been criticised for his 'tone deaf' statement on City's guilt, in which he shared his concern about the prospect of losing City's Abu Dhabi owners. Speaking at the home of his side Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, he said: 'I would be really concerned to lose (Man City's Abu Dhabi owners).

Your browser does not support iframes.

'They've been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester and obviously the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is. 'I can't intervene more in the process. It would be wrong for me to do that. It would be wrong, I think, to jump to a conclusion before having really studied all of the detail, but obviously it's ongoing, and because it's still contested by Manchester City, then I think it's right that I don't say much more.' Stan Collymore suggested that Burnham's 'concern' was 'tone deaf', highlighting the 'clunky' comments as an example of the power of sports-washing. Rio Ferdinand added that he thought Burnham was 'on the back foot referencing Manchester City', but other commenters on the site were more critical. 'This is political interference,' one wrote. 'Already stating that he sees them as a positive influence and not wanting them gone. Unacceptable interference by influencing the (government's Football) Regulator.' Another added: 'Absolutely disgusting statement from the PM. He's basically saying you can cheat the system all you want if you pay enough. Just shows what sort of morals he really has'. The row spilling over into the highest levels of politics shows the enormity of the biggest cheating scandal in British sporting history and would appear to validate Neville's fears about how the Premier League could now suffer as a result.

Sports.title: Courtney Meppen-Walter's family pay tribute to 'truly special soul' following footballer's death aged 32 - as fundraiser is launched to cover funeral costs
Sports.content:
The family of tragic footballer Courtney Meppen-Walter have paid tribute to a 'truly special soul' following his death aged 32.

Ex-England Under 18 captain Meppen-Walter's passing was announced by his current club, Bury, on Tuesday. No details have been announced regarding the circumstances of the defender's death.

The footballer, who was let go by Manchester City after he was jailed for 16 months for causing the death of two people by careless driving, had spells at Ashton United, Stockport County, Glossop North End, Chorley, AFC Telford United, Radcliffe, Guiseley, Nantwich Town, Bury and Stalybridge Celtic.

On Wednesday night, his family paid tribute to the 32-year-old - who had become a father for a third time in July - while launching a GoFundMe page to help cover the cost of his funeral.

'Courtney was an unforgettable Dad, partner, son, brother, friend, and an unforgettable player,' the statement read. 'He was someone who made an impression on everyone he met, and his absence will be felt by so many people who had the privilege of knowing and loving him.

'Courtney was a truly special soul. He was the kind of person who could bring light into every room he walked into. He brought laughter to every table, could turn an ordinary moment into a memory, and had the incredible ability to make friends with a chair. That was just Courtney — his personality, his humour, and the way he made people feel comfortable around him were something that cannot be replaced.

'He had a way of making people smile, even when they were having a difficult day. Whether you knew him as family, a friend, a teammate, or simply someone you crossed paths with, there is no doubt that Courtney left his mark.'

A candle light vigil was held for Meppen-Walter on Tuesday night, with family and friends releasing balloons and fireworks in honour of the 32-year-old.

Courtney Meppen-Walter's family have paid tribute to a 'truly special soul' after his death. Pictured left

Ex-England youth star Meppen-Walter has passed away at the age of 32

Meppen-Walter had been part of Manchester City's youth set-up and captained England's Under-18 side. He was released by Man City in 2013 after he was jailed for 16 months for causing the death of two people by careless driving.

Kulwant Singh, 32, and his sister Ravel Kaur, 37, were both pronounced dead at the scene following a high-speed crash in Manchester.

Meppen-Walter was released after serving half of that sentence.

The defender joined Carlisle United following his release from prison and spent two seasons at the Cumbrian side.

Meppen-Walter was released by Bury in the summer of 2025 after a loan spell at Stalybridge Celtic.

In 2019, when Meppen-Walter was playing for Chorley, he was banned from being behind the wheel for 22 months after he was caught drink-driving.

Meppen-Walter had been found to have been more than twice the legal limit when he was stopped in his vehicle by police in Manchester city centre.

The footballer had been arrested and taken to a police station where he gave a positive reading of 85 microgrammes of alcohol in 100 millilitres of breath – the legal limit being 35mcg.

Meppen-Walter became a father for the third time in July. Pictured in 2010

Meppen-Walter was jailed in 2013 for causing the death of two people by dangerous driving

Brother and sister Kulwant Singh and Ravel-Kaur died following the high-speed crash in Manchester

Meppen-Walter was also ordered to serve a 12-month community order, as well as completing 80 hours of unpaid work.

'I know what you are probably thinking and what everyone else is thinking,’ Meppen-Walter said in court.

‘I will probably get called every name under the sun and I deserve it. I'm just embarrassed.'

The court had heard that alcohol played no part in the deaths of Mr Singh and Ms Kaur who had come to the UK from Afghanistan in 2001 to start a new life after fleeing persecution by the Taliban.

A pre-sentence probation report noted his drink-driving reflected 'poor judgment' when considering his previous conviction and that 'again he has failed to consider the consequences of his actions'.

Caitriona McLaughlin, defending, said: 'The most significant mitigation in this case is his genuine remorse which has been reflected throughout. He is truly sorry for his actions.

'It was a mistake and it is the one and only drink mistake on his record.'

Chairwoman of the bench Margaret Hutchinson said: 'We hope this will be a lesson to you and we will not see you in court again.

'Drink-driving is a very serious matter and the consequences could have been much graver than today.'

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
