Sports.title: “Bring snow chains and hand warmers” if Formula 1 moves final race to Imola | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 drivers expect unusually cold conditions if the series moves its final round to Imola in Italy.

The championship is weighing whether its final two events in the Middle East can take place as the war between Iran and the USA continues.

Formula 1 cancelled its two April rounds in the Middle East, which were due to take place in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia. The former event is taking place this weekend but has been relocated 6,000 kilometres away to Sepang in Malaysia.

If F1 does abandon its plans to race in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, the series is expected to arrange a single replacement round at Imola. The series previously raced at the track in November six years ago, but a potential December finale could be held in very cool conditions.

“I think we should bring the snow chains and the hand warmers,” said Haas’s Oliver Bearman. “Let’s see how it goes, but it will definitely be cold if we’re in Imola in December. I was living close by for a good few years and in winter it’s definitely cold. You know about it.”

Some teams have already tested at the circuit this year, including Racing Bulls, which is based nearby. “It’ll be a bit colder than Abu Dhabi,” said the team’s driver Arvid Lindblad.

“In the end we’ll do whatever F1 thinks is best. I know they’re managing it. I don’t know all the ins and outs of what’s happening, but I’ve heard that Imola is the back-up.

“It will get a bit darker a bit earlier, but I think there’s still enough hours for us to drive fine, so I don’t think that would be an issue. It’ll just be a bit cold, maybe wet.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

F1 has already raced in Italy once this year. The country has recently changed its tax arrangements for elite athletes, but Max Verstappen does not expect this or the weather will cause a problem for drivers.

“There are worse places to be in the wintertime than in Imola,” he said. “Yes, it’s a little bit colder than in the summer, it gets darker a bit sooner, but I think we’re all clever enough to make sure that we don’t drive in the dark.

“And there is no tax issue. You just have to pay tax.”

F1 held the Emilia-Romagna Grand Prix at Imola between 2020 and 2025, except in 2023 when flooding forced its cancellation.

Sports.title: Inconsistent Haas performance has affected both drivers, Bearman admits | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Haas driver Oliver Bearman confirmed the problems with inconsistency his team mate referred to have compromised both drivers this year.

The team announced yesterday Esteban Ocon will not remain alongside Bearman next year. Ocon, who has scored fewer points than Bearman so far this year, said his performances were compromised by inconsistencies in their car’s performance at times.

“When the car is working, it helps [you] to get something better,” he said. “When the inconsistencies of the cars are here, where you struggle more, you don’t look as good.”

Bearman admitted the team has suffered from the problem for much of the season. “It’s an issue that we’ve been struggling with, to be honest, all throughout the year and not really understanding why,” he said.

“From one weekend to the next, even one day to the next [and] not changing parts, we can have differences in car performance compared to the other car but also compared to your own car. So it’s really tough, hard to understand why, which is of course why it’s still happening.”

He said the situation began to improve at the Italian Grand Prix. “To be honest, I think the last few events since we bought this latest upgrade in Monza, everything has seemed to calm down a little bit.”

Bearman, who finished ninth behind Ocon at the last round in Baku, said the problem was “a reason for underperformance as a team and across cars.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“It’s challenging because you go into the weekend and from the first lap of FP1 you know if it’s going to be a good one or not because you can feel if the car is feeling nice and if it is feeling good then you can perform well,” he explained.

“I had a situation in Baku in FP1, everything felt really poor and I was strapping in for a long weekend, but actually we changed a few parts and everything was performing well and I had a good weekend after that.

“So it’s something that has challenged both of us to an extent and something that as a team we need to improve on because it makes our life challenging because we’re not really sure what we’re working with heading into a weekend. Even heading into FP3, for example, after a decent Friday, sometimes that can fall apart, so it’s challenging.”

In his first full season in F1 last year, Bearman out-scored Ocon by 41 points to 38. Haas has not yet announced who Ocon’s replacement will be but Bearman indicated he expects to be the senior driver in the team next year.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Bearman said Ocon “has been a great team mate and it’s a shame to see him going.”

“I’ve learnt a lot from him over the year-and-a-half we’ve been together,” he added. “Of course he’s a very quick driver but also the way that he works with the team has been quite interesting for me to see.

“Coming in as an F2 driver, where you’re almost a client of the team and you get told what to do, you step up to F1 and now the team looks to you for inspiration, for motivation, for a direction in terms of development and things like that, which is the first time I’ve been in that situation. So in that sense I learnt a lot from Esteban, that’s been really useful for me.

“There’s no doubt about his speed, he’s shown that on many occasions. So it’s a shame to see but I’m looking forward to coming into a new role within the team as the leader, being the most experienced driver within the team potentially, so in that sense I think it’s a good opportunity for me to continue to learn.”

The 21-year-old, who made his F1 debut at Ferrari as a substitute for Carlos Sainz Jnr in 2024, says he feels ready to step up and become a team leader.

“I think that I’ve come a long way in those two years. My first few races were very, very unique circumstances. But even if I compare to the level that I was performing at last year, I’ve definitely come a long way, especially with how I interact with the team off-track and what I understand about how to get the most out of the guys and developing the car as well. So in that sense, I’m looking forward to this new role.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Aston Martin driver Lance Stroll sympathised with Ocon, whom he replaced at his current team in 2019. “Formula 1’s not always fair and sometimes you’re in situations where it’s just shit and that’s kind of, I think, the situation he’s in,” he said.

“I think he’s demonstrated over the years that he’s been great in Formula 1 and he’s had a lot of good results. So it definitely sucks for him.

“All I can say is I really hope he bounces back and he finds himself in a good situation in the near future. If that’s here, if that’s somewhere else, whatever, I just only wish him the best.

“He’s a great driver and, he’s demonstrated that not just in Formula 1 but all of his junior years. I was racing in Prema in a similar time to him in our junior career, and I was in F4 and he was in F3, and he was winning all those races and stuff. Even when we were in karting together, he was always really quick. So I only wish him the best.”

Sports.title: Verstappen eager to avoid his first win-less season since F1 debut | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen believes he is getting closer to his first victory of 2026 as he nears the end of what could be his first win-less season in 10 years.

He has never failed to win at least one grand prix per season since Red Bull promoted him to their top Formula 1 team during 2016, his second year in the championship. However with eight rounds of the 2026 campaign remaining – and serious doubt over whether the final two will go ahead – Verstappen is yet to take a win.

“I’m trying everything I can,” he said. “We are scoring quite a few podiums now, but I want to win. That’s what I’m here for.

“I’m getting close, but I want at least to win one race this year. I hope we can do it at some point.”

Red Bull’s performance has improved since the start of the season. Verstappen reached the podium just twice in the first nine rounds but has reached the rostrum in five of the last six.

He and team mate Isack Hadjar both reached the podium at the last round in Baku, Red Bull’s best performance of the season so far. However Verstappen believes the RB22 was flattered by that particular circuit.

“We have some solid results. I think also the parts that we [put] on the car in Baku, they worked well.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“But we also know that Baku always has been quite a good track to us. It’s quite unique with the 90-degree corners, you don’t really have a lot of high-speed corners.”

Red Bull’s performance over the remaining races could have a significant bearing on the decisions they make on their new car for next year,” Verstappen added.

“We have to wait a little bit now in the coming races [to see] how our car is going to perform, which is also quite good for us probably to see all these different kinds of tracks. Because for next year we’ll probably learn a lot now over these coming races [about] what we need, what we want to do with the car.

“We’re anyway not fighting for the championship, so for us it’s a big learning curve, but of course the last few weekends have been a lot better at the start of the season.”

Sports.title: Ukraine club urges FIA General Assembly discussion of Russia’s alleged violations | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The Federation Automobile d’Ukraine (Ukraine Automobile Club) is calling for the FIA General Assembly to discuss alleged violations of the governing body’s statutes by Russia.

The Ukraine club claims the FIA has failed to respond to its previous enquiries on the matter. It claims the Russian Automobile Federation is operating offices in Ukrainian territory which Russia annexed following its invasion of the country.

“We are surprised by the position of the authorised bodies of the FIA, which are trying to hush up this situation,” said FAU president Oleksandr Feldman.

“For example, our appeal of 26th August to the FIA Ethics Committee, requesting urgent consideration of the violator’s actions, not only provoked no reaction but was left entirely unanswered.

“It is precisely because of the inaction of the FIA bodies that we propose to bring this issue before the General Assembly.”

The FAU claims the RAF’s conduct breaches article 3.3 of the FIA Statutes, which requires member clubs’ activities be confined to “the whole of the national territory.”

They also claim a breach of article 1.4.1 of the International Sporting Code, which states: “One ASN [Autorite Sportive Nationale – national motorsport club] shall be recognised by the FIA as sole international sporting power for the enforcement of the Code and control of motor sport throughout the territories placed under the authority of its own country.”

Russia began its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Formula 1 and the FIA responded by cancelling the Russian Grand Prix in Sochi. The FIA also prevented Russian competitors from taking part in its competitions under the Russian flag, but abandoned this restriction in August.

Sports.title: A new track for half the field: Six ‘Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia’ talking points | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 will race at the Sepang International Circuit for the first time in eight years this weekend. Here’s what to watch for at the awkwardly-named ‘Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia’.

Return of a modern classic

The Sepang International Circuit was one of the first examples of Formula 1’s international expansion into explored territories far beyond its traditional European heartland. Though it had gone to existing circuits in Asia and elsewhere before, Sepang proved a template which other countries later followed.

Some like South Korea and India did not endure as long as Malaysia. Others, like China and Bahrain, out-lasted it: Sepang held its last grand prix in 2017.

F1 arguably lost one of its better modern tracks when it left. Sepang features some impressively quick corners and astonishingly wide straights. The climate often created drama, too, as rain showed can be sudden, unexpected and intense.

A new(ish) challenge

Exactly half the grid has no prior F1 experience at this track. Only three teams have drivers who have both driven it in F1 before: Cadillac, Aston Martin and Ferrari. For the latter, Charles Leclerc has never raced at this circuit, but participated in first practice for Sauber at the 2017 event.

Three teams have pairings with no prior F1 experience at this track: Mercedes, McLaren and Racing Bulls. This will also be the first visits to Sepang for Isack Hadjar, Franco Colapinto, Oliver Bearman, Alexander Albon and Gabriel Bortoleto.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Mercedes’ killer blow?

Mercedes’ early dominance was followed by a mid-season run during which they won just two out of six rounds. However they have rebounded since then, winning all of the last three races, without putting any significant updates on their W17.

It is therefore ominous for the opposition that the team is bringing new parts for their car this weekend. Will Mercedes be untouchable this weekend?

One factor may work against them: George Russell is expected to need a new power unit soon and will have to take a penalty when he does. He took a useful bite of out his team mate’s championship lead in Azerbaijan, but he’ll be badly hamstrung if he has to start near the back in Sepang.

Alonso’s faith in Aston Martin – and F1

Fernando Alonso made it clear he would only continue to race in Formula 1 if he was happy both with the car Aston Martin gave him and the state of the series’ regulations. The two-times world champion has been one of the most vehement critics of F1’s 2026 power unit rules.

So it won’t just be Aston Martin owner Lawrence Stroll who breathed a sigh of relief when Alonso committed to return in 2026 – FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem will too. But will he also be pushing to give more help to Aston Martin’s power unit supplier Honda too?

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Au revoir Ocon?

Esteban Ocon hinted in Azerbaijan his days at Haas are numbered. The team confirmed today he will not drive for them again next year. With just eight rounds to go, Ocon’s chances of finding a seat elsewhere for next year do not look good, however defiant he sounds about his F1 career not being at an end.

The situation has noticeable parallels with Ocon’s departure from Alpine two years ago. That too was announced long before the end of the season with no official word on the identity of Ocon’s replacement.

On that occasion Ocon wasn’t able to start his final race for the team as Alpine dropped him so suddenly he wasn’t able to use the special helmet he’d prepared. There’s no indication Haas may do the same, though it wouldn’t be a surprise if he isn’t the only driver who doesn’t get to race in Abu Dhabi this year…

Will there be a ‘Bahrain Grand Prix in Bahrain’?

F1’s return to Sepang has come about due to the volatility in the Middle East caused by the war between the US and Iran. The conflict appears far from over, yet F1 is dragging its feet in reaction.

F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali originally indicated a decision would be taken in mid-September. Now F1 appears to be hanging on as late as possible in the hope of minimising its financial losses.

In the meantime it has already announced the Bahrain Grand Prix will be held in the country to open the 2027 season. That’s just six months away, which is already beginning to look optimistic.

Sports.title: America’s 1976 Boxing Gold Leads To Unequal Rewards
Sports.content:
Howard Davis Jr. left the 1976 Montreal Olympics with lightweight gold and the Val Barker Trophy as the tournament’s outstanding boxer. Fifty years later, his professional career offers the most surprising outcome from that celebrated American team: all four of his fellow gold medalists won major world titles. Davis never did.

The United States collected five gold medals, one silver and one bronze in Montreal. The team eventually produced five professional world champions, including three heavyweight champions, but those achievements conceal very different careers. Some fighters built years of success. Others reached the top and lost their titles in their first defense.

Davis challenged Jim Watt and Edwin Rosario for the WBC lightweight title before facing Buddy McGirt for the IBF light welterweight belt. He lost all three attempts, finishing 36-6-1. His split-decision defeat against Rosario in 1984 was the closest he came to joining his Olympic teammates as a champion.

His career shows the limits of treating an Olympic medal as a forecast. Davis had proved himself against elite amateurs. Professional championship boxing required him to repeat that success over longer fights against established titleholders.

Sugar Ray Leonard made that transition spectacularly. The light welterweight gold medalist became a five-division champion, with victories over Wilfred Benitez, Roberto Duran, Thomas Hearns and Marvin Hagler. His detached retina interrupted his career and contributed to his first retirement in 1982; it should not be used as a blanket explanation for his defeats. Leonard’s professional reputation rests on whom he beat, well beyond what he achieved in Montreal.

Michael Spinks also built a career that surpassed his Olympic achievement. The middleweight gold medalist became the undisputed light heavyweight champion before moving up to defeat unbeaten Larry Holmes in 1985. He beat Holmes again in their rematch and retired at 31-1 after his sole defeat, against Mike Tyson in 1988. Reducing his career to that final knockout overlooks his championship work in two divisions.

His brother Leon reached heavyweight glory much faster. The Olympic light heavyweight champion defeated Muhammad Ali in his eighth professional fight in February 1978, winning both the WBA and WBC titles. He lost the Ali rematch and eventually finished 26-17-3. That final record reflects his struggles after becoming champion, but the victory over Ali remains an extraordinary achievement for such an inexperienced professional.

John Tate, Montreal’s heavyweight bronze medalist, became the team’s third heavyweight champion by outpointing Gerrie Coetzee for the vacant WBA title in South Africa in October 1979. His reign ended brutally: Mike Weaver knocked him out in the 15th round of his first defense while Tate led on all three scorecards. A subsequent knockout loss to Trevor Berbick helped derail a career that ended at 34-3.

Flyweight gold medalist Leo Randolph experienced an equally brief championship reign. He stopped Ricardo Cardona to win the WBA super bantamweight title in May 1980, then lost it to Sergio Victor Palma in August. Randolph retired after that defeat at 17-2. Olympic gold and a professional world title were substantial achievements, even without a lengthy career.

The remaining team members—Davey Lee Armstrong, Clint Jackson, Chuck Walker and Louis Curtis—turned professional without winning major world championships. Bantamweight silver medalist Charles Mooney chose a different route, remaining in the Army rather than entering the paid ranks.

Montreal produced an exceptional group, but its professional legacy deserves more than a medal count. Leonard and Michael Spinks sustained success against great opponents. Leon Spinks, Tate, and Randolph reached championship level without establishing long reigns. Davis, the tournament’s outstanding boxer, never secured the title his Olympic performance appeared to promise.

Fifty years later, those different outcomes make the team worth revisiting. The medals identified talent. The professional careers revealed how differently that talent could develop.

Sports.title: Three Failed WBO Purse Bids Point Toward Zuffa
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley’s reported move to Zuffa Boxing adds another abandoned fight to the WBO’s purse-bid record, following Hamzah Sheeraz’s title surrender and Keyshawn Davis’s withdrawal from a shot at Devin Haney.

Two champions have chosen to give up their belts, while a mandatory challenger rejected a payday exceeding $2 million. That suggests the issue extends beyond one poorly funded defense: the WBO’s process is producing terms fighters are willing to leave behind.

“Three consecutive purse bids, all end with no fight and the parties who walked away all headed in the same direction,” boxing reporter Jake Donovan wrote on X. “Couldn’t be a clearer path if it had a neon sign pointing that way.”

Bentley reportedly signed a multi-fight Zuffa deal and will appear against an opponent to be named on the November 7 Chris Billam-Smith–Chev Clarke card in London. Dan Rafael reports that Bentley will relinquish his WBO middleweight title rather than accept $160,000 to defend against Yoenli Hernandez.

Sheeraz previously surrendered his WBO super-middleweight championship after Queensberry won the September purse bid for his mandatory defense against Janibek Alimkhanuly.

Davis’s case involved considerably more money. Top Rank won the Haney fight with an $8.55 million bid, leaving Davis entitled to $2,137,500 under the WBO’s 75–25 split. He declined to proceed as the challenger.

For Zuffa, these departures offer a recruitment opportunity. Established fighters can arrive with name recognition built through championship boxing without bringing the same mandatory obligations into their next appearance.

The WBO can enforce its rules by removing a title or replacing a challenger. What it cannot guarantee is that either consequence will persuade a fighter to accept the resulting purse.

That leaves Hernandez and other contenders exposed. Earning mandatory status can secure an order, yet still fail to deliver the intended opponent.

Donovan sees the departures pointing toward Zuffa. Bentley’s reported signing gives that argument substance, although it does not establish that Zuffa coordinated all three withdrawals.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Credits Dana White For U.S. Return
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury credits Dana White with helping resolve the visa issue that kept him out of the United States for years, opening the door to his return to South Florida for training ahead of the Anthony Joshua fight.

White’s help puts Fury back in familiar surroundings with SugarHill Steward in Delray Beach and opens the door to more fights in the United States.

“Listen, it all got done through Dana on Donald Trump’s table,” Fury told Mike Coppinger of The Ring. “And Donald Trump just went bang: ‘Tyson’s a great guy. Come on in.’ And that’s how it works. That’s how G’s go, innit? They make [things] happen.”

That is Fury’s account of how the matter was handled, and his appreciation for White is clear. After a lengthy absence, returning to America means access to a familiar training environment and another major market for the closing stretch of his career.

Fury is already looking beyond Joshua to a third fight with Oleksandr Usyk, which he wants at Madison Square Garden next year. That bout remains unsigned, but his return to the United States makes an American venue possible again.

It is easy to see why Fury appreciates White’s help. Getting him back into America has allowed him to resume training in Florida and consider U.S. fights again, giving Fury a clear reason to value their relationship.

Fury also spoke warmly about his American audience, describing recognition from boxing followers and viewers of his Netflix series. Returning allows him to reconnect with both groups while preparing for another major event.

From Fury’s perspective, White has already helped improve his options. The Florida camp is the immediate benefit. The chance to finish his career with more American appearances could prove the bigger one.

Sports.title: Jake Paul Mocks Canelo Alvarez Over Halloween Fight
Sports.content:
Jake Paul has used Canelo Alvarez’s October 31 fight against Christian Mbilli to renew his claim that the Mexican star is afraid to face him. The Halloween joke gets Paul into the conversation, but it does little to strengthen his sporting case for the matchup.

Paul wants a reaction. An argument with Canelo would give him something to promote without having to earn the opportunity against ranked contenders.

“Canelo fighting on Halloween is perfect,” Paul wrote on X. “He’s been dressed up as a guy who’s scared of me for three years.”

There is commercial history behind the complaint. Canelo signed a four-fight Riyadh Season deal in February 2025, moving away from a proposed Paul matchup. Paul can resent losing that opportunity, but choosing another substantial agreement does not establish fear.

Canelo is now preparing to challenge Mbilli for the WBC super middleweight title in Riyadh. Paul is trying to turn that event into a discussion about himself.

Silence would be Canelo’s strongest dismissal. Leaving the jab unanswered treats Paul like a spectator shouting from the cheap seats. A rebuttal gives him another clip to circulate; ignoring him leaves Paul carrying the argument alone.

There is also Alalshikh’s role to consider. If Mbilli represents the third fight of the four-fight agreement, Paul would need the event backer to support using the remaining bout on him. That looks unlikely when an established contender or major rematch could offer greater sporting significance.

For fans who judge credibility through opposition, the costume joke changes nothing. Calling Canelo scared is easier than beating contenders who could establish a legitimate claim to the fight.

Paul’s commercial appeal is clear. His sporting case needs work. If he wants recognition as a serious prizefighter, climbing the rankings would do more for him than another social media lottery ticket.

Sports.title: Denzel Bentley Chooses Zuffa Over WBO Title Defense
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley is choosing a multi-fight deal with Zuffa Boxing over a $160,000 mandatory defense against Yoenli Hernandez, with the WBO middleweight champion reportedly preparing to vacate his title.

The move gives Zuffa another established British fighter while exposing how little financial protection a world championship can provide when a purse bid attracts minimal interest.

Dan Rafael reports that Bentley has signed with Zuffa and will face an opponent to be named in the November 7 London co-feature beneath Chris Billam-Smith against Chev Clarke. According to Rafael’s source, Bentley will reject the terms of this week’s purse bid and relinquish the belt.

Warriors Boxing won the Bentley-Hernandez bidding with the $200,000 minimum. Queensberry attended but did not submit a bid, leaving Hernandez’s promoter with control of the proposed defense.

That outcome gave Bentley little financial incentive to stay. A world title carries prestige, but risking it against a dangerous mandatory for $160,000 becomes a harder sell when another promoter offers a multi-fight commitment. Bentley’s Zuffa purse has not been disclosed, so the size of any immediate financial improvement remains unknown.

For Zuffa, the value extends beyond adding a name to November’s card. Bentley arrives with championship recognition and a clear reason for changing direction. His departure allows the promotion to argue that it offers established fighters an alternative when the traditional title system produces an unattractive payday.

There is a sporting cost. Hernandez earned the mandatory position and would lose the opportunity to challenge the reigning champion. Bentley would leave that obligation behind without settling the matchup in the ring.

Aaron McKenna remains a possible future opponent, but the terminology matters. The WBO previously required Bentley to face Hernandez before pursuing McKenna. If Bentley vacates, a meeting with the IBF champion would no longer unite their two belts.

Bentley’s November opponent will help show what this change delivers. The contract provides a new promotional future; the matchmaking must provide fights worth watching.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua Willing To Scrap Fury Fight Over Hearn Loyalty
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua is willing to help Eddie Hearn pull the plug on the Tyson Fury fight if a renewed dispute over Dana White’s involvement leads his promoter to withdraw. That puts a promotional disagreement ahead of an unconditional commitment to face Fury.

Joshua wants credit for helping bring the fight to Britain. Yet when asked whether White’s return could make him walk away, his answer centered on what Hearn wants.

“My loyalty is with Eddie,” Joshua told talkSPORT Boxing. “So, whatever he wants to do, if he wants to pull the plug, I’ll be right there tugging that plug with him.”

That gives Hearn considerable leverage. He can oppose White knowing his headline fighter has publicly offered to support withdrawal. A commercial dispute becomes much harder to resolve when one promoter has the backing to take away half the main event.

Joshua’s loyalty is understandable. He credits Hearn with securing the British venue and values their long relationship. But supporting a promoter does not require handing him the decision over whether to fight your biggest domestic rival.

For the public, the distinction is simple. They are being sold Joshua against Fury. Asking them to accept cancellation over a disagreement about White’s role would require a much stronger explanation than loyalty to Eddie.

Joshua’s answer also creates a potential escape route. Any future withdrawal could be presented as standing beside Hearn, shifting attention from the fighter’s decision to the promoter’s objections. That does not establish that Joshua wants an excuse to avoid Fury. It does mean he has publicly supplied a business reason for walking away.

If White returns, Joshua would face an uncomfortable choice: support Hearn’s withdrawal or explain why his position has changed.

Hearn gains bargaining power from this declaration. Joshua takes on the reputational risk. Fans are left hoping the men arranging the fight can settle their differences before those differences cost them the fight itself.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury’s Extra Rounds Fail to Hide Decline
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury credits his fights against Arslanbek Makhmudov and Mariusz Wach with preparing him for Anthony Joshua. Those rounds gave him time in the ring, but they offered little evidence that his movement, speed, and punching authority had returned.

Fury looked slow and heavy in both outings. This physical decay traces directly to his second beating from Oleksandr Usyk, completely destroying the comeback rust excuse.

“Of course, 16 months out of the ring. It wasn’t to have one round,” Fury told The Ring. “I needed rounds. The same with the other fellow, Wach Mariusz. I needed rounds. I actually have the perfect grounding for this fight. I fought one 6’7″ guy in Wach and one 6’8′ guy in Makhmudov. So they’re perfect for Joshua.”

The height comparison is a thin argument. Tall opponents provide practice managing reach, but their dimensions do not reproduce Joshua’s timing, combinations or speed when he closes the distance.

Wach was 46. Getting seven rounds against him supplied work, but offered limited evidence that Fury could still control a dangerous heavyweight with his feet. His 12 rounds against Makhmudov answered the endurance question more clearly than the movement question.

The version of Fury who beat 39-year-old Wladimir Klitschko in 2015 was nowhere to be seen. That Fury used feints, changes of rhythm and quick repositioning to leave Klitschko reluctant to throw. Recent performances have shown far less of that elusive fighter.

Fury can still draw on his experience, size and awkwardness. However, when his feet slow, he spends longer within punching range. Without enough authority behind his own shots, discouraging Joshua from advancing becomes harder. Fury also claims Joshua’s team wanted him inactive. That accusation does nothing to settle the question raised by his performances.

Needing rounds is understandable. Calling them “perfect grounding” asks the public to accept that ring time has restored tools Fury has yet to show.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Promises Knockout Against Anthony Joshua
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury promises to meet Anthony Joshua head-on, telling today’s press conference that he intends to trade punches and finish the fight rather than keep his distance.

That gives Joshua something to test when they enter the ring. Fury can talk about a knockout now, but committing to exchanges would also give Joshua opportunities to land his own heavy shots.

“I ain’t gonna run away, I’m gonna throw down,” Tyson Fury said in a clip from today’s kickoff press conference . “I’m gonna catch him, and when I do it’s gonna be curtains.”

The important part is Fury’s promise to engage. Catching Joshua requires creating an opening, and coming forward does not automatically make that easier. Joshua would have less ground to cover if Fury stayed within punching range.

Fury could use his jab and feints to draw a reaction before attacking. That would fit a knockout plan without requiring him to stand and trade throughout. His press conference language leaves out those details, which will matter more than how loudly he promises a finish.

For Joshua, the danger would be treating Fury’s comments as a reliable preview. Preparing exclusively for an aggressive opponent could leave him chasing if Fury instead uses movement and makes him reset. Joshua needs to be ready for both approaches.

There is also a difference between hurting Joshua and finishing him. If Fury lands cleanly, his next decisions would matter: press immediately, control the distance, or risk getting caught while looking for the stoppage. A knockout prediction skips over that difficult work.

Fury has supplied a clear promotional promise. He wants the audience expecting a confrontation and a decisive ending. Joshua’s job is to make him pay for entering range, and force Fury to reconsider how much of that promise he intends to keep.

Ghana News.title: Yaw Ampofo Ankrah suspended as NSA Director-General amid World Cup visa controversy
Ghana News.content:
Yaw Ampofo Ankrah has been suspended from his position as Director-General of the National Sports Authority (NSA), following controversy over an alleged visa facilitation arrangement linked to the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

JoySports has sighted a letter signed by the Secretary to the President, Dr Calitus Mahama, communicating the decision to Mr Ankrah.

His removal comes weeks after allegations emerged that about US$623,000 was received from prospective travellers seeking assistance with visa and travel arrangements for the World Cup.

The allegations triggered a police investigation, with Mr Ankrah and other individuals connected to the matter appearing before the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) of the Ghana Police Service.

Mr Ankrah appeared before the police last week, where he denied the allegations levelled against him.

The Director-General had previously denied knowledge of any arrangement involving the collection of money from prospective World Cup travellers.

The NSA has also maintained that it did not authorise any visa facilitation service or establish an office to collect money from members of the public seeking to travel to the tournament.

In a statement issued in September, the Authority said its relationship with TRIBE FEST, a FIFA-licensed partner involved in fan-experience activities, World Cup viewing events and mobilisation, did not extend to authorising the collection of money for visa procurement.

The controversy followed a petition reportedly submitted to the CID on September 8, alleging that individuals connected to the NSA received money from prospective travellers on the understanding that their travel and visa arrangements for the World Cup would be facilitated.

The Minority in Parliament subsequently called for Mr Ankrah to be dismissed or suspended while investigations continued.

The Ranking Member on Parliament's Youth and Sports Committee, Vincent Ekow Assafuah, said information available to the Minority suggested that some prospective travellers were charged as much as $8,000 for assistance with World Cup travel arrangements.

The Minority said the alleged arrangement generated more than US$600,000 and demanded answers about who authorised it, who received the money and what services were provided.

The NSA, however, rejected the suggestion that the alleged operation was an official arrangement of the Authority.

It said no employee had been authorised to collect money or facilitate visas on behalf of the NSA.

The Authority further said its legal team was cooperating with the police investigation and that Mr Ankrah and other relevant officials would make themselves available to investigators if required.

Mr Ankrah's removal therefore comes while the police investigation into the allegations remains a live matter.

The dismissal itself does not establish criminal liability or prove the allegations against him.

Mr Ankrah had been Director-General of the NSA during a period of heightened scrutiny over the management of the country's sporting facilities and administration.

On September 2, President John Dramani Mahama dissolved the governing board of the National Sports Authority as part of a wider decision affecting several state institutions. The board was subsequently expected to be reconstituted.

The latest decision now brings Mr Ankrah's tenure as Director-General to an end.

It also comes at a critical period for Ghanaian sport, with the country continuing preparations for several international competitions and renewed attention on the management, financing and accountability of state sports institutions.

The police investigation is expected to establish whether money was collected from prospective travellers, who received the funds, what representations were made to those who paid, and whether any public officials or institutions were involved.

Associate Professor at the University of Education, Winneba, Emmanuel Sarpong hss been appointed as acting Director-General.

Ghana News.title: Yaw Ampofo Ankrah sacked as NSA Director-General
Ghana News.content:
Yaw Ampofo Ankrah has been removed from his position as Director-General of the National Sports Authority (NSA), bringing his tenure at the sports governing body to an end.

His dismissal comes just weeks after controversy surrounding an alleged visa facilitation scheme linked to the 2026 FIFA World Cup, for which the Minority in Parliament had called for his suspension or removal. The NSA has denied the allegations and said its legal team was cooperating with a police investigation.

Ampofo Ankrah’s removal follows a meeting involving himself, Sports and Recreation Minister Kofi Adams and other senior government officials at Jubilee House on Thursday.

Professor Emmanuel Osei Sarpong, a former member of the NSA Governing Board and Associate Professor of Exercise and Sports Science at the University of Education, Winneba, is expected to replace him. Osei Sarpong was among the members of the NSA board dissolved by President John Dramani Mahama earlier this month.

Ampofo Ankrah assumed the position in March 2025 and faced mounting scrutiny over the management and maintenance of sports facilities across the country, particularly the condition of major stadia.

His tenure also saw several controversies, including a dispute over the recruitment of 17 staff members, which resulted in the NSA board directing management to revoke the appointments.

The latest development brings to an end an 18-month tenure that has been marked by both institutional initiatives and sustained scrutiny over the management of Ghana’s sports infrastructure and administration.

Ghana News.title: SSNIT increases stake in Societe Generale Ghana to 24.36%
Ghana News.content:
The Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) has announced that it has secured an additional 5.0% stake in Societe Generale Ghana.

The development now brings SSNIT's total holding in the bank to 24.36%, from 19.36.

In a statement issued today, SSNIT said the development follows the completion of the acquisition of Societe Generale Group’s 60.22% controlling stake in the bank by Attijariwafa Bank and SSNIT.

It explained that the “Trust appreciates the support of the Government of Ghana, particularly the Minister responsible for Finance, who was instrumental in securing the additional stake and completing the transaction”.

“The deal enhances the Trust’s position to safeguard and grow contributors’ retirement assets while supporting the long-term development and stability of the Bank”, it added.

SSNIT continued that “The transaction also advances greater Ghanaian participation in the banking sector by increasing local ownership in a major financial institution”.

“This reflects the importance of ensuring that Ghanaian workers, pensioners and institutions benefit more directly from the growth and performance of the country’s financial sector”, SSNIT added.

The Trust commended Attijariwafa Bank for its cooperation throughout the transaction and acknowledged the Bank of Ghana and the Securities and Exchange Commission for their regulatory oversight.

Ghana News.title: Africa cannot rely on government budgets alone to finance climate ambitions – Deputy Finance Minister
Ghana News.content:
Deputy Finance Minister Thomas Ampem Nyarko

Deputy Finance Minister Thomas Nyarko Ampem says Africa cannot rely on government budgets alone to finance its climate ambitions, as countries face growing pressure on public finances.

Speaking at the opening of the Green Climate Fund’s Regional Dialogue for West and Central Africa in Accra, Mr Nyarko Ampem said governments were already stretched by competing demands for public funding, from education and healthcare to infrastructure and social protection, while climate change was adding further financial pressures.

He said public and concessional financing should instead be deployed strategically to lower investment risks and help mobilise private capital.

“We cannot fund every climate investment from the public purse, nor should we attempt to. The national budget cannot be the only engine pulling the climate finance train,” he stated.

According to the African Development Bank, Africa needs an estimated $2.7 trillion between 2020 and 2030 to implement its climate commitments.

Mr Nyarko Ampem said the challenge was therefore not only about securing climate finance but also about using public resources to unlock significantly larger volumes of private investment.

He said this approach would help countries respond to their climate financing needs without placing additional pressure on already constrained public finances.

Ghana currently has 13 projects in its Green Climate Fund portfolio, with about $209 million in GCF financing and a further $5.7 million in approved readiness support.

The figures highlight Ghana’s engagement with the Fund as the country seeks to mobilise resources for climate-related investments.

Green Climate Fund Director for the Africa Region, Catherine Koffman, said the Fund has so far committed about $20 billion towards its $50 billion target for 2030, representing roughly 40 percent of the target.

Ms Koffman said the GCF was working towards its $50 billion financing target by 2030, with a significant share of its commitments expected to support climate action in Africa, particularly in the West and Central Africa region.

“We want to achieve 50 billion by 2030. At the moment we are at $20 billion at GCF, and 40% of that goes to the Africa region, which is about $7.6 billion. And for West and Central Africa, which is what this dialogue is about, it's about $2.9 billion,” she said.

The Green Climate Fund has committed about $2.9 billion across 80 projects in West and Central Africa, according to the Fund.

The four-day regional dialogue is bringing together governments, financial institutions, and private-sector partners from 25 countries to discuss ways of scaling up access to climate finance.

The meeting comes as the Green Climate Fund begins its third replenishment process and works towards expanding its regional presence in Africa.

The dialogue is expected to provide an opportunity for stakeholders to discuss financing needs and ways to mobilise greater resources for climate investments across West and Central Africa.

Ghana News.title: COMAC gives Finance Ministry 14 days to suspend implementation of Section 136 of Customs Act
Ghana News.content:
Dr. Riverson Oppong

The Chamber of Oil Marketing Companies (COMAC) has given the Finance Ministry a 14-day ultimatum to suspend the implementation of Section 136 of the revised Customs Act.

According to the Chamber, the failure to do this will result in an emergency general meeting to agree on the next steps through all legitimate administrative, regulatory, and legal channels.

In a statement, COMAC, pointed out that “we have no interest in disruption, given the essential service its members provide to households and businesses”.

It is, however, unable to operate with confidence under a framework that has not been tested, explained, or justified, and which in its view shifts the risk of enforcement failures to operators and ultimately to the Ghanaian consumer.

The Chamber stated that it considers Section 136 to be a transfer of risk and not reform.

“That is why our position remains that existing controls should be enforced, with full transparency on overrides and exceptions and a complete accounting for products, before any replacement of the system is contemplated”, it pointed out.

Again, the Chamber argued that it wants an immediate and indefinite suspension of Section 136to be announced publicly by the Minister of Finance.



It also wants the retention of the existing framework: BIDECs to pay import duties and port charges at importation, and OMCs/LPGMCs to continue accounting for taxes and levies ex-pump.

Background

COMAC, in a letter this week seen by JOYBUSINESS argues that it is kicking against the implementation of the sections of the Customs Act due to the fact that Section 136(3) requires a BIDEC to account for tax at the point of sale, while section 136(5) permits the Commissioner-General (CG) to defer payment for up to 21 days via a bank guarantee.

The Chamber went ahead to state that “It migrates liability currently secured by OMC/LPGMC guarantees, bonds, and self-recognisance to the bulk-supply tier.”

It recalled at the meeting that the GRA’s rationale to deal with “fewer entities” and address marketer defaults was unsupported by any memorandum or assessment, highlighting that this stated rationale is flawed.

COMAC also raised serious concerns about enforcing the act, arguing that the current system is effective when enforced. “GRA would face an impossible choice: enforce and trigger a national supply shock, or forbear and allow arrears to balloon. Risk becomes concentrated, not reduced”.

Ghana News.title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers
Ghana News.content:
WhatsApp is introducing new parental controls for teenagers as tech companies come under pressure to provide more age-appropriate experiences for children.

The social messaging app's new tools will give parents a range of options, such as being told when their child joins or leaves a group. It will also let them decide on privacy settings for their account.

In a blog post, WhatsApp clarified that parents would not be given the ability to see the messages their teen sends and receives, which, along with calls, would remain private and protected by end-to-end encryption.

And it said the controls were optional, which social media analyst Matt Navarra called an "obvious weakness".

He said the move was "fairly convenient" for Meta, which owns WhatsApp, because it reduced the company's reliance on age verification by putting some responsibility on parents and teenagers.

"Meta is trying to show regulators we have a child safety system, we have parental controls, and we're rolling it out across our platforms," he said.

"I think the big unanswered question is whether enough families will actually use it."

The minimum age to use WhatsApp is 13 in the UK, although it is higher in some countries.

According to the firm, parents will be able to adjust or switch off the controls at any time.

The settings will be "straightforward to set up" using a Pin set by a parent, which teens will need if they want to switch off the controls.

Some of the new privacy tools include selecting who can see a child's profile photo and who can add them to groups.

Parents can also choose how their teenager uses Channels, which allows organisations and public figures to send out content.

And they will have the option of choosing between the default 13+ setting for Meta AI, the app's optional built-in AI assistant, or a stricter "Limited Content" option.

"All of these controls are being designed to support open conversations about how to use WhatsApp between parents and teens, while keeping everyone's personal messages private," the company said.

The changes come as pressure mounts on tech companies from governments and regulators to change the way they operate in order to better protect children using their platforms.

In June, the government announced it plans to ban under-16s from social media platforms, with the restrictions expected to come into force in March 2027.

It said "highly effective age assurance" measures would be used to check the age of those using social media.

WhatsApp is currently excluded from the ban because the government considers it a messaging service.

Ghana News.title: Afoko could help Bawumia pursue ‘clean break’ ahead of 2028 – Dr Amakye-Boateng
Ghana News.content:
Political Science lecturer Dr Kwasi Amakye-Boateng says the fact that New Patriotic Party (NPP) flagbearer Mahamudu Bawumia and National Chairmanship candidate Awentami Paul Afoko are both from northern Ghana should not, in itself, be a consideration in determining their suitability for leadership positions in the party.

Speaking on Kumasi-based Akoma FM, the Senior Lecturer at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) said the regional background of the two politicians should be immaterial if they were considered capable of contributing to the party’s objectives.

His comments followed a question about concerns that having Dr Bawumia as the NPP’s flagbearer and Mr Afoko as National Chairman could lead to complaints that both leaders come from the same broad part of the country.

“Why should that be an issue? If they are capable and they can contribute to the collective aspirations of the party, then what is the problem?” he asked.

Dr Amakye-Boateng said such considerations should not overshadow what he described as the party’s collective aspirations.

He argued that the NPP’s history showed that competence and the ability to contribute to the party had often taken precedence over individuals’ specific backgrounds.

“If your opponent has nothing else to say, they will resort to trivialities,” he said.

According to him, the party’s interests should be prioritised when choosing people for leadership positions.

He said political opponents could resort to what he described as “trivialities”, including regional background, when they believed they had little else to argue.

Dr Amakye-Boateng also pointed to what he described as an emerging tradition within the NPP of supporting people based on their competence.

He cited Dr Bawumia’s rise within the party as an example, arguing that party members recognised his capacity when they elected him as their presidential candidate.

The political scientist also referred to the NPP’s history of diverse leadership, arguing that the backgrounds of its leaders had not prevented the party from bringing different people together around its political objectives.

Afoko’s return to active politics

Dr Amakye-Boateng said Mr Afoko’s return to active politics could provide the NPP with an opportunity to pursue reconciliation and bring back members who had become disaffected or withdrawn from the party.

His comments come ahead of the NPP’s national officers’ elections scheduled for October 3, 2026, as the party prepares for the 2028 general election. The election will be held in Kumasi, with four candidates contesting the National Chairmanship position: John Boadu, Sammy Crabbe, Paul Afoko and Boakye Agyarko.

Ghana News.title: Global Capacity Hub conference connects Ghanaian businesses to technology, investment opportunities in London
Ghana News.content:
Global Capacity Hub has held the third edition of its AI, Emerging Technologies & Investment for Business Growth Conference in London, bringing together technology experts, investors, entrepreneurs and business leaders to explore opportunities for innovation, investment and growth.

The conference, held on Saturday, September 26, 2026, at the Sheraton Heathrow Hotel under the theme, “Innovate. Invest. Grow.”, marked the second time the event has been hosted in London.

The latest edition expanded the focus of the conference from artificial intelligence and emerging technologies to include investment and business growth.

According to the organisers, the expansion was intended to provide Ghanaian-owned businesses in Ghana and the United Kingdom with access to investors, funding opportunities and strategic partnerships.

The conference was organised by Stephen Forson, Director-General of Global Capacity Hub, and Edward Akorsah, the organisation’s UK Country Director.

Anthonia Adesuwa Owie and Afia Aninwaa served as co-hosts.

Participants attended both physically and virtually, with the programme featuring keynote presentations, panel discussions, practical workshops, exhibitions, networking sessions and a formal dinner.

Focus on practical use of AI

A key message from the conference was the growing role of artificial intelligence as a practical business tool rather than simply a subject for discussion.

Sessions focused on how entrepreneurs and organisations can use AI and emerging technologies to improve productivity, address business challenges, access new markets and remain competitive.

Speakers included Alex Flint, Executive Director at NatWest; Augustine Gyawu Adjei, Head of Engineering at Hubtel; Dr M. G. Srikanthan, Principal AI Strategist; Leanne Boytler, a British business executive in global operations and life sciences; and Isaac Appiah-Kubi, Founder and CEO of Crowned Eagle Financial Services.

Others were Frederick Afrifa, Founder and Managing Director of Leadership Communication Group; AI governance specialist Anthony Baafi; AI automation consultant Fredrick Lutterodt; and business development professional Amina Tabiou.

One of the key sessions was an investment pitching segment, during which selected businesses presented their ventures to potential investors.

The organisers said the session was designed to turn the conference’s expanded investment focus into practical opportunities for participating businesses.

Ghana’s investment opportunities

The Ghana High Commission in the United Kingdom also attended the conference and used the platform to highlight Ghana’s investment potential to prospective investors.

Its participation, according to the organisers, reinforced the conference’s objective of connecting international capital and expertise with business opportunities in Ghana.

The event was supported by Hubtel as the Main Sponsor, with Crowned Eagle Financial as Organising Partner and CoreConnect Limited as Marketing Partner.

iPRO Solutions and Enniclic also provided sponsorship support.

The organisers also recognised Isaac Appiah-Kubi, CEO of Crowned Eagle Financial UK, for his contribution to the organisation and delivery of the conference.

Networking and partnerships

Beyond the presentations and workshops, the conference placed emphasis on networking and relationship-building among participants.

The organisers encouraged professionals and entrepreneurs to view conferences and similar platforms as opportunities to build relationships, exchange ideas and identify potential partnerships and investment opportunities.

“Some of the most important opportunities begin with a conversation. Conferences bring people with different ideas, experiences, resources and networks into the same space. When people connect and share ideas, possibilities for collaboration, investment and growth emerge,” the organisers said.

They urged entrepreneurs, business owners, professionals and young people to make greater use of conferences, seminars and networking platforms to expand their knowledge and professional networks.

Dubai, Accra editions ahead

The London conference forms part of Global Capacity Hub’s planned international programme, with the next edition scheduled for Dubai in March 2027.

The conference is expected to return to Ghana in June 2027.

The organisers said the upcoming editions would continue to focus on the intersection of emerging technologies, investment and enterprise, while providing businesses and professionals with opportunities to gain knowledge, build networks, establish partnerships and explore potential investment.

Global Capacity Hub expressed appreciation to its speakers, partners, sponsors, participants, volunteers and other stakeholders for supporting the third edition.

The organisation said it would continue to develop platforms aimed at connecting people, ideas and opportunities to create measurable impact.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: HIV prevention drug hailed as breakthrough, but who gets access?
World.content:
Lenacapavir, a twice-a-year injection could transform HIV prevention, but it will not be available to all.

Share HIV prevention drug hailed as breakthrough, but who gets access? on social media

A medicine injected just twice a year could transform the fight against HIV.

In a 2024 clinical trial involving more than 2,000 young women in South Africa and Uganda, no participants who received lenacapavir contracted HIV.

Developed by United States pharmaceutical company Gilead Sciences, the injectable drug can be used to prevent HIV.

“It’s the most innovative tool that has reached the HIV arena for the last decade, because it’s the closest we have [to] a vaccine,” Carlota Baptista da Silva, global HIV lead at Doctors Without Borders (known by its French initials, MSF), told Al Jazeera.

The World Health Organization has recommended the long-acting injectable as an additional form of pre-exposure prophylaxis, or PrEP – medicine to reduce the risk of getting HIV.

But the arrival of the drug comes at a challenging juncture in the global fight against HIV.

International funding for HIV fell 18 percent in 2025, to $7.3bn, its lowest level in nearly two decades, according to the United Nations programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS). The squeeze has already hit prevention programmes: The number of people receiving medicine to reduce risk fell from 1.4 million in 2024 to 1.1 million in 2025.

That makes the arrival of a highly effective, twice-yearly prevention option significant. The question of who can access it is now more urgent.

For MSF, the scientific question has largely been answered: lenacapavir can prevent HIV with remarkable efficacy.

The fight now is whether the rules governing manufacture, price and supply will allow that scientific breakthrough to reach the people who need it.



Why some countries are excluded

In the United States, lenacapavir costs about $28,000 per person annually. Generic versions are expected to cost about $40 a year.

A generic version is a copy of the original drug made by another manufacturer after the patent holder licenses the technology. It contains the same active ingredient, but it can be produced and sold at a much lower price.

In June 2025, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved lenacapavir for HIV prevention, giving people the option of an injection twice a year. But in several low- and middle-income countries, access to cheaper versions is not expected at scale until 2027.

Gilead is supplying its own version of lenacapavir at no profit for programmes supported by the Global Fund and the US President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), with rollouts under way in countries including South Africa, Kenya, Zambia, Nigeria and Eswatini.

These are not the cheaper generic versions expected to cost about $40 per person a year. Gilead has licensed six manufacturers to produce those, with large-scale generic rollout expected in 2027.

At least 26 middle-income countries are excluded from Gilead’s generics agreement, MSF says, including countries with rising HIV infections and some that helped test the drug. Among them are Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Peru.

“People should not really help generate the evidence for breakthrough medicine and then find that their country is excluded from affordable generic access,” da Silva said.
