World.title: Liberia: Relief for Struggling Parents as CYTO Movement Delivers School Supplies Across Liberia’s Southeast
World.content:
South East, Liberia– For families struggling to get their children ready for school, the cost of copybooks, bags and shoes can be difficult to meet. Across southeastern Liberia, a school supplies distribution by the CYTO Movement is helping some parents carry that burden.

By Jaheim T. [email protected]

Led by its Chief Executive Officer, Cytarus Grace Dahn, the movement has been distributing educational materials to children as part of a drive covering Grand Gedeh, Sinoe, Maryland, River Gee and Grand Kru counties.



The supplies were provided through the Ministry of State for Presidential Affairs under President Joseph Boakai’s back-to-school initiative, according to Dahn. She said the focus is on children whose parents or guardians cannot afford some of the basic items needed for classes.

The materials include school bags, copybooks, pens, pencils, sneakers and jackets. The movement says the consignment includes approximately 5,000 copybooks, 5,000 pairs of sneakers and a combined 5,000 jackets and reflective jackets.

Dahn said the support is meant to ease pressure on families and help children return to school prepared.

More Than 800 Children Reached in Grand Kru

In Barclayville, Grand Kru County, more than 800 students, predominantly girls, received school materials, according to a September 21 report by journalist James Myking Suah of Grand Kru TV.

CYTO’s National Chairperson, Tommy Wesseh, told reporters that the distribution mainly targeted children from nursery through third grade.

He said seven schools were reached, including George Toe Washington Elementary School, Assembly of God Mission School and Pentecostal Foundation School. Children received bags, copybooks, shoes and other school essentials.

The assistance also extended beyond the classrooms. Elders and young people in Flohken received clothing and footwear.

Wesseh thanked the Office of the President for supporting the exercise and acknowledged the cooperation of local education officials and community members.

He also addressed questions about school bags bearing President Boakai’s image. According to Wesseh, the image was intended to acknowledge the President’s support for the programme, rather than ask beneficiaries to support him politically.

Support for Schools in Maryland

In Maryland County, the team distributed materials to selected schools in Harper and engaged communities in Pleebo.

Schools listed among the beneficiaries included Cape Palmas High School, Harper Demonstration School, East Harper High School, John Hillary Tubman High School, S. E. Gibson Kindergarten and Elementary School, Big Town Public School and Samuel H. Marriem School.

Dahn said the assistance was intended to help students from households facing financial difficulties.

During her engagement in Pleebo, however, she raised a concern that went beyond the shortage of school supplies. She said some children she encountered could not read the words printed on a shirt.

That experience prompted her to call on President Boakai and the Ministry of Education to give greater attention to learning conditions in rural communities.

Her concern pointed to another need: children require books and bags, but they also need the teaching and support that will help them learn.

The team also distributed reflective jackets to motorcyclists in Maryland. The wider tour included stops in Grand Gedeh and River Gee, with the movement reporting that its school materials distribution concluded in River Gee.

From an Election Group to Community Support

Dahn said CYTO was founded in 2023 and now has about 1,206 members, with a presence in seven counties.

She explained that the movement grew out of a group of young people she brought together to support Boakai during the elections. After the elections, she began looking for ways to help those young people improve their lives.

Some received assistance to attend school. Others received financial support to start small businesses.

According to Wesseh, the movement has also helped young people access scholarships at vocational training institutions and universities.

Dahn said the organisation’s wider goal is humanitarian, reaching Liberians who need assistance and working with individuals, organisations and government institutions willing to support that effort.

She travelled with CYTO colleagues and Edward Lahai of Congo Town for the southeastern distribution exercise, which was planned as a five-day trip across the five counties.

For the children reached, the support provides basic items they need for school. For their parents and guardians, it takes some of the pressure off the household budget at a time when getting a child back into the classroom comes with several expenses.

Dahn said the movement hopes to secure further support so it can reach more children and communities.

World.title: Liberia: APM Terminals Elevates Liberian Talent, Names First Female Shift Manager, New Head of Operations
World.content:
Monrovia – As Liberia’s gateway to global trade continues to evolve, building local expertise remains essential to delivering safe, efficient, and reliable port operations. For more than a decade, APM Terminals Liberia has invested in developing Liberian talent, creating opportunities for employees to grow into leadership positions across the Freeport of Monrovia.

The recent appointments of Edwina Decontee Mowon and Ebenezer Opoku reflect the results of that long-term commitment to skills development, career growth, and succession planning.

Edwina joined APM Terminals Liberia in 2011 as the terminal’s first female Gate Administrator. Through continuous learning and experience across several operational functions, she advanced through roles including Dispatcher, Auxiliary Operations, and Berth Supervisor. In 2023, she became the terminal’s first female Berth Supervisor, and in 2026 achieved another milestone as the terminal’s first female Shift Manager.



Today, she plays a key role in coordinating vessel, yard, and gate operations, helping ensure the smooth movement of cargo through Liberia’s busiest port.

Ebenezer’s journey began in 2013 as an Intern after studies at the Liberia Maritime Training Institute (LMTI). Over the years, he progressed through a series of operational and planning leadership positions, gaining expertise in terminal operations, planning, and performance management. His leadership capabilities also saw him contribute to operational standardization initiatives across Asia and the Middle East.

On 1 September 2026, he was appointed Head of Operations within the Senior Management team, becoming one of the Liberian leaders responsible for overseeing operations at the country’s main trade gateway.

Together, their stories demonstrate how investment in people can strengthen local capacity and prepare Liberian professionals to lead increasingly complex maritime operations.

Developing local talent has remained a key focus for APM Terminals Liberia since the start of the concession. Through training, mentorship and leadership development, many Liberians have built careers in port and marine operations, engineering, safety, administration and management, contributing to a stronger and more capable Liberian maritime workforce.

As trade volumes grow and customer expectations continue to evolve, the development of skilled Liberian professionals remains central to the terminal’s ability to support Liberia’s economic ambitions and maintain an efficient gateway for imports and exports.

The journeys of Edwina and Ebenezer highlight what can be achieved when talent, opportunity and investment come together and demonstrates the growing role Liberian professionals are playing in shaping the future of our country’s maritime sector.

World.title: Liberia: How Chief Justice Gbeisay’s Judiciary is Bringing the Gavel Closer to the Ordinary in Bong County
World.content:
Dafuwah hasn’t made headlines with landmark rulings. What’s drawn attention instead is something smaller and, in some ways, harder to quantify that the way he runs his courtroom. Where the law allows for it, he’s known for slowing down before assigning winners and losers — asking questions, hearing both sides out fully, and testing whether the dispute in front of him can be settled through dialogue rather than confrontation

GBARNGA, Bong County — Ask most Liberians what the word “court” conjures, and the answer rarely involves comfort. For decades, the courthouse has stood in the public imagination as two separate buildings occupying the same address: one for those who can pay their way through the system, and another — slower, colder, more intimidating — for everyone else.

By Selma Lomax, [email protected]

That divide wasn’t invented by any single scandal. It was built up over years of war, weak institutions, whispered accusations of bias on the bench, case backlogs that stretched on indefinitely, and legal fees that put the process out of reach for the people who needed it most. A farmer, a market seller, a motorbike taxi driver weighing whether to file a complaint wasn’t just asking “am I right?” They were asking whether they could survive the process long enough to find out.



A Different Kind of Magistrate

That backdrop makes it easier to understand why people in Gbarnga have started talking about Stipendiary Magistrate Richard M. Dafuwah, who took over the city’s Magisterial Court roughly a year ago from his predecessor, Daniel Dolokelen.

Dafuwah hasn’t made headlines with landmark rulings. What’s drawn attention instead is something smaller and, in some ways, harder to quantify that the way he runs his courtroom. Where the law allows for it, he’s known for slowing down before assigning winners and losers — asking questions, hearing both sides out fully, and testing whether the dispute in front of him can be settled through dialogue rather than confrontation.

People who’ve watched him work describe a magistrate who treats the poorest litigant with the same attention as anyone else. One resident familiar with the court’s proceedings put it simply: coming before Dafuwah, a person doesn’t feel dismissed for being ordinary — he lets them explain themselves fully before he acts. Another resident described the effect as almost as important as any verdict: being taken seriously restores a person’s faith that the process is actually working for them.

The Health Workers’ Case

The clearest test of that approach came when Bong County’s health worker protests spilled into legal territory. After a night in police custody, the workers’ leader was brought before the Gbarnga Magisterial Court — a moment that could easily have hardened into a standoff between striking workers and the government.

Instead, accounts from the community describe Dafuwah working to de-escalate the situation, engaging both sides directly rather than letting the confrontation deepen. It’s a small case study in what advocates of court-based mediation argue is possible: using the authority of the bench not to punish, but to create space for people to find their own resolution — without ever abandoning the law that governs the outcome.

That distinction matters. Mediation isn’t a replacement for adjudication, and no one — including Dafuwah’s admirers — argues it should be. Serious crimes, constitutional questions, and cases that legally demand a formal ruling still have to go through the full judicial process. But plenty of disputes that land in a magisterial court don’t need that kind of weight brought down on them. Sometimes what’s needed is simpler: someone willing to actually listen before deciding.

Justice as a Relationship, Not Just a Ruling

There’s a practical reason this matters beyond any single case. In a place like Gbarnga, the parties to a dispute don’t disappear from each other’s lives once a judgment is entered. They still share a market, a church, a school, a water source. A ruling can settle who’s legally right. It can’t necessarily repair what broke between two neighbors — but a resolution both sides had a hand in shaping just might.

That’s the argument residents make when they describe what they’ve seen from Dafuwah: that treating people with dignity and giving them room to be heard doesn’t soften justice — it expands what justice is capable of doing. As one community member framed it, people don’t just want a ruling; they want to be seen and treated with respect along the way, and that’s what they say they’ve gotten from him.

A Bigger Story Than One Courtroom

Dafuwah’s rising local reputation lands at a moment when Liberia’s Judiciary, under Chief Justice Yamie Quiqui Gbeisay Sr., has been pushing to make courts more present — and more credible — outside Monrovia. In September 2026, the Judiciary formally seated 73 newly appointed magistrates across all 15 counties, a move officials framed as extending access to justice into the country’s most remote areas.

Earlier, in June 2026, Gbeisay announced a performance-based evaluation system meant to reward professionalism and accountability among judges and magistrates annually.

Dafuwah’s rising local reputation lands at a moment when Liberia’s Judiciary, under Chief Justice Yamie Quiqui Gbeisay Sr., has been pushing to make courts more present — and more credible — outside Monrovia. In September 2026, the Judiciary formally seated 73 newly appointed magistrates across all 15 counties, a move officials framed as extending access to justice into the country’s most remote areas

Those are administrative moves, made from the top. But their success or failure will be measured almost entirely at the bottom — in rooms exactly like the one Dafuwah presides over. For most Liberians, the Supreme Court in Monrovia is an abstraction. The magistrate down the street is the actual, physical face of the justice system: the person who decides, in real time, whether the law is something that protects them or something that happens to them.

That’s precisely why a single magistrate’s demeanor carries outsized weight. A citizen who leaves a courtroom feeling heard walks away more willing to trust the next institution they encounter. A citizen who leaves feeling dismissed carries that suspicion into every future interaction with the state — and, in the worst cases, may decide that formal institutions aren’t worth the trouble at all, pushing disputes back into the community where they can curdle into retaliation and violence instead.

The Limits of Popularity

None of this means Dafuwah should be judged, or judge himself, by how well-liked he is. A magistrate’s job isn’t to be popular — it’s to apply the law, and sometimes that means handing down decisions that disappoint the very people who’d otherwise praise him. A year on the bench is a short track record, and his long-term legacy will rest on the consistency of his rulings, his independence from outside pressure, and his fidelity to due process — not on goodwill alone.

But the goodwill itself is worth paying attention to, because of what it reveals about what Liberians have been missing. The admiration building around Dafuwah isn’t really about him as an individual. It’s a proxy for a much larger and older demand: fairness, access, timeliness, and the basic experience of being taken seriously — regardless of how much money or influence a person carries into the room.

What Comes Next

The real test of Liberia’s judicial reform push won’t be the number of magistrates seated or systems announced. It will be what happens after those magistrates put on the robe: whether citizens feel safe walking into their courtrooms, whether the poor believe they’ll get a fair hearing, whether political and financial pressure gets resisted, and whether officers of the court can tell the difference between a dispute that needs mediation and one that demands a formal ruling.

In Gbarnga, those questions are still being answered one case at a time. Dafuwah’s tenure is young, and its ultimate verdict — pun intended — will be written over years, not months. But for now, his court offers a glimpse of something Liberians have long been told to expect and have too rarely experienced: a justice system that treats ordinary people as though they belong inside it.

For a country still working to convince its own citizens that the courthouse door swings open for everyone, that glimpse — however modest, however local — is not nothing.

World.title: Liberia: MFDP Commences Executive Budget Hearings for FY2027 Today as Several Entities Lined Up
World.content:
Monrovia, September 30, 2026 – In an effort to have the 2027 National Budget submitted on or in time so as to enhance its full implementation, the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning (MFDP) has scheduled today, Thursday, October 1, 2026 for the kick-off of the budget hearing processes.

By Emmanuel Weedee-Conway

The Executive Budget Hearing is a legal requirement under the Public Financial Management (PFM) Act, wherein the Budget Policy and Coordination Committee consult with all Ministries, Agencies and Commissions (MACs) on their programs and budget justifications for the next fiscal year.



According to a statement issued by the MFDP, the exercise is another critical phase in the Government of Liberia’s national budget formulation process.

By law, MFDP must submit the national budget to the Legislature no later than October 31 of every year. In a bid to achieve this and especially to ensure that allocations are not arbitrary, there will be a thorough consultative process to ensure efficiency and effectiveness. During the hearings, MACs will be made to defend their budget to convince the panel of experts whether there is a need for addition or subtraction.

The process also among other things, aims to ensure that the FY2026 Budget align with the government’s 5-year development plan, the ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development (AAID).

The hearings, coordinated through the National Budget Committee (NBC), will allow spending entities to present and justify their proposed programs, priorities, expenditure requirements, and planned activities for Fiscal Year 2027.

The process is in line with the statutory mandate requiring the MFDP to consult with spending entities on their programs, commitments, and budgetary priorities before the preparation and submission of the National Budget.

The opening session on Thursday will focus on the Ministry of Mines and Energy, the Special Presidential Project Coordinating Committee (SPPCC), and the Public Procurement and Concessions Commission (PPCC), bringing together key institutions responsible for managing Liberia’s mineral and energy resources, coordinating priority presidential development projects, and overseeing public procurement and concessions.

During the hearings, participating institutions are expected to outline their proposed programs and activities, provide justification for their budgetary requests, and respond to questions concerning their priorities, implementation plans, and resource requirements.

The Executive Budget Hearings are scheduled to run through Friday, October 9, 2026, and will cover a broad range of sectors and spending entities across government.

World.title: State House Challenges Catholic Bishops’ Statement
World.content:
State House has challenged concerns raised by the Zambia Conference of Catholic Bishops over fear, ethnic manipulation and the shrinking democratic space, saying such claims should be supported by evidence.

In a statement issued in Lusaka, State House Chief Communications Specialist CLAYSON HAMASAKA said Government respects the Church’s role in national life but disagrees with suggestions that the country is facing a national crisis.

Mr. HAMASAKA said concerns about fear and anxiety should not be presented as representing the experience of the entire country without evidence.

He also defended the electoral process, saying concerns over elections should identify specific failures and demonstrate how they affected the outcome before questioning the decision made by voters.

On arrests involving opposition figures, State House said lawful accountability should be distinguished from political persecution.

Mr. HAMASAKA said an arrest does not amount to proof of guilt or persecution, adding that allegations of unlawful detention should be examined on an individual basis.

He also rejected suggestions of widespread insecurity or military control, following concerns raised by the Bishops regarding military personnel, violence and insecurity.

The Catholic Bishops had expressed concern over political polarisation, the manipulation of ethnic identities and tribal sentiments, freedom of expression, electoral credibility and reports of arrests and political violence.

State House welcomed the Bishops’ call for dialogue, civic education, accountability and reconciliation, but said such efforts should be based on verified facts and respect institutional independence.

Government also raised concern about the timing of the pastoral statement in relation to ongoing court proceedings involving a senior member of the clergy.

Mr. HAMASAKA said the timing of the statement alone does not establish an intention to influence the proceedings, but cautioned that messages portraying widespread fear and institutional failure could affect public sentiment around a matter requiring independent determination.

He stressed that the accused person’s dignity, presumption of innocence and right to a fair hearing must be protected, while investigators, prosecutors and the courts should perform their duties without interference.

State House has called for measured public communication, saying national dialogue should promote peace, cooperation and respect for lawful processes.

World.title: MUKANDILA Faces Forgery and False Document Charges
World.content:
Tonse Pamodzi Secretary General CELESTINE MUKANDILA has pleaded not guilty to charges of forgery and uttering false documents.

Mr. MUKANDILA, aged 36, entered the plea yesterday before Lusaka Resident Magistrate ANNA HOLLAND.

The prosecution alleges that between July 14, 2022 and July 25, 2024, Mr. MUKANDILA forged the signature of YAEES SALIM SHETH on a letter purporting to surrender shares in ZRIMS Farm Limited.

It is alleged that the letter falsely indicated that Mr. SHETH had surrendered his shares in the company.

Mr. MUKANDILA is also accused of fraudulently uttering a notice of forfeiture or surrender of shares, which is a document issued by the Patent and Companies Registration Agency -PACRA-.

Meanwhile, Mr. MUKANDILA has been granted 20,000 Kwacha cash bail pending trial.

He has also been ordered to provide two working sureties, each bound in the sum of 15,000 Kwacha in their own recognisance.

World.title: HELSB Seeks Private Investment in Student Loans
World.content:
The Higher Education Loans and Scholarships Board -HELSB- is calling for increased private sector investment in student financing to help bridge the funding gap in higher education.

HELSB says 45.3 percent of student financing needs remained unfunded in 2025, highlighting the need for additional sources of funding beyond government support.

HELSB Chief Executive Officer JOHN MACHAYI says banks, pension funds, insurance companies and asset managers can play a greater role in financing higher education.

Dr. MACHAYI says expanding the financing base will help increase access to higher education and provide Zambia with the skilled workforce needed for economic growth.

Speaking at the Zambia Capital Market Conference and Awards in Livingstone, Dr. MACHAYI, who is also President of the Association of African Higher Education Financing Agencies, said investment in student financing allows young people to acquire qualifications and enter the labour market.

He said HELSB’s annual disbursements increased from about 558 million Kwacha in 2021 to 1.8 billion Kwacha in 2025, while its loan portfolio grew to more than 10 billion Kwacha by June 2026.

Dr. MACHAYI has called on commercial banks to develop education-financing products tailored to the needs of working families.

He proposed financing options such as salary-linked repayments, staged payments based on verified university costs, and loans covering tuition, accommodation and learning materials.

Dr. MACHAYI said having a salary does not necessarily mean parents can meet university expenses when payments fall due.

He has also encouraged pension funds, insurers and asset managers to consider investing in structured education-financing arrangements.

Dr. MACHAYI said possible financing models could include bonds, social bonds and other investment instruments, but clarified that no bond issuance or investment commitment has been announced.

He said improved loan recovery will be important in building investor confidence.

HELSB recovered about 233.8 million Kwacha in 2025 and 129.9 million Kwacha during the first half of 2026, while the number of beneficiaries repaying their loans increased to more than 22,000 by June 2026.

Dr. MACHAYI has urged employers and beneficiaries to make timely repayments, saying recovered funds are used to support other students.

He said financial barriers could prevent young people from acquiring the skills needed for Zambia’s future development.

Dr. MACHAYI said he will prepare a concept proposal for consideration by the HELSB Board and engage relevant government authorities on possible financing options.

This is according to a statement issued to the media by HELSB Manager Corporate Affairs CHISELWA KAWANDA.

World.title: DEC Unearths Suspected Counterfeit Fertiliser Plant
World.content:
The Drug Enforcement Commission (DEC) has uncovered a plant allegedly involved in the manufacture of counterfeit fertiliser in 9 Miles and Meanwood Vorna Valley.

DEC Public Relations Officer Allan Tamba says the operation spans Chibombo and Chongwe districts in Central and Lusaka Provinces.

Mr. Tamba says four people have been arrested in connection with the alleged operation.

They are 40-year-old agricultural consultant Iwa Siame and businessmen John Ngulube, 34, Fortune Kalima, 49, and Stan Penti, 45.

Mr. Tamba says the four have been charged with producing farming requisites at an unregistered plant, possession of property suspected to be proceeds of crime, conspiracy to commit a felony and money laundering.

He said in a statement that the suspects allegedly manufactured and processed farming requisites at unregistered premises between January 1, 2025 and September 19, 2026.

Mr. Tamba said the DEC has seized 739 bags of suspected counterfeit fertiliser, as well as raw materials and equipment allegedly used in the operation.

He said the suspects are also accused of setting up an unauthorised operation involving the deceptive packaging and distribution of the fertiliser.

Mr. Tamba further alleged that proceeds from the sale of the suspected counterfeit fertiliser were used to acquire property for the suspects’ benefit.

He said the four suspects are in custody and are expected to appear in court soon.

Mr. Tamba has urged farmers and members of the public to exercise caution when buying fertiliser and other farming inputs and to source them only from legitimate suppliers and distributors.

He has also called on the public to report suspected criminal activities to the authorities.

World.title: Business community tipped on ZRA voluntary disclosure
World.content:
Central Province Permanent Secretary Milner Mwanakampwe has urged the business community to take advantage of the Extended Voluntary Disclosure Scheme by the Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA).

Dr Mwanakampwe says the scheme allows businesses and individuals to disclose previously declared liabilities and settle principal tax obligations with relief from qualifying penalties and interests.

Speaking when he officiated at the stakeholder engagement meeting on the Extended Voluntary Disclosure Scheme organized by ZRA in Kabwe, Dr Mwanakampwe said the voluntary exposure scheme seeks to regularise tax affairs on favourable terms to avoid penalties.

He emphasized that sustainable national development relies heavily on a robust revenue collection and voluntary tax compliance.

He said the government’s goal is to build a prosperous country powered by fair, transparent and collaborative tax administration.

And ZRA Assistant Director Sylvia Mukwiza says the Extended Voluntary Disclosure Scheme has been introduced to address tax-related challenges facing the business community.

Ms Mukwiza says ZRA wants to ensure that every eligible taxpayer in Central Province accesses this opportunity and operates with greater tax certainty and peace of mind moving forward.

Under this programme, taxpayers who disclose undeclared liabilities and settle their principal tax obligation receive a proportionate waiver of qualifying penalties and interest of up to 100 percent.

World.title: Government calls for healthcare protection
World.content:
Government has called on citizens, the private sector and quasi-government institutions to protect the gains Zambia has made in the health sector while strengthening the country’s capacity to finance and deliver quality healthcare.

Public Private Dialogue Forum (PPDF) Co-Chairperson Lackson Kasonka says increased domestic production of essential health commodities will contribute to Zambia’s economic growth.

Professor Kasonka, who is also Permanent Secretary for Special Duties at Cabinet Office, observed that diminishing donor funding is putting pressure on essential services and challenging the country to develop a more sustainable health financing model.

He was speaking in Lusaka today during the second PPDF Technical Working Group meeting held at the Mulungushi International Conference Centre.

He said the government has a central responsibility in strengthening the health sector, while the private sector brings valuable resources, innovation, expertise and investment.

He observed that a healthy population is critical to productivity, enterprise, investment and national prosperity.

The Co-Chairperson Government- side called for stronger partnerships between government, the private sector and other stakeholders to develop practical solutions that respond to national priorities and deliver measurable benefits to communities.

Prof Kasonka said the meeting should result in clear priorities, shared responsibilities and actionable commitments towards building a stronger and more resilient health sector.

Meanwhile, PPDF Co-Chairperson, Shailen Desai has urged members of the technical working group to actively participate in discussions aimed at strengthening public-private partnerships.

Dr Desai said stakeholders should utilise the platforms provided to openly discuss challenges and identify win-win solutions rather than raising concerns after meetings.

He said the public sector has a responsibility to facilitate an environment in which the private sector can operate effectively and contribute to economic growth.

He cited the tourism technical working group as an example of a sector where public-private collaboration has contributed to improved cooperation and development.

The Co-Chairperson Private-side stressed that the PPDF provides an opportunity for stakeholders; public and government to work together towards Zambia’s economic growth.

The meeting was attended by development experts and other stakeholders with expertise in economic development.

World.title: Chisamba family left homeless after fire
World.content:
A family of four in Chisamba District has been left homeless after their house was gutted by fire in a suspected case of arson.

The family is now spending nights in an open shelter after household property valued at approximately K46, 200 was destroyed in the fire.

Misheck Kapiya, 52, of Chisumpa Village in Chief Chamuka’s area, told ZANIS in Chisamba that the incident happened on September 7, 2026, around 21:00 hours.

Mr Kapiya said he saw flames coming from the thatched roof of his two-bedroom house as he approached his home.

“I saw flames where I was talking to my friends and somehow rushed home where I confirmed it was indeed my house on fire,” he said.

He said that by the time he reached the house, his wife, Idah Kapiya, was trying to rescue their two young grandchildren from the fire.

Mr Kapiya said all family members managed to escape unharmed, but their household belongings were completely destroyed.

Mrs Kapiya said she noticed flames coming from a corner of the bedroom shortly before she was about to fall asleep.

She said she immediately got out of the house with the children.

“When I saw the fire coming from the corner of the bedroom, I walked out with my grandsons, Felix Tembo, aged three, and Max Tembo, aged one year and some months, and some belongings,” she said.

Mrs Kapiya further alleged that while attempting to put out the fire, she saw Edward Mwansa running away from the direction of the house, whom she suspects of starting the fire.

The family said the property destroyed included 15 by 50-kilogramme bags of maize, kitchen utensils, a bag of sunflower seed, school uniforms, books, shoes, clothes, a bed and beddings.

The family has since appealed to Government, through the Disaster Risk Management Division for financial and material assistance.

Meanwhile, the suspected arsonist is in police custody and is appearing before court.

World.title: Mob beating claims life of suspected burglary suspect in Petauke
World.content:
A 28-year-old man has died after allegedly being beaten by a mob following a suspected burglary incident in Petauke District.

The deceased, identified as Stephen Banda of Tasala 5 Compound in Chief Kalindawalo’s area, died while receiving treatment at Petauke District Hospital.

The incident occurred around 02:00 hours on September 30, 2026, in Riverside Compound.

Eastern Province Police Commanding Officer Robertson Mweemba said 48-year-old Paul Zulu, the reporter in the matter, was asleep with his family when his wife, 38-year-old Mary Phiri, heard a loud noise coming from inside the house.

Mr Mweemba said Ms. Phiri woke up to investigate and found the kitchen door open, where she allegedly saw four unidentified people standing near the doorway.

She raised an alarm, attracting neighbours who managed to apprehend one of the suspects, identified as Mr Banda.

Mr Mweemba said Mr Banda was allegedly beaten by the mob before neighbourhood officers intervened and took him to Petauke Police Station.

He said Mr Banda was issued with a police medical report form and later taken to Petauke District Hospital, where he died while receiving treatment.

The body has since been deposited in the mortuary awaiting a postmortem examination as investigations into the matter continue.

World.title: Kenya: Politrack Poll - Ruto 45.1 Percent, Sifuna 19.6 Percent, Kalonzo 10.3 Percent If Elections Held Today
World.content:
Nairobi — President William Ruto leads the presidential preference survey by Politrack Africa, with 45.1 per cent of respondents saying they would vote for him if elections were held today.

The survey, released at a press conference in Nairobi on Thursday, places Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna second at 19.6 per cent, followed by Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka at 10.3 per cent. Undecided respondents account for 8.4 per cent, while former Interior Cabinet Secretary Fred Matiang'i has 7.2 per cent and former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua 6.0 per cent.

In its assessment, Politrack says Ruto "leads the national presidential preference tally at 45.1%", while Sifuna has emerged as a significant challenger with 19.6 per cent support.



Other candidates recorded lower levels of preference, with Prof George Wajackoyah at 1.1 per cent, Martha Karua and David Maraga at 0.8 per cent each, James Orengo at 0.4 per cent and Jimmy Wanjigi at 0.3 per cent.

At party level, Ruto's United Democratic Alliance leads with 32 per cent, followed by the Democracy for the Citizens Party at 11.7 per cent and ODM at 10.6 per cent. Jubilee has 6.9 per cent, Wiper 5.6 per cent, Kenya Kwanza 3.5 per cent and Azimio 3.2 per cent.

The survey also found a near-even split over the direction of the country, with 45.2 per cent saying Kenya is moving in the right direction and 44.6 per cent saying it is moving in the wrong direction. Another 10.2 per cent were unsure.

On government performance, respondents identified roads and housing, both at 16.3 per cent, as the areas where the government is performing best, followed by health services, SHIF and SHA at 13 per cent and agriculture at 10 per cent.

However, health services, SHIF and SHA also featured prominently among areas respondents viewed as performing poorly, at 19.2 per cent, followed by the fight against corruption at 18.4 per cent and the economy and cost of living at 12 per cent. Jobs and youth opportunities followed at 10.4 per cent.

The survey also examined attitudes towards a woman becoming Kenya's first female deputy president. Politrack reports that 53 per cent of respondents were ready for a woman deputy president, comprising 16 per cent who were "very ready" and 37 per cent who were "somewhat ready". Among those open to the prospect, Anne Waiguru had 36 per cent support, followed by Martha Karua at 27 per cent and Gladys Wanga at 15 per cent.

Politrack says the survey was conducted between September 15 and 25 among 20,419 respondents across the country. The national estimates were weighted according to each county's share of registered voters, with a margin of error of plus or minus three percentage points and a 95 per cent confidence level.

World.title: Kenya: Nairobi Tests Flood Response As Agencies Set Up Emergency Command Centre
World.content:
Heavy rains left more than 23 people dead in Nairobi in March 2026.

Nairobi — Nairobi has begun testing its emergency response system ahead of the October-December rains, with national and county agencies setting up a joint command centre at Charter Hall.

The exercise, dubbed Operation Okoa Maisha, is intended to test how authorities would respond to flooding and other emergencies, including the flow of information, deployment of rescue teams and evacuation of residents from high-risk areas.

The exercise brings together the Nairobi County Government, National Disaster Operations Centre, Kenya Red Cross, Kenya Defence Forces, Kenya Coast Guard and other emergency agencies.

Charter Hall will serve as the central coordination point during the exercise, with participating agencies expected to relay reports from the field to a single command post.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Governor Johnson Sakaja said the arrangement was intended to avoid different agencies working with separate information during an emergency.

"We need one report and one communication," Sakaja said.

The preparations come amid renewed attention to Nairobi's vulnerability to flooding, particularly in areas around the Mathare, Ngong and Nairobi rivers.

County teams have been clearing drains, desilting waterways and deploying earth-moving equipment in areas identified as flood hotspots.

The county has also identified evacuation centres and established emergency numbers 1508 and 1190 for residents requiring assistance.

Sakaja said authorities would also seek to move people living in areas considered dangerous, including sections of riparian land.

"Occupying riparian land is non-negotiable. You must move. We do not want you to die," he said.

The simulation is expected to expose weaknesses in the response system before an actual emergency occurs.

Among the issues being tested are how quickly an alert reaches response teams, how agencies coordinate rescue operations and whether residents in affected areas can be moved to safety.

The exercise also provides an opportunity to establish which agency takes responsibility for particular operations when several government and humanitarian organisations are responding to the same incident.

Nairobi has in previous rainy seasons experienced flooding in several parts of the city, disrupting transport and displacing residents.

The county is now using the simulation to test whether its current arrangements can cope with a major flood emergency when the rains intensify.

World.title: Nigeria: Tinubu Compares His Tough Policies to Painful Cancer Treatment
World.content:
"Nigeria was like a sick patient who receives the terrible news that he has cancer."

President Bola Tinubu on Thursday compared his tough policies to the essential cancer treatment a patient needs.

The Nigerian leader, in a televised address marking the country's 66th Independence Anniversary, said the situation inherited in 2023 warranted tough decisions that economists argue have caused Nigeria's worst cost of living crisis in a generation.

"Nigeria was like a sick patient who receives the terrible news that he has cancer. His doctor explains that the treatment will be difficult and painful, but that it offers a strong prospect of recovery. The patient has a choice. He can begin treatment, endure its discomfort and fight the disease. Or he can ask only for morphine, dull the pain and leave the cancer to spread.



"For too long, Nigeria's leaders chose morphine while praying for a miracle that never came," he said.

Mr Tinubu said previous administrations had focused on the symptoms of the country's economic problems while allowing the underlying issues to worsen.

"When this administration assumed office, we resolved to do things differently. We chose to excise the cancer. The reforms that followed were difficult. The side effects were real. Yet, we must never confuse the medicine with the disease," he said.

The President's comparison comes at a time when cancer remains a major health burden in Nigeria, with many patients diagnosed late and facing difficult treatment.

Cancer burden

The latest estimates from the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) show that Nigeria recorded an estimated 152,261 new cancer cases and 90,795 cancer deaths in 2024.

Breast cancer accounted for the highest number of new cases, followed by prostate and cervical cancers.

The figures highlight the scale of a disease that continues to claim thousands of lives in Nigeria each year, particularly where patients present late or are unable to access timely treatment.

Nigeria's 2025 Cancer Control Capacity and Needs Assessment also found that more than 70 per cent of cancer patients in the country present with advanced disease.

The National Institute for Cancer Research and Treatment (NICRAT) conducted the assessment with support from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the World Health Organisation (WHO).

The report identified late presentation as one of the major challenges affecting cancer outcomes in the country.

A 2025 study involving 264 cancer patients in Kano and Ibadan also found significant delays in diagnosis.

Close 

Researchers reported a median period of 12 months between patients first noticing symptoms and receiving a cancer diagnosis, with patients visiting a median of three health facilities before receiving a formal diagnosis.

Chemotherapy, other treatments can be difficult

Chemotherapy, one of the major treatments used for cancer, can cause side effects including severe tiredness, nausea and vomiting, hair loss, mouth sores and reduced blood-cell counts, depending on the drugs used and the individual patient.

Other treatments, including surgery and radiotherapy, can also be physically demanding and may require repeated hospital visits over weeks or months.

In Nigeria, access to these treatments remains a challenge. The 2025 national cancer-control assessment estimated that more than 120 radiation machines would be needed to adequately treat the country's cancer patients, but only 13 functional radiation machines were available at the time of the assessment.

It also found that patients often have to travel long distances to access radiotherapy.

The report further identified shortages of oncology specialists. It estimated that Nigeria had about 0.03 oncologists per 100,000 people and noted that skilled oncology staff were inadequate for the country's population.

World.title: Ethiopia: 'We Are Completely Isolated - Humanitarian Access Is Urgently Needed'
World.content:
Adigrat — "It is extremely urgent to facilitate humanitarian access, dialogue for peace and every form of dialogue. We are completely isolated, communications are blocked, and we have no contact with anyone." This is the message sent to Fides by the Eparch of Adigrat, Tesfaselassie Medhin, in a brief message sent with the support of UNICEF, which continues to assist the Church and, where possible, to maintain a minimum connection with the outside world.

"All communications are blocked; our Church, our missions, religious, the local clergy, we are in our places, as usual," the Eparch said. "We will accompany and help the people with our presence, through which we carry out the Church's mission of incarnation."

Medhin describes a situation of mounting difficulty: "Banks are also closed. We do not know for sure how our seminaries and schools will continue operating, but it is our intention to continue. We have no idea how we will manage provisions. Only God knows; we rely on Divine Providence."

Meanwhile, the situation in Ethiopia's northern region continues to deteriorate (see Fides, 30/9/2026). At the end of yesterday's General Audience, Wednesday, September 30, Pope Leo XIV expressed his "deep concern" over the renewed outbreak of hostilities in Tigray and appealed to all parties.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"I extend my heartfelt plea to all parties to choose the path of dialogue," the Pope said. "Armed conflict never solves problems but only worsens them, leaving in its wake a trail of death, destruction, and resentment. Only honest engagement can lay the foundations for lasting peace." Leo XIV also expressed the hope "that the international community will offer its generous and timely contribution, to ensuring that all humanitarian aid be provided to those in need."

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - October 1, 2026
World.content:
press review

Ethiopia Fighting Kills 52 Civilians in Tigray

At least 52 civilians have been killed during three days of heavy fighting around Alamata in Ethiopia's northern Tigray region. Government troops appeared to have taken control of the town and may be advancing towards Mekelle. Clashes have also spread to neighbouring Amhara and Afar regions. More than 700 wounded people have reportedly been admitted to hospitals supported by Médecins Sans Frontières. The fighting follows months of tension between the federal government and the Tigray People's Liberation Front, which accuse each other of violating the 2022 peace agreement. Communications and banking services have been disrupted in Tigray, worsening the humanitarian situation. Dozens of foreign tourists remain stranded in Lalibela after the airport closed. There are also concerns that Eritrea could become involved in the conflict.

Botswana Criticised for Killing 23 Elephants for Independence Celebrations



Botswana has authorised the killing of 23 elephants and other wildlife for meat as part of celebrations marking the country's 60th anniversary of independence, drawing criticism from animal rights and conservation groups. The Elephant Protection Society warned that using elephants for celebratory feasts could undermine conservation efforts and encourage poaching. The decision has also sparked concerns over hygiene and disease amid a foot-and-mouth outbreak. Local officials are calling for the meat to be processed and distributed more safely. Botswana has more than 130,000 elephants and defends regulated hunting as a way to manage human-wildlife conflict and generate funds for communities and conservation. The government's hunting policy remains controversial, with conservation groups questioning its sustainability while supporters point to the damage elephants do to crops, property and communities.

Somali Families Face Renewed Violence as Hunger Crisis Worsens

Children have been killed and injured in renewed fighting in Baidoa, Somalia, with a health facility also damaged, according to UNICEF and other humanitarian agencies. Clashes between government forces and fighters loyal to the former South West State president have intensified in recent weeks, adding to an already severe humanitarian crisis. About two million children across Somalia are acutely or severely malnourished, while 26,000 people in Baidoa face catastrophic food insecurity. Families are also struggling with displacement, droughts, floods and conflict. Humanitarian funding cuts have sharply reduced food assistance. The World Food Programme now reaches just over 670,000 people, compared with more than four million during previous crises.

Morocco Whistleblower Reveals Surveillance of Journalists and Activists

Amnesty International has accused Moroccan authorities of operating an extensive surveillance system targeting journalists, human rights defenders and other critical voices. In a new report, the organisation says authorities have used spyware, phone interception, tracking devices, hidden recording equipment and other technologies to monitor and intimidate critics. Evidence linked the Direction Générale de la Surveillance du Territoire to the use of Pegasus spyware. Amnesty said its investigation identified 103 Moroccan phone numbers entered into the country's Pegasus system in 2017, including those belonging to journalists, human rights defenders, lawyers and academics. Morocco has previously denied using spyware against its citizens. Amnesty is calling for an end to unlawful surveillance and for independent investigations into alleged abuses.

Malawi MPs Demand Answers Over Chilima Wreckage Discovery

Malawi's parliamentary committee investigating the 2024 plane crash that killed former Vice-President Saulos Chilima and eight others has raised concerns over conflicting records showing when the wreckage was discovered. The Malawi Defence Force logged the discovery at 10:58 am while police reportedly logged it at 9:30 am, raising questions about the search operation, possible survival opportunities and the handling of evidence. The committee plans to travel to the Northern Region to verify evidence and question police, firefighters and other witnesses involved in the search. Former MDF commander Major General Richard Chagonapanja also told the inquiry that the military continued searching overnight despite fog, poor visibility and concerns over night operations. He said the aircraft's emergency locator transmitter was not functioning because its battery had expired, making the search more difficult. The inquiry is also examining conflicting witness accounts as it works to establish a definitive timeline of the crash and recovery operation.

World.title: Namibia: Health Ministry 'Illegally' Pays Suppliers N$13m
World.content:
Auditor general Junias Kandjeke has exposed widespread financial irregularities and the unauthorised spending of over N$13 million at the health ministry through improper emergency procurement.

Kandjeke revealed this in his audit report on the Ministry of Health and Social Services' accounts for the financial year ended 31 March 2025.

The report shows that despite listing items in its annual procurement plan, the ministry bypassed standard tender processes.



"Although the ministry had outlined goods and services as part of its planned activities in the procurement plan, the audit discovered that the ministry resorted to using the emergency procurement method for acquiring various goods and services amounting to N$13 221 043.97," Kandjeke says.

"This procurement approach was used despite the goods and services not meeting the criteria or requirements for an emergency procurement method," he adds.

In addition to emergency procurement abuses, the audit exposed illegal retrospective payments made to suppliers without required approvals.

The accounting officer incurred N$377 313 during the financial year for goods and services delivered in previous financial years without proper authorisation.

"These financial payments were made without the authorisation or approval required by the act, therefore they are unauthorised," the auditor general states.

The report also highlights another case of legal non-compliance, adding that an invoice amounting to N$245 844, relating to the 2023/24 financial year, was paid during the 2024/25 financial year without obtaining the required treasury authorisation.

Furthermore, four operational subdivisions were exceeded by N$52 554, and one developmental subdivision was exceeded by N$4.4 million, resulting in unauthorised expenditure under Section 6(a)(iii) of the State Finance Act.

The auditor general flagged significant discrepancies in the ministry's financial record-keeping, including a negative miscellaneous revenue balance of N$27.6 million.

"The absence of detailled supporting schedules explaining the nature and origin of the negative balance limits transparency and increases the risk of misstatement in the financial statements," Kandjeke says.

The audit findings further reveal millions paid in fixed overtime to staff members who were on full-time study leave, without evidence that any work was performed.

Close 

The audit highlighted outstanding commitments of N$36.7 million that were not submitted for processing before year-end, understating the ministry's financial statements.

While the ministry left N$352.7 million (3.11%) of its total budget unspent, Kandjeke says this money could have been used for other national priorities.

World.title: Zimbabwe: Wicknell Chivayo and Wife, Lulu, Killed in Helicopter Crash - Report
World.content:
Cape Town — Six people died when a helicopter crashed in Marondera Rural on Wednesday evening. The government said there were no survivors.

NewZimbabwe.com reported that the dead include businessman Wicknell Chivayo and his wife, Lulu. The government has not yet named any of the victims, and said the Zimbabwe Republic Police will confirm their identities in due course.

Information Permanent Secretary Nick Mangwana said the aircraft carried one high-profile businessman, three other passengers and two pilots. He extended the government's condolences to the victims' families and friends.

Police said the helicopter went down at around 5pm. Officers were at the scene on Wednesday evening, and the force said it would release further details once they had been established.

Authorities have not said what caused the crash, and it is not yet clear where the flight originated or where it was headed.

This is a developing story and will be updated as police confirm the victims' names and the circumstances of the crash.

World.title: Nigeria: Nollywood Actor Cjay Dies
World.content:
Cjay featured in films such as "Larry Cold", "Mum Overnight", "A Day to My Wedding", "The Lies She Tell", among others.

The Nigerian entertainment industry has been thrown into mourning following the death of Nollywood actor Chijioke "Cjay" Nwokafor.

His colleague, actress Nkechi Blessing, broke the news on Instagram on Wednesday, where she shared videos of herself with the late actor.

Blessing did not reveal what caused Cjay's death but said she cancelled the release of her movie, "Egusi Ogbono," to honour him. The late actor featured in the film.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The actress initially scheduled the movie for release at 5 p.m. on Wednesday but withdrew it after a hospital confirmed Cjay's death.

Blessing said she spoke with Cjay early Wednesday morning before she received the news of his death.

"Cjay Nwoke Oma, so this is really the end? Omo we had plans. I spoke to you at 8 a.m. today and a few hours later you are no more with us.

"Omo please return if possible because I refuse to type otherwise and this is too much for me to handle," Blessing wrote.

As of press time, Cjay's family and colleagues had yet to disclose further details about his death or announce his funeral arrangements.

Cjay

Cjay began his career in 2021 and went on to feature in several films before his death.

The Anambra-born actor appeared in movies such as "Larry Cold," "Mum Overnight," and "A Day to My Wedding."

Speaking with Trybe TV on 21 September, Cjay recalled how his first experience on a film set influenced his decision to pursue acting professionally.

He said he worked on the set with filmmaker Ruth Kadiri and became inspired after watching the way the actors carried themselves.

The actor also spoke about how people perceived his personality. According to him, many people considered him arrogant, but the impression did not reflect who he really was.

Following his death, two Instagram posts Cjay shared on 23 and 12 September have drawn renewed attention from his fans and colleagues.

In one post, he wrote, "No pressure, lifestyle cost na you no know."

He wrote in another, "Life's too short to be unhappy, live every minute like it's your last. Live, love, laugh."

Brianna Coppage may have lost her teaching career, but she certainly didn't take a pay cut.

The "Double Lives of Suburban Wives" star told Fox News Digital that her adult-content business has transformed her family's finances, revealing that her most successful month brought in a staggering $550,000.

"Oh, my best month was 550,000," Brianna told Fox News Digital.

‘DOUBLE LIVES’ STAR REVEALS STAGGERING $550K MONTH AFTER LEAVING TEACHING CAREER

The figure marks a dramatic departure from her former life as an English teacher at St. Clair High School in Franklin County, Missouri. In 2023, Coppage was placed on administrative leave after her adult-content work was discovered. She later resigned from her position.

Asked whether she now makes more in a single month than she previously earned in an entire year as a teacher, Brianna didn't hesitate.

"Yes," she said.

'DOUBLE LIVES' STAR SAYS BEING KICKED OUT OF CHURCH OVER ADULT CONTENT CAREER DIDN'T SHAKE HER FAITH

And despite the controversy that followed the end of her teaching career, Brianna said she wouldn't go back even if given the opportunity.

"Never. Never," she told Fox News Digital when asked whether she would accept her teaching job back tomorrow.

"Yeah, just the lifestyle and the time and being able to just be in control of myself and in my business," she continued. "It's changed my family's life and just everything for the better."

Brianna is one of the women featured on TLC's "Double Lives of Suburban Wives," which follows six couples in the St. Louis area navigating marriage, parenthood and suburban life while maintaining careers creating adult content.

According to TLC, what began as a financial pivot for Brianna and her husband, Phillip, quickly became a lucrative business. But that success came with consequences when Brianna's online career was publicly exposed and she lost her teaching job.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Brianna told Fox News Digital that she still struggles with whether losing her career was justified.

"I think … it's a difficult concept to even wrap my mind around," she said. "So obviously like professions have a level of professionalism, but also they couldn't cite anything that I technically broke."

"So was I really doing anything wrong? I don't know," she continued. "I think it's on a basis of morality."

Brianna also pushed back on what she described as a misconception surrounding her former employment.

"There was no like morality clause, which is a lot of… there's a misconception about that, that I signed something or a clause, a morality clause," she said. "There wasn't one. So I don't know."

While losing her teaching career forced Brianna onto a different professional path, she said the financial impact of her new work has been life-changing.

"My family was able to pay off all of our debts. I paid off my student loans," she told Fox News Digital. "So I stopped putting groceries on credit cards."

"Like yeah, it just is so freeing, and I don't know, it's been life-changing."

That financial freedom is one of the central tensions explored on "Double Lives of Suburban Wives," where the women weigh the benefits of their unconventional careers against the judgment and loss of privacy that can accompany them.

For Brianna, the cost has been significant.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"I think the greatest thing it has cost me is the privacy, the lack of privacy," she told Fox News Digital.

Being thrust into the public eye has sometimes left her feeling as though people forget there's a person behind the headlines.

"And being in the public eye, it's like, I'm not a human anymore," Brianna said. "I'm not normal just like everybody else when truly I am. Like we are human beings too."

But when weighing that loss against what her new career has made possible for her family, Brianna said the benefits extend far beyond her income.

"I think the greatest thing it has afforded is just memories and time with my family that I wouldn't trade for the world," she said.

‘DOUBLE LIVES’ STAR OPENS UP ABOUT MARRIAGE ‘BETRAYAL’ AFTER ADULT-CONTENT CAREER CHANGES HER LIFE

Brianna said her own upbringing has shaped how she views the opportunities she can now provide for her children.

"Like growing up, I grew up fairly poor. And I mean family vacations and letting my kids experience things that I never would have is really priceless."

But despite the financial success and freedom Brianna says the career has given her family, she stopped short of saying she would encourage her daughter to follow the same path.

Asked how she would respond if her daughter came to her as an adult and said she wanted to pursue the same kind of work, Brianna said her first priority would be making sure she understood what she was getting into.

DREA DE MATTEO SAYS ONLYFANS BECAME ‘POLITICAL STATEMENT’ AFTER FINANCIAL STRUGGLES THREATENED HER HOME

"I want to raise, you know, my daughter to be open-minded. Don't judge other people. It's okay if people are different," Brianna told Fox News Digital.

"So if she came to me, first, I would want her to have all the correct information. Is she safe? … It's not something that I'm going to encourage," Brianna said.

Still, she said she would offer her daughter the same acceptance she wants from others.

"But also just as I want people to love me and respect me and not judge me, I would give her that same … that same love and respect."

Her success hasn't eliminated the complications that come with mixing marriage and business.

Brianna and Phillip's relationship became another major storyline on "Double Lives of Suburban Wives," with viewers watching the couple confront trust and boundary issues while simultaneously juggling life as parents and business partners.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Brianna told Fox News Digital that the demands of those overlapping roles require constant communication.

"I think that with everything we're juggling, being parents, spouses, business partners, lifestyle, content creators, there is a lot to communicate about and a lot of boundaries to establish, and no relationship is perfect," she said.

She added that she was glad viewers were seeing some of those difficulties rather than an artificially polished version of their marriage.

"I like that this is on the show honestly, because it does show that no marriage is perfect and people go through struggles," Brianna said. "But I think at the end of the day, it matters how you work through that."

When asked whether she considered Phillip's actions cheating, Brianna drew a distinction.

‘DOUBLE LIVES OF SUBURBAN WIVES’ STAR WENT FROM FOOD STAMPS TO MAKING $100K A MONTH

"It wasn't a physical act, so no," she said. "But yeah, definitely a breach of trust and a betrayal."

The couple turned to therapy as they worked through their problems.

"There's been a lot of learning and taking accountability," Brianna told Fox News Digital. "Without that, I don't know where we would stand."

"Being in therapy and working on communication boundaries and taking ownership of our mistakes has really helped," she continued.

World.title: 'the Girls' podcast debuts as co-hosts take on Lindsay Clancy case, Ms Rachel's political activism
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The debut episode of FOX News Podcasts’ "the Girls" delivered an unfiltered conversation where no subject was off-limits, as the hosts discussed the Lindsay Clancy trial, Ms. Rachel's political activism, the realities of grief and more.

Each episode features a rotating cast of women with distinctive voices and experiences spanning news, politics, sports, comedy and culture. Thursday’s premiere brought together Fox News’ Harris Faulkner, Rachel Campos-Duffy and Kat Timpf, former secretary to New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo Melissa DeRosa and former ESPN host Samantha Ponder.

The conversation got intense as Ponder weighed in on Clancy, the Massachusetts woman charged with murdering her three young children, whose trial ended in a mistrial last month.

FOX NEWS MEDIA EXPANDS PODCAST PORTFOLIO WITH NEW ORIGINAL SHOW ‘THE GIRLS’

"If I’m a mom and this has been done to my kids, I want this woman put away forever," Ponder says in a preview clip.

"You can say things were hard, [but] you still gotta be in prison."

The group also debated whether children’s entertainer Ms. Rachel is a bad influence because of her political activism, with Timpf defending her and Faulkner questioning how much parents should know about the political views of children's entertainers.

"Is Ms. Rachel bad for kids? I don't think it's that deep," Timpf said. "She just sings songs... I still listen to Michael Jackson. Where do you draw the line? I grew up listening to Nirvana. I love Kurt Cobain. I wore flannel. I've yet to shoot up heroin," she added.

Faulkner said that parents should consider the political views children may absorb from online personalities.

"When she says she wants to do away with ICE, when she says that she’s more for letting those people come across our border illegally, when she says those things — why do I know that about her?" Faulkner said.

MOMS FOR LIBERTY CO-FOUNDER WARNS PARENTS ABOUT MS RACHEL’S POLITICAL ACTIVISM, ‘NOT MR ROGERS’

The premiere also took a more personal turn when Timpf opened up about losing her father shortly before becoming pregnant with her second child.

"Not to make it weird, but I think about death pretty much all the time because my dad died," Timpf said.

Timpf said she had spoken to her father the morning he died and later learned from a doctor she had never met that he had suffered an aortic dissection after initially going to the hospital with a stomach ache.

Her father had been intensely focused on his health, which made his sudden death especially difficult for her to process.

"He was very fit. He would not drink out of a plastic water bottle," Timpf said. "When he died, he was going up north for a day of sailing."

SAM PONDER CALLS OUT THE WNBA FOR COWARDICE: 'BE COURAGEOUS. STAND FOR WOMEN'

Timpf said the loss left her questioning whether people have any real control over their health or fate. She noted that her mother also died before turning 60 and that she battled cancer during her first pregnancy.

"I almost learned the wrong lesson of like, ‘What can you do?’" she said. "Do I want to live forever? I’m scared so much to die."

The conversations capture the podcast's freewheeling nature, covering an array of topics across news, politics, sports, comedy and culture.

"the Girls'" is available on Fox News Digital, Apple, Spotify, YouTube and wherever you get your podcasts.

World.title: Sotomayor denies mom's bid to get son into elite NYC school amid racial discrimination fight
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Justice Sonia Sotomayor denied a Brooklyn mother's emergency bid to enroll her Asian American son at an elite New York City high school, alleging that a city program geared toward admitting students from economically challenged neighborhood into the school discriminates against Asian students.

The lawsuit centers on allegations by Yi Fang Chen, whose son was denied admission to Stuyvesant High School, that New York City’s revised admissions requirements intentionally discriminate against Asian students while increasing enrollment among Black and Hispanic students. Chen filed the lawsuit in April, accusing the city of violating the 14th Amendment's equal protection clause and Title VI of the Civil Rights Act.

"Delayed justice is always frustrating, but we remain confident that the courts will ultimately uphold core equal protection principles and ensure that no student, including our client’s son, is treated as less deserving of educational opportunities because of their race," Dean McGee, an attorney for the plaintiff with Pacific Legal Foundation, told Fox News Digital.

DUKE LAW'S ALLEGED RACE-BASED ADMISSIONS ACCUSED OF DEFYING SUPREME COURT RULING: DOJ

Sotomayor did not offer an explanation Monday for denying the emergency bid, which stems from a lawsuit pending in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit.

Chen's son, identified as M.P. in court documents, scored a 558 on the Specialized High School Admissions Test — a requirement for admission. He was just three points shy of being admitted for the school year, but the lawsuit argues that M.P. would have been admitted if the city had not raised the cutoff score, a change attributed to the city reserving 20% of its admissions for students deemed "economically disadvantaged." The change was part of Mayor Bill de Blasio's expansion of the Discovery program in 2018.

BERKELEY MATH PROFESSOR SOUNDS ALARM ON LIBERAL 'TEST-BLIND' POLICIES, WARNS MANY STUDENTS BADLY BEHIND

The program was limited to students who attended middle schools where at least 60% of students were considered economically disadvantaged, meaning some economically disadvantaged students could be excluded from the program if their school fell below the threshold.

No student admitted through the Discovery program this year scored higher than 495 — at least 66 points below the cutoff for students admitted based solely on the SHSAT without economic disadvantage considered.

Although nearly three-quarters of Asian American students in New York City come from low-income families, many attended middle schools that did not meet the 60% Economic Need Index threshold.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

The lawsuit points to internal communications from the New York City Department of Education and the Mayor's Office that Chen's attorneys allege show the program's intent was to increase enrollment of Black and Hispanic students at the expense of Asian students.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Yi Fang Chen’s son was denied a seat at Stuyvesant because the City turned a program meant to help economically disadvantaged students into a tool for racial engineering—one that actually excluded disadvantaged children throughout the city," Dean McGee, an attorney with Pacific Legal Foundation, said in a statement. "Equal protection means treating kids as individuals, not as demographic statistics."

Welcome to October. For those of you who may have missed it, Joe made the call to the bullpen as he takes a couple of days off to hit the golf course. I'll be on the mound covering Screencaps today and Friday. So keep my inbox full.

I'm going to start this Thursday morning edition off by celebrating the Yankees advancing to the ALDS thanks to a complete domination of the Red Sox in what was an absolute joke of a Wild Card Series.

By no means is the work done, and I'm not popping any champagne, but you want to know what's better than winning a Wild Card Series? Beating the Boston Red Sox in that series.

PAIGE SPIRANAC WELCOMES FALL GOLF BY REVISITING SUMMER FUN, ALLIE RAE GEARED UP FOR VIKINGS IN TAMPA & MEAT

You want to know what's even better than that? Sweeping them and making it about as lopsided as a series can get. That's what happened. The Red Sox scored just two runs in the two games while the Yankees hung 18 on them.

The Yankees pitching was phenomenal. The bats are alive. They're playing with a ton of confidence and not even Sonny Gray and a neck covered in sticking stuff could shut them down.

What a series, but as I said, the work isn't finished. It's onto Tampa Bay and a Rays team that I expect is going to put up much more of a fight than Boston did.

It's October now, and it's time to show up when the lights are bright.

You don't have to tell NFL sideline reporter Melanie Collins that. She doesn't hesitate when the lights are bright. She brings it each and every day, no matter what the situation is.

Wednesday was a perfect example of that. It's the middle of the week and the last day of the month of September. Eyes are on baseball, and she fires off a farewell post to the month that was and it has folks talking.

NFL WIFE FIRES BACK AT LEAGUE OVER RIDICULOUS 15K FINE, PRESIDENTS CUP HAS NO JUICE & CBS'S MELANIE COLLINS!

Collins put together a complete package. She included football. She included inspirational quotes. And she included a few selfies to round it all out.

You're not going to find a much better send off for September than that. This is how you stay one step ahead of everyone else.

Melanie Collins has done it again. Let's get to the emails (keep those coming) and get the rest of this column rolling, shall we?

Daughter Wedding

- Neil writes:

Hey SeanJo, congrats on your daughter's wedding, I gotta know, how much did you stress over your father of the bride toast? I revised mine 18 times and sent it to my sister who writes for a living, and while she may have had a constructive edit or 2 her overriding comment was, you're never getting through this without crying. Not only no tears, but it was a tight 8 minutes that killed. After reflection I realized, nobody was here for me, and that has set me free when daughter 2 gets married. Best wishes to the newlyweds, may their future be blessed!

SeanJo

Thanks for reaching out. I didn't stress about it at all. Mainly because I wasn’t asked to do it. I didn’t have to wait until the ceremony to realize that nobody was there for me. I knew that immediately.

Our focus leading up to the wedding was to get as much as we could exactly the way our daughter wanted it. That went for the planned speakers as well. There were two, and I wasn't one of them.

She might have been worried that her old man was going to say something inappropriate or embarrassing and she's probably right. I would. I did write her a note that she read the morning of her big day and that was far more impactful than any toast I would have delivered anyway.

Here's my homemade sourdough bread boule.

Party ribs again

SeanJo

You had to. I don’t see much of a choice. Ribs on sale plus time equals firing up the smoker. Nobody does it better than you do Homebrew Bill. Keep sending me your meat.

Meat

Hey Sean, greetings from North Las Vegas. Another nice weekend on the patio with football and the grill! Can’t go wrong with cheese burgers and fries. Threw a flat iron on the grill with some Roma tomatoes. Sean we appreciate you and everyone at Outkick. Continue the great work you do.

SeanJo

Thanks Bob for the support and for sending me your meat (keep it coming). It doesn’t get much better than hanging out on the patio, enjoying football, and firing up the grill.

MLB playoff and birthday meat

Hey SeanJo,

Great to see you answering the call from the bullpen for the Wild Card Round. Hopefully, you nail Thursday and Friday so you can relieve the pressure of a "must win" on Sunday. Trust your stuff...it's what got you here!

World.title: NFL rookie drops incredible cliché as he tries to help Bucs avoid 0-4 start against Packers
World.content:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers rookie Jalon Daniels will make the first start of his career on Sunday as he goes under center for an injured Baker Mayfield.

Now, before we get to that, let’s remember that the NFL world is filled with cliches. Players and coaches love saying, "We gotta take it one quarter at a time," "Each week is a season," "We’re trying to go 1-0 each week" – well, you get the picture.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Well, the former Kansas Jayhawks star dropped a new one on Wednesday as he talked to reporters ahead of the Buccaneers’ Week 4 game against the Green Bay Packers. He was asked if he was going to be able to stay calm when it’s his turn to take the field.

"Absolutely. I think that one thing I learned in college was, you can't be the thermometer, you have to be the thermostat," he said. "You have to be someone who comes in and is able to set the temperature of the room, not test the room and try to be able to blend in with it. If a team is low, I have to be able to pick it up to be able to make sure that they're even.

"If we're high, then I have to be able to be low to be able to make sure that we're even. I try to be as even-keel as possible. I think that being able to go out there and have that even-keeled feel, the team around you feels that."

Love it when a new cliché drops, especially one you can use randomly in everyday life.

But there’s another cliché to use when it comes to the Buccaneers’ Week 4 game – "must win."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

It’s usually reserved for a team that is vying for a playoff spot. However, for Tampa Bay, it’s used here to save the season. The Buccaneers face the stark reality of dropping to 0-4 and a Mount Everest-type climb to get back into contention with Mayfield out for the next three weeks at least with a dislocated right thumb.

Daniels will get a real shot to show what he’s made of against the Packers.

"For us, it's just trying to get a win," coach Todd Bowles said when asked about trying to get a win. "(Jalon Daniels) is not playing by himself. Everybody has to do their job. We've got to coach it the right way on both sides of the ball, including special teams. He's got to play and just do his job.

"We've got 21 other guys that (are) going to be out there playing with him, so he's not by himself. It's (a) nervous (feeling) but it's exciting at the same time because you get to see somebody play. No matter where you come from, your first NFL game has to come at some point, whether you're a first-round pick or whether you're a free agent. You've got to touch the field for the first time at some point, and then you've got to play. He's just got to play."

Of course, Daniels tapped Mayfield for some advice before the pivotal matchup.

"He simply put it as: you've been dreaming of this opportunity, just stay composed, play as yourself," Daniels said. "Don't try to be anybody else besides you, and go out there and just go make football plays."
