World.title: Ibiza Is Coming to Prague: A Night of DJs, Lasers and Tropical Vibes
World.content:
On April 17, 2027, OX Club in Prague will transform for one night into an Ibiza-inspired party featuring DJs, immersive visuals and tropical-themed spaces.

The Sound of Ibiza event will bring British DJ and producer Daxson, Dutch DJ and producer Laura Van Dam, Czech DJ Lucca and DJ TiGi to one stage.



The night will combine electronic music with a full immersive laser show, acrobatic performances above the dancefloor and Ibiza-inspired décor throughout the club.

There will also be a dedicated Sunset Experience for photos and social media, as well as a Chillout Zone with its own DJ programme and mentoring by Pavel Bidlo.

Daxson has performed at major festivals and clubs including Creamfields, EDC, UNTOLD and Ministry of Sound, while also creating several anthems for Transmission Festival. Laura Van Dam has appeared at Tomorrowland, Ultra, EDC, Sziget and Ushuaïa Ibiza and has built a following with her melodic techno and trance sound.

DJ Lucca, one of the country’s best-known electronic music artists, has performed alongside international names including Carl Cox and Paul van Dyk.

The event will also feature competitions for an iPhone and other prizes. An Ibiza Beach Outfit is suggested, although the dress code is optional.

With a capacity of 1,000 people, Sound of Ibiza aims to recreate the atmosphere of the famous Mediterranean party island in the centre of Prague for one night.

Tickets went on sale on October 1, with standard tickets starting at 599 CZK and VIP tickets from 1,299 CZK. Party packs are also available.

The event has no age restriction. Tickets are available through GoOut.

World.title: The Prague Post’s First Issue Goes Online 35 Years Later
World.content:
The Prague Post has launched a digital archive marking 35 years since the publication of its first issue.

October 1, 2026, marks the 35th anniversary of the newspaper’s debut.

Founded in 1991, The Prague Post was Czechoslovakia’s longest-running English-language weekly newspaper.



The newly launched archive begins with that very first issue, which is available to read in full, browse online and search by text.

A new issue will be added each week, corresponding to the same week 35 years earlier.

The project will allow readers to follow the political, social and cultural changes of the early 1990s through the newspaper’s coverage, much as readers did at the time.

The Prague Post Archive is also active on Facebook and Instagram, where updates about newly digitized issues and the project will be shared.

The archive is administered by Modrá sova z.s., a nonprofit English-language library and learning center in Loužnice, where The Prague Post’s physical archives are housed.

Issues published between 1991 and 1994 have already been scanned and processed.

Around two decades of additional issues remain to be digitized, making the project a long-term and costly undertaking. Modrá sova has independently funded the digitization work since the project began and is now inviting organizations and individuals interested in supporting the project to contribute through the archive’s website.

The archive will also continue to handle requests from people looking for specific articles and welcomes visitors by appointment.

For more information, contact Mimi Fronczak-Rogers at [email protected] or +420 721 518 385.

World.title: Halloween Trick-or-Treat for Charity to Return to Prague on October 22
World.content:
A Halloween charity event will bring children and families to several Prague neighbourhoods on October 22, combining trick-or-treating with fundraising for SOS Children’s Villages.

The Halloween Trick-or-Treat for Charity will take place from 4 p.m. to 8 p.m. across Vinohrady, Vršovice, Žižkov, Prague 15, Holešovice and Barrandov.



The concept is simple. Children dressed in Halloween costumes and accompanied by their parents will visit participating host locations, which can include cafés, restaurants, shops, confectioneries, schools, children’s centres and other businesses or organisations.

The participating locations will remain a secret until children register for the event and receive a special map showing where they can go trick-or-treating.

At each location, children will make a contribution of at least CZK 10 to a sealed collection box supporting SOS Children’s Villages. In return, they will receive a sweet treat before continuing to the next location.

Last year’s event attracted more than 1,100 registered participants and raised CZK 296,157 despite rainy weather.

The entire amount was donated to SOS Children’s Villages, which has supported children, families, young people and foster carers in the Czech Republic for more than 50 years.

How it started

Dinah Spritzer-Richter and several of her friends organized the first American Halloween in Prague for her two children in 2017. The event has supported charity from the very first year, with the proceeds going to help children in SOS Children’s Villages.

Dinah sees the charity side as just as important as creating a joyful and memorable experience for the kids.

How to take part

Families who want to participate can register in advance and then use the secret map to find the participating locations on October 22.

Children are encouraged to come in costume and bring enough coins to make contributions at the individual stops.

Businesses and organisations can also join the event as hosts. Each host is asked to prepare sweets, add some Halloween decorations and wear at least part of a costume or Halloween accessory.

Hosts must be available for at least two hours between 4 p.m. and 8 p.m.

The organisers will provide the collection boxes, while hosts provide the sweets for visiting children.

World.title: Prague Study Reveals How Much Waste Tourists Leave in the City Center
World.content:
Specialists from Prague City Hall and the Institute of Circular Economy (INCIEN) have analyzed the contents of public waste bins in central Prague, finding that about one ton of rubbish is discarded on Wenceslas Square every day.

The latest analysis was carried out to examine how the composition of waste changes with the seasons and fluctuations in tourist traffic.

A similar measurement was conducted during the winter, providing a basis for comparison.



Beverage packaging made up roughly one-third of the waste collected from bins on Wenceslas Square. Cans and plastic bottles were among the most common items.

Another third consisted of disposable food-service items, particularly cups. The remaining third was made up of general household waste.

Researchers also found waste originating from businesses in the surrounding area, including cafes and shops. Some household rubbish appeared to have been left by tourists staying in apartments rented through short-term accommodation platforms.

Food waste was another recurring part of the findings. Partially eaten food was frequently found in the bins, with trdelník pastries among the more common examples.

The summer analysis gives Prague authorities a clearer picture of the waste generated in one of the city’s busiest public spaces during the peak tourist season and allows them to compare the results with the winter survey.

World.title: Prague Hospitals Warn of Critical Blood Shortages
World.content:
Several hospitals in Prague are reporting critically low blood supplies, prompting the Czech Ministry of Health to urge people to donate blood in the coming days.

The shortage is affecting more than individual blood groups. Hospitals and transfusion centers in several parts of the Czech Republic are reporting a broader decline in available supplies, with some facilities nearing the minimum levels needed to maintain safe operations.



The situation differs from one region to another. Some transfusion centers still have adequate reserves, while others are short of particular blood groups or are approaching critical levels.

The shortage also extends to individual blood components. In Prague, the Institute for Clinical and Experimental Medicine (IKEM) is currently seeking more platelet donors regardless of blood type.

People planning to donate are advised to check the latest information on the website or social media channels of their chosen transfusion center before visiting.

Why hospitals need more donors

Hospitals depend on regular blood donations not only during emergencies but also for planned medical treatment.

Blood is routinely needed for surgery, childbirth and the treatment of patients who require repeated transfusions. This includes some cancer patients whose treatment can interfere with the body’s production of blood cells.

Blood donations are also essential in cases of severe complications during childbirth. Heavy blood loss can become life-threatening within a short period, and an adequate supply of donated blood can be critical to saving the lives of mothers and newborns.

The demand for blood can increase during the summer and holiday period, when hospitals continue to perform scheduled procedures while also dealing with more injuries and traffic accidents. At the same time, the number of people coming to donate tends to fall as residents leave the country or travel elsewhere.

Number of donors continues to decline

Official figures indicate that the Czech donor base has been shrinking. Around 348,000 people donated blood last year, down from 362,000 the previous year.

Transfusion centers are also losing older regular donors as they reach the age limit, while the number of younger people replacing them has not been sufficient.

In the Czech Republic, adults can generally donate blood until the age of 65, provided they weigh more than 50 kilograms. Additional eligibility restrictions may apply, including for people who have recently travelled to countries where certain infectious diseases are present.

Donating blood in the Czech Republic is voluntary and free of charge. Donors are entitled to time off work on the day of their donation, while some health insurance companies provide additional benefits or rewards for regular donors.

World.title: Bangkok Gears Up for the 2026 IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings
World.content:
All eyes are on Thailand as the country prepares to host the 2026 International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Group (WBG) Annual Meetings, also known as the 2026 Annual Meetings or AM2026 Thailand.

Running from 12-18 October 2026, at the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center (QSNCC) in Bangkok, the event will mark Thailand’s second time hosting the meetings, following its first in 1991. This will make Thailand one of only three nations to have hosted the IMF–WBG Annual Meetings twice.



The IMF–WBG Annual Meetings, held for two consecutive years in Washington D.C. and every third year in one of the 191 member countries, serve as a gathering of top economic figures from around the world. By covering a broad range of issues, the meetings aim to strengthen global financial stability, combat poverty, and ensure inclusive economic growth and job creation.

Thailand’s selection to host again in 2026 highlights how the country has advanced over the past three decades in terms of its institutional progress, economic resilience, and sustained engagement with international partners. As host, Thailand brings decades’ worth of experience in economic transformation and regional leadership to the table.

The “Olympics of Finance”

Often dubbed the “Olympics of Finance,” the meetings are set to attract more than 15,000 participants, including finance ministers, central bankers, economists, business leaders, civil society representatives, and journalists from the IMF and World Bank’s 191 member countries, including the Czech Republic.

The Annual Meetings will be held under the theme of “Thailand’s New Horizons: Empowering People, Building Resilience”. Therefore, the meetings will focus on enhancing people’s potential and creating opportunities, with the goal of fostering a financial and economic system that is safe, sustainable, and inclusive.

Under the theme, the government plans to showcase four policy priorities it believes are increasingly relevant in an era marked by geopolitical fragmentation, economic volatility, and demographic change. These are indeed the issues that warrant serious conversation and sincere collaboration among the global community and all stakeholders to address them in the most efficient way:

Digital Transformation : The first centers on digital transformation and artificial intelligence, using the examples from Thailand’s Digital Public Infrastructure, including PromptPay and cross-border QR payment systems.

The first centers on digital transformation and artificial intelligence, using the examples from Thailand’s Digital Public Infrastructure, including PromptPay and cross-border QR payment systems. Connected Economy : A second pillar focuses on what is called “Building Resilience in a Fragmented World”. In order to achieve this, the concept of a “Connected Economy” capable of bridging divides between competing blocs while strengthening supply chains and investment links will be explored.

A second pillar focuses on what is called “Building Resilience in a Fragmented World”. In order to achieve this, the concept of a “Connected Economy” capable of bridging divides between competing blocs while strengthening supply chains and investment links will be explored. Climate Finance : The third pillar addresses climate finance, with emphasis on reforms to help countries adapt to climate change.

The third pillar addresses climate finance, with emphasis on reforms to help countries adapt to climate change. Longevity Economy: The final priority seeks to turn the challenges of ageing populations into new sources of economic growth.

Alongside these focus areas, the Bank of Thailand plans to unveil the “Bangkok Blueprint,” an international framework developed jointly with the IMF and the World Bank aimed at combating digital financial fraud and strengthening trust in the digital economy.

Readiness in All Aspects

According to the Fiscal Policy Office, Thailand’s overall readiness has been assessed at “Grade A” following months of coordination between the Ministry of Finance, the Bank of Thailand, and the IMF–World Bank Annual Meetings Secretariat.

Preparations extend beyond the conference venue. Authorities have developed contingency plans for traffic management, emergency responses, and arrangements for high-level foreign officials. A working group has also been established to address cybersecurity matters.

Beyond Tourism: A Regional Economic Capital

Beyond its long-established reputation as a world-renowned tourist destination, the 2026 Annual Meetings offer Thailand an excellent opportunity to present another dimension of the Kingdom to the international community.

AM2026 reinforces Thailand’s standing as a trusted international partner while highlighting its growing role as a regional economic capital and a hub for finance, investment, policy innovation, and multilateral dialogue in Southeast Asia. Having said that, countries and companies vying for economic and business opportunities cannot overlook Thailand and its potential to become an important impetus for their long-term prosperity and growth.

(Source material and reporting courtesy of Thailand NOW)

World.title: British Pop Star Robbie Williams to Headline Colours of Ostrava 2027
World.content:
British pop star Robbie Williams will headline the opening day of Colours of Ostrava 2027, organisers have announced.

Williams will perform on Wednesday, July 21, at the Dolní Vítkovice industrial complex, marking his return to the Czech Republic after his recent concert at Prague’s O2 Arena.



The 2027 edition of Colours of Ostrava will run from July 21 to July 24. Williams is the first major act confirmed for the festival’s lineup.

“For me, Robbie Williams is, above all, a personality. He is someone you know, even if you aren’t necessarily a fan,” said Colours of Ostrava artistic director Filip Košťálek.

“Over more than three decades, he has managed to stay relevant, evolve and surprise audiences while remaining true to himself. And those are exactly the kind of personalities we want to bring to Colours.”

Košťálek said the festival is looking for artists with strong stories and songs who can create memorable moments for audiences.

Williams fits that profile after more than three decades at the centre of British pop. Since launching his solo career in the 1990s, following his departure from Take That, he has become one of the UK’s most successful solo artists.

His latest studio album, Britpop, was released in early 2025 after a delay. Williams had originally planned to release the record earlier but moved the date following the announcement of a new album by Taylor Swift.

The delay was also connected to Williams’ ambition to return to No. 1 on the UK album chart. The strategy paid off, with Britpop reaching the top of the chart and extending his record-setting run of No. 1 albums in the UK.

Williams has remained a major live attraction as well. His most recent Czech concert took place at Prague’s O2 Arena, where he combined songs from across his career with the humour and interaction that have become a defining part of his performances.

More artists for Colours of Ostrava 2027 are expected to be announced in the coming months.

World.title: Techno, Art and Live Performance Come Together at Strahov on October 10
World.content:
On October 10, the Prague electronic music collective EDEN will bring Rotten To The Core to Stadion Strahov for one of the collective’s largest and most ambitious events to date.

Running from 10pm until 7am, the night will bring together international and local DJs, dancers and visual artists for an event built around music, performance and visual art.



The lineup includes VLACE, SCHELLT, RiVid, 2NDRA and Mila (5), with the programme focused on techno and acid.

Among the artists, 2NDRA is a Prague-based schranz and techno producer and performer and one of the founders of EDEN Collective. RiVid, meanwhile, is a Czech-Japanese hard techno duo.

The event takes a broader approach to the club experience, combining the music programme with visual elements, art installations and live performances.

That approach comes at a time when electronic music events are becoming increasingly commercialised, while promoters and venues face rising production costs and growing regulatory pressures.

The event will take place beneath Strahov Stadium in Prague 6, continuing EDEN’s connection with unconventional venues and large-scale rave productions.

The collective previously hosted its 40-hour ALT BABYLON weekender in Prague in August, featuring dozens of local and international artists.

The event is for ages 18 and over, with tickets starting at CZK 300.

World.title: “Outrageous, betrayal”: Budapest district mayors clash with Mayor Karácsony as deal with PM Magyar hands parking revenues to capital
World.content:
Several Budapest district mayors have accused Mayor Gergely Karácsony of negotiating over their parking revenues without their involvement, as the government and the capital seek a deal to keep Budapest financially operational. A deal has now been reached, under which the capital will take over the collection of parking revenues and receive HUF 120 billion in one-off government support.

District mayors object to proposed parking revenue changes

Tensions have erupted between Budapest Mayor Gergely Karácsony and several district mayors ahead of Thursday’s meeting of the Capital Development Council (FKT), the forum for negotiations between the Hungarian government and Budapest.

The dispute centres on a proposal that would transfer parking revenues currently collected by Budapest’s districts to the capital. The measure is being discussed as part of efforts to address Budapest’s difficult financial position.

Ferencváros Mayor Krisztina Baranyi, Józsefváros Mayor András Pikó, Terézváros Mayor Tamás Soproni, Erzsébetváros Mayor Péter Niedermüller and Zugló Mayor András Rózsa held a press conference on Thursday morning to object to the proposal.

Baranyi, who is also a member of the FKT, said she would ask the council to remove the parking-related proposal from its agenda. The mayors said they had not been adequately involved in the negotiations between the capital and the government, despite the proposal directly affecting their municipalities.

Photo: MTI

“Is this what the transformation means?”

Karácsony arrived at the reopening of the renovated Madách Imre Road shortly after the mayors’ press conference, where he was confronted with questions about the parking proposal.

Zugló Mayor András Rózsa asked: “Parking?” Karácsony said there was a proposal concerning the restructuring of parking arrangements, prompting Baranyi to question whether “restructuring” was simply a euphemism for taking the revenues away from the districts.

Baranyi then asked Karácsony whether he supported the proposal. “We will discuss it,” the mayor replied.

Baranyi subsequently raised concerns about the capital taking over parking operations, referring to Budapest’s previous experience with the former Centrum parking company.

“Is this so important that you would betray the districts for HUF 10 billion?” Baranyi asked, according to Telex.

Karácsony did not immediately give a substantive response. The figure of around HUF 10 billion (EUR 27.2 million) refers to the parking-related revenue at the centre of the dispute.

Mayors threaten to suspend cooperation with Karácsony

Pikó said the districts had learned about the proposed arrangement without being properly consulted. He argued that the situation undermined the principle of local self-government, particularly because districts would lose a significant source of revenue while continuing to face their existing responsibilities.

Pikó also announced that the affected mayors would suspend their membership of the Association of Budapest Local Governments, led by Karácsony, until the dispute was resolved. He said they could consider leaving the organisation altogether if no satisfactory solution was reached.

The district mayors have also argued that they have taken on costly responsibilities from the capital in recent years to help ease its financial burden. Rózsa said parking revenues are used in Zugló for services including the operation of its public CCTV system and school prevention programmes.

Soproni, meanwhile, said Karácsony had not acted fairly by reaching an agreement with the government “over the heads” of the districts.

Karácsony and Vitézy stress the importance of cooperation

Speaking at the Madách Imre Road reopening, Karácsony thanked the district mayors for their “honesty” and said disagreements could ultimately lead to constructive results.

Transport and Investment Minister Dávid Vitézy also attended the event and stressed the importance of dialogue between the government and Budapest. According to Vitézy, the purpose of negotiations between the capital and the government is to ensure that Budapest remains operational.

The FKT was recently re-established following legislation adopted by parliament. The body is jointly led by Prime Minister Péter Magyar and Karácsony and is intended to make decisions unanimously on major Budapest development issues.

Deal reached: Budapest to take over parking revenues

The dispute took a new turn after the FKT meeting, with Karácsony announcing that Budapest and the government had reached an agreement on the capital’s finances.

Under the deal, the government will provide Budapest with a one-off HUF 120 billion in support and withdraw previous lawsuits it had filed against the capital, according to Telex. Karácsony said the funding would allow Budapest to pay its solidarity contribution, settle certain debts and, despite the difficulties, close the year without running out of money.

The agreement also includes a reduction in the solidarity contribution, although the exact amount applicable to Budapest will only become clear once an agreement has been concluded with all municipalities. In return, the capital has committed to making HUF 20 billion in operating-cost savings in 2027.

Karácsony also said the agreement would involve the creation of a regional BKK system covering Budapest and its agglomeration. Under the proposed model, the state and the capital would jointly make decisions about the operation of the transport system and would finance it on an equal basis.

The parking dispute was also settled as part of the agreement. Karácsony announced that the capital would now organise parking across Budapest and collect the resulting revenues, rather than the money remaining with the individual districts. He argued that a unified system could be operated more efficiently and said the capital would establish a Budapest road fund using the parking revenues.

Karácsony said the change was justified in part by the capital’s responsibility for Budapest’s road management, while the districts currently receive the parking revenues. He also argued that parking is operating with an unsatisfactory profitability rate and that a unified system could reduce operating costs.

The agreement was reached despite the objections raised by the district mayors earlier on Thursday. The mayors had argued that the parking revenues were essential to financing services in their districts and objected to the negotiations being conducted without their involvement. Karácsony said he remained open to discussions with the district mayors over the changes.

World.title: Former Orbán-era minister Hankó placed in pre-trial detention: prosecutors cite potential lengthy prison sentence
World.content:
A court in Kecskemét has ordered the detention of former Culture and Innovation Minister Balázs Hankó, who is being investigated over alleged misuse of state cultural funds.

Hankó brought to court in handcuffs

Balázs Hankó, a Fidesz MP and former Culture and Innovation Minister, was brought to the Kecskemét District Court in handcuffs on Thursday morning, accompanied by officers of Hungary’s National Tax and Customs Administration (NAV).

Hankó was transported from a detention facility in Cegléd to the court, where a judge was due to decide whether he should be placed in pre-trial detention.

The court ultimately ordered Hankó’s detention for one month, Marianna Bodó, spokesperson for the Bács-Kiskun County Chief Prosecutor’s Office, told Telex.

Before entering the courtroom, Hankó told reporters: “I have made a statement about everything.”

After leaving the hearing, he shouted that the prosecution had prevented him from making a statement, adding: “So much for freedom of speech.” The hearing was held behind closed doors. Hankó and his defence lawyer reportedly left and returned to the courtroom several times to review case documents before the decision was issued.

Prosecutors cite flight and interference risks

The Bács-Kiskun County Chief Prosecutor’s Office had requested Hankó’s detention on the grounds that the suspected offence carries a potentially lengthy prison sentence and that his extensive network of contacts creates a risk of flight or hiding.

Prosecutors also said there was a risk that he could unlawfully influence the proceedings, referring to what they described as an organised and hierarchical offence allegedly carried out over an extended period.

The prosecution said the aims of the detention – including ensuring the suspect’s presence and preventing interference with evidence – could not be achieved through less restrictive measures. The court’s decision on detention does not determine Hankó’s criminal responsibility. The investigation remains ongoing.

If you missed it: Orbán-era ministers arrested as National Asset Recovery and Protection Office and prosecution order detention

Another former minister detained in separate case

Hankó is the second former government minister to be placed in detention this week. Former National Development Minister Miklós Seszták, a KDNP MP, was ordered into detention for 30 days on Wednesday in a separate investigation concerning alleged bribery connected to contracts involving Volánbusz. His detention decision was appealed.

Hankó’s detention is linked to the separate NKA investigation, in which several other suspects have previously been detained. The investigation into the alleged misuse of cultural funding is continuing.

World.title: BREAKING: Russia expels Hungarian diplomats
World.content:
Moscow has ordered a group of Hungarian diplomats to leave Russia within two weeks, in response to Hungary’s expulsion of 10 Russian diplomats last month, Russian news agency TASS reported. The exact number of Hungarians affected has not yet been disclosed.

Russia announces retaliatory expulsions

Russia has announced the expulsion of Hungarian diplomats following Hungary’s decision last month to order 10 Russian diplomatic staff to leave the country.

Hungary’s chargé d’affaires in Moscow, Gábor Gergics, was summoned to the Russian Foreign Ministry on Thursday morning and informed of the measures. According to the Russian ministry, staff members of the Hungarian Embassy in Moscow and the Hungarian consulates in St Petersburg and Kazan have been ordered to leave Russia within two weeks.

The Russian announcement did not specify how many Hungarian diplomats are affected. The move comes a bit more than three weeks after Hungary announced the expulsion of the 10 Russian diplomats. Russia has described its latest action as a retaliatory measure.

Hungary says it will maintain its diplomatic presence

Hungary’s Foreign Ministry said it had taken note of the Russian decision and described it as a response to Budapest’s earlier measure.

“The Hungarian government takes note of the Russian side’s decision, which we regard as a response to the previous Hungarian measure,” the ministry said.

“Hungary is not interested in an escalation of diplomatic tensions, while maintaining its previously taken decision based on national security considerations,” it added. The ministry also stressed that Hungary’s diplomatic missions in Russia would continue operating.

“The operation of our missions in Russia remains uninterrupted, and Hungary’s diplomatic presence in Russia will be maintained,” the statement said.

The Russian Embassy in Budapest. Photo: Wikimedia Commons

Budapest expelled 10 Russian diplomats in September

On 8 September, Foreign Minister Anita Orbán announced that Hungary had ordered 10 members of Russia’s diplomatic mission to leave the country.

According to the Hungarian government, the 10 individuals had engaged in activities that, in Hungary’s assessment, were unacceptable for diplomats under the Vienna Convention. The government did not officially describe the activities as espionage.

The decision represented an unusually large-scale expulsion of Russian diplomats by Hungary. It followed a quieter expulsion of a Russian diplomat in May, according to a previous report by VSquare.

Russia signalled at the time that it would respond. Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said the response would be “tough and painful”, while Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov later said Moscow would give an “appropriate response”.

The Russian Foreign Ministry has now carried out that retaliatory measure.

Exact number of Hungarian diplomats remains unclear

For the time being, neither the Russian announcement nor the Hungarian Foreign Ministry’s statement has specified the exact number of Hungarian diplomats who have been ordered to leave. The Russian measure affects personnel at Hungary’s embassy in Moscow and its consulates in St Petersburg and Kazan.

Hungary has said that its diplomatic presence in Russia will remain in place despite the expulsions, meaning the latest move does not amount to a severing of diplomatic relations between the two countries.

World.title: Budapest’s Grand Boulevard set for major green makeover – VISUALS
World.content:
Detailed plans have been completed for the renewal of the tree-lined Grand Boulevard, with new trees, rainwater-management solutions and other green infrastructure planned along the route.

No trees to be removed for construction

The Budapest Transport Centre (BKK) has completed permit-level plans for the renewal of the tree-lined sections of the Grand Boulevard, one of Budapest’s best-known urban thoroughfares. The plans cover the section between Nyugati Square and Boráros Square, where around 600 trees currently stand. According to the plans, none of these trees will be removed for construction purposes.

Where trees do have to be replaced because of their condition, however, the city plans to plant at least three new trees for every tree that cannot be saved.

“The aim is to make the existing tree lines healthier in the long term,” said Sándor Bardóczi, Budapest’s chief landscape architect.

“We will not cut down a single tree on the Grand Boulevard for construction reasons, and for every tree that cannot be saved, we will plant at least three. One in its original location and the others elsewhere along the boulevard. We will also create new tree lines in places where there are no trees at all today,” he said.

Photo: BKK

Fewer tree replacements thanks to targeted interventions

According to BKK, the design process has focused on keeping tree replacements to a minimum. Several dozen trees will receive targeted interventions intended to extend their lifespan, allowing trees that are still valuable and attractive to remain in place.

As a result, replacements will only be carried out where they are unavoidable because of the condition of a tree, and the number of trees requiring replacement is expected to remain below 10 per cent of the existing stock.

The species selected for the renewed and new tree lines have also been chosen with both the existing appearance of the boulevard and climate change in mind. Where trees are being replaced within existing rows, visual consistency is an important consideration. For new tree lines, including those planned on Ferenc Boulevard, species better suited to changing climate conditions will have a greater role.

Photo: BKK

Don’t miss this: Green light for 280 new Budapest homes as huge development acquires permits

New green infrastructure and rainwater management

The plans go beyond replacing trees. Budapest also intends to expand green areas along several sections of the Grand Boulevard. The city plans to introduce modern rainwater-management solutions and green infrastructure based on “sponge city” principles. These are intended to help create better conditions for trees and other vegetation to develop over the long term.

The goal is to increase the number of trees along the boulevard while also giving existing tree lines better conditions in which to survive and grow.

Photo: BKK

Residents can inspect the plans in October

BKK says it considers local involvement an important part of the Grand Boulevard project. Previous public consultations attracted the views of thousands of Budapest residents. Four public walks will now be held in October, giving residents and other interested people the opportunity to examine the plans on site.

Tree assessment specialists will explain the current condition of the trees, why certain trees need to be replaced and where new trees and tree lines could be created. The planned dates are:

7 October, 5 PM – Angyal István Park, District 9

– Angyal István Park, District 9 8 October, 5 PM – corner of Corvin köz and József Boulevard, District 8

– corner of Corvin köz and József Boulevard, District 8 13 October, 5 PM – in front of 53 Erzsébet Boulevard, District 7

– in front of 53 Erzsébet Boulevard, District 7 14 October, 5 PM – Nyugati Square, in front of the fountain, District 6

The public walks will also provide an opportunity to learn more about the tree species selected for the project and the criteria used to determine which existing trees can be preserved or need to be replaced.

World.title: Budapest to host 32nd Canadian Lobster Dinner – Registration deadline approaches!
World.content:
The Canadian Chamber of Commerce in Hungary will host its 32nd Annual Lobster Dinner, bringing together members of the Hungarian and international business community for an evening centred around Canadian cuisine, entertainment and networking.

The event will feature Nova Scotia lobster, unlimited drinks, live music and entertainment, as well as various exhibitors, a silent auction and raffle prizes. A dedicated shuttle service will also be available to guests, provided by Renault.

The Lobster Dinner has become a regular event in the Canadian Chamber’s annual programme, offering members, business partners and guests an opportunity to meet in a more informal setting while enjoying an evening built around Canadian hospitality.

For those planning to attend, 5 October is an important date: it is the last day to register at the current participation rates. Registration itself will remain open until 27 October.

Photo: Canadian Chamber of Commerce in Hungary

World.title: Orbán’s brother allegedly asked Austrian contact if he could stop another Ukrainian cash shipment
World.content:
A newly published 444.hu investigation says Áron Orbán contacted a former political acquaintance in Graz just weeks before Hungary’s 2026 election, asking whether an incoming Ukrainian shipment could be “caught” in Austria.

Áron Orbán, the younger brother of former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, allegedly contacted a Hungarian businessman living in Graz on 26 March, according to an investigation by Hungarian news outlet 444.hu.

The two men had not spoken for several years. The businessman, Csongor Lászlóvári-Thoma, had previously been involved in Austrian politics and had appeared on the ÖVP’s list in a 2021 Graz municipal election, although he did not win a seat.

According to messages obtained by 444.hu, Orbán first asked how much influence his former acquaintance had in Austria before referring to a shipment travelling through the country. He then asked whether they could “catch” it.

The businessman understood the reference as concerning a cash shipment and asked for clarification. Orbán reportedly said it was a new shipment, rather than the one already intercepted in Hungary earlier that month.

The background: Hungary’s “gold convoy” affair

On 5 March, Hungarian authorities stopped two vehicles carrying around HUF 27 billion (EUR 75 million) worth of cash and gold while travelling from Vienna through Hungary towards Ukraine. Seven Ukrainian citizens accompanying the shipment were detained and later expelled from Hungary. The authorities initially cited suspicion of money laundering.

The shipment was subsequently returned to the Ukrainian bank that owned the assets, while the investigation into the money carriers was closed by Hungary’s tax and customs authority for lack of evidence of a crime.

The case has since developed into a larger investigation into the circumstances of the operation. Former TEK chief János Hajdu was questioned as a suspect over the alleged unlawful detention of the Ukrainian money carriers.

What happened after the messages?

According to 444.hu, Lászlóvári-Thoma did not agree to help. He reportedly told Orbán that Austrian authorities could only intervene if there were grounds for suspicion and advised him to make a formal report if he had evidence of wrongdoing.

The businessman later showed the messages to the lawyer representing the Ukrainian money carriers and said he also alerted Austrian intelligence services and the Austrian People’s Party, citing concerns that someone might otherwise act on the request.

444.hu says it verified that the phone number used to send the messages belonged to Áron Orbán. The outlet also contacted Orbán for comment but had received no response by publication time.

World.title: Could this be the end of night flights at Budapest Airport? Residents demand stricter limits
World.content:
Hungary’s Transport and Investment Ministry has set up a working group to examine night-time flights at Budapest Airport, after hundreds of aircraft movements were recorded during the legally restricted deep-sleep period.

Hundreds of flights recorded after midnight at Budapest Airport

Under Hungary’s current rules, no more than six commercial aircraft movements may be scheduled at Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport between midnight and 5 AM, the period designated as the “deep-sleep” hours. Exceptions can be authorised by the aviation authority in specific circumstances.

However, data published by HungaroControl show that the limit was exceeded frequently in the first quarter of 2026. A total of 829 aircraft movements were recorded during the five-hour period, averaging 9.2 take-offs or landings per night.

The figures also show that 65 of the 90 nights in the quarter saw more than six aircraft movements. On the busiest night, 6 January, as many as 30 aircraft took off or landed between midnight and 5 AM.

Weather conditions and delays caused by air-traffic congestion can partly explain the higher numbers, but the scale of the figures has renewed concerns about noise affecting communities around the airport.

The areas most affected include Budapest’s 10th, 14th, 17th and 18th districts, as well as parts of Vecsés and Üllő.

Don’t miss this: Wizz Air rethink could reshape ticket prices and routes across Europe

Ministry working with airport and airlines

The issue was discussed in late August when Transport and Investment Minister Dávid Vitézy held talks with Wizz Air CEO József Váradi. The ministry has since established a working group involving Budapest Airport, HungaroControl and Wizz Air to examine the situation.

József Váradi and Dávid Vitézy held talks in August 2026. Photo: Facebook/Vitézy Dávid

According to the ministry, the group is reviewing current conditions, operational experience and available data before deciding what measures may be necessary.

“Within the framework of the working group, we are examining what steps need to be taken to ensure, to the greatest possible extent, that residents living in the area can enjoy peaceful rest during the deep-sleep period,” the ministry told 24.hu.

The government body has not announced a decision to introduce a complete night-flight ban.

Local authorities call for tougher restrictions

Several affected municipalities, however, are pushing for much stricter measures. Local authorities argue that the only effective solution would be a complete and strict ban on night-time traffic during the deep-sleep period. They also want representatives of the affected districts and settlements to join the ministry’s working group so they can directly represent local residents.

András Rózsa, the mayor of Zugló, has also called for compensation for the district because of the additional noise burden. For now, the ministry’s working group is analysing the available data and operational practices. Its review could determine whether Hungary’s existing restrictions on night flights at Budapest Airport need to be tightened.

World.title: Hungary’s first smart supermarket opens: say goodbye to closing time
World.content:
Hungary’s smart retail revolution has reached supermarket scale, with Szeged opening what is being presented as the country’s first staffless supermarket. The new Coop Szeged store on Temesvári Boulevard operates as a conventional shop during staffed hours before switching to an automated mode, allowing registered customers to shop without cashiers or sales assistants.

A supermarket that stays open

The 470-square-metre store stocks more than 6,000 products, meaning customers can do a full grocery shop rather than simply pick up a handful of items from vending machines. Outside normal opening hours, customers registered with the 247 Shop app can enter using a QR code. They select their goods from the shelves and pay by bank card at a self-service checkout, writes 24.hu.

To leave, they scan a code displayed on their receipt or available in the app. A remote dispatcher is available if customers need assistance. The system combines traditional retail with technology rather than eliminating staffed shopping altogether. During regular opening hours, the store operates normally, while the automated system extends its availability into the evening and overnight.

Living, working or doing business in Hungary?

Make things easier with professional support in English. Explore Daily News Hungary’s Services in English and find the help you need.

AI keeps watch

Although no employees are physically present during the automated period, the supermarket is not left completely unattended. Its camera surveillance system is supported by artificial intelligence, which can detect and flag suspicious incidents. A remote dispatcher monitors the store and can intervene when necessary or assist customers.

Coop Szeged chief executive János Kelemen said the company’s first hybrid smart shop, which opened at Szeged’s Szent István Square in May 2025, had provided encouraging results. During its first year, the smaller 150-square-metre shop recorded more than 27,000 purchases during staffless periods. The average basket value was around 22% higher than during conventional opening hours, while 24-hour operation generated 23.61% additional revenue, according to the company.

In case you missed it: Can farming survive Hungary’s growing drought crisis? New documentary reveals the stakes

Could the model spread?

Coop Szeged studied similar hybrid shops in the Czech Republic before introducing the concept. Kelemen said the experience had shown that customers were willing to change their shopping habits, with some deliberately choosing staffless hours.

The model could also have applications beyond larger cities. Kelemen suggested that smaller settlements could benefit from shops operating with limited staffing, particularly where maintaining a conventional grocery store is difficult. Such a system could allow residents to shop locally rather than travelling 20 or 30 kilometres to the nearest supermarket.

Kelemen does not expect every Hungarian shop to become staffless within a few years. However, the company hopes the hybrid model will spread beyond Szeged and eventually become a more familiar feature of Hungarian retail.

World.title: Bosnian Serb Wartime Leader Biljana Plavsic Dies Aged 96
World.content:
Biljana Plavsic at the war crimes tribunal in The Hague, January 2000. Photo: EPA PHOTO/POOL REUTERS/JERRY LAMPEN.

Biljana Plavsic, a senior wartime leader of the Bosnian Serbs, died on Thursday aged 96 in Belgrade, where she had been living since release from prison, the public broadcaster of Bosnia’s Serb-led entity, Republika Srpska, RTRS, reported.

As vice-president of the Serb-led Republika Srpska entity during the 1992-5 war, she was sentenced to 11 years in prison in on February 2003 by the UN tribunal in The Hague after pleading guilty to the persecution of Bosniaks, Croats and other non-Serbs.

In June 2003, she was transferred from The Hague to Sweden to serve her sentence and she released in October 2009, having served two-thirds of her sentence.

She then returned to Belgrade, where she lived a reclusive life and was not politically active. She was divorced and had no children, RTRS wrote in its report on her death.

Plavsic was born in 1930 in the Bosnian town of Tuzla. She was the only woman to be indicted and convicted of wartime crimes by the International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia, ICTY, in The Hague.

But she later told Swedish magazine Vi that she only admitted guilt to get the other charges against her dropped, and had “done nothing wrong”.

She told BIRN in 2019 that she could not remember expressing remorse in court for causing suffering during the war. “I try to forget that period,” she said.

A former biology lecturer, Plavsic became the Serb member of Bosnia’s tripartite presidency from November 1990 until December 1992. She was later one of the vice-presidents of the newly-founded Republika Srpska, under Radovan Karadzic.

After the war, in 1996, she became Republika Srpska’s second president, a position she held until November 1998.

The Hague prosecution charged her alongside Momcilo Krajisnik, Republika Srpska’s speaker from 1991 to 1996. Krajisnik was found guilty of deportation and forced displacement; he died in September 2020 due to the consequences of COVID-19.

Since her release from prison, though not active in public life, Plavsic sometimes gave interviews to nationalist, pro-government, pro-Russian or far-right media.

World.title: With Jansa’s Return, Slovenia’s Media Landscape Is Being Reshaped
World.content:
Chokehold could tighten even without Orban

Milosavljevic says it would only be “a wild guess what could happen next”. He points to other important actors on the Slovenian and wider regional market, which recently included United Group deals with the Czech investment group PPF, resulting in the pushing down of N1 and Nova S outlets in the Serbian cable line-ups after PPF sold these to state-owned Telekom Srbija.

Moreover, in 2024, the United Arab Emirates technology and investment group e& acquired a controlling stake in PPF’s telecom assets in Bulgaria, Hungary, Serbia and Slovakia, paving the way for the UAE’s historic entry into EU and EU candidate markets. With his close ties to the UAE, there is speculation that Vucic himself could be “behind the UAE links”.

PPF also received negative publicity for scaling down critical news reporting on Markiza, the largest commercial TV channel in Slovakia, shortly after the populist Robert Fico rebranded himself as a pro-Kremlin nationalist and Orban ally, and then made an improbable return to power in 2023.

“PPF Group might be interested in taking over Telemach, one of Slovenia’s four internet providers,” Ribac says, repeating speculation reported in the Slovenian media in September. At the same time, he says, the group “might be ready to relinquish its ownership of production company Pro Plus in exchange for control of Telemach.”

One of the richest Slovenes, Dari Juzna, is reported to be interested in buying Pro Plus, the largest media house in Slovenia. Pro Plus is part of Central European Media Enterprises, which PPF acquired in 2020 from Time Warner. At the time, the IPI and other press associations raised concerns with PPF’s owner, the late Petr Kellner, regarding media ownership and editorial independence.

“A group of wealthy individuals close to current Prime Minister Jansa might conversely be interested in taking over Pro Plus, as it produces the most popular commercial television channel POPTV and the most visited news website in the country 24.com,” Ribac explains.

This fits with Jansa’s desire to keep a primary focus on Slovenia while maintaining ties with like-minded politicians and businessmen abroad. “Jansa alone has no designs to influence Croatia or other countries near abroad,” Pengov Bitenc tells BIRN, but adds that even if Jansa’s main focus remains domestic, it won’t stop him continuing to make use of the existing network of nationalist leaders abroad to boost his credibility.

Jansa is “now indebted to Netanyahu”, Pengov Bitenc tells BIRN, referring to the involvement of the Israeli Mossad-linked company Black Cube in Slovenia’s election campaign. He argues that Jansa is much more likely to return favours to the sitting Israeli prime minister than to Orban, “who is out of power and the money flows have been turned off”.

Indeed, Israeli Minister of Foreign Affairs Gideon Saar visited Slovenia in September, when he opened Israel’s permanent embassy in Ljubljana and heralded the country’s shift from being one of the most outspoken critics of Israel’s campaign in Gaza and violence against Palestinians in the West Bank to one of its staunchest backers.

World.title: Pro-Russian Voters May Hold Key in Bulgaria’s Presidential Election
World.content:
On October 25, Bulgarians will vote for a new president in an election that highlights old-school East-West divisions in the country.

The election will likely produce a second round run-off between current acting President Iliana Iotova, the frontrunner, who is supported by President Rumen Radev’s ruling Progressive Bulgaria, the pro-Kremlin Bulgarian Socialist Party and the smaller nationalist far-right party VMRO-BND.

On the other geopolitical side of the race is former interim prime minister Andrey Gyurov - a pro-EU, Western-oriented candidate supported by the centre-right opposition parties We Continue the Change and Democratic Bulgaria.

Apart from Gyurov and one other candidate, former agriculture minister Ivan Hristanov, almost all the contenders are fronting Eurosceptic, nationalist campaigns, which often border on Russia-sympathetic sentiment.

Experts say voters who support such stances might back various rivals to Iotova in the initial round, but switch to her if she faces a pro-EU candidate like Gyurov in the second round, in early November.

World.title: Bosnian Parties’ Election Gender Quotas Mask Failure to Empower Women
World.content:
On paper, Bosnia and Herzegovina boasts some of the most progressive gender representation mandates in the Western Balkans. Ahead of the current election, political parties have met the state’s legal requirement: that at least 40 per cent of candidates on their electoral lists belong to the less represented gender. Officially, women make up 42.2 per cent of all political hopefuls across the country.

But beneath this formal display of civilizational progress lies a bleaker administrative reality. Recent metrics released by the United Nations in Bosnia and Herzegovina through its ongoing "Izvan Fokusa" (Out of Focus) monitoring campaign show women head just 15.5 per cent of all electoral lists. This is significant, as candidates topping lists are more likely to get elected than those lower down. Crucially, the share of female-led lists has plummeted by 6.1 percentage points compared to the 2022 general elections.

World.title: Romania’s Crisis Spirals as Parliament Rejects PM-Designate’s Govt
World.content:
Romania’s parliament on Wednesday rejected the programme and proposed cabinet of Siegfried Muresan, a Member of the European Parliament, adding to the country’s political crisis.

The Prime Minister-designate needed 233 votes for his government to be approved. He received only 182.

“The parties that triggered the political crisis have voted to prolong it … We are now waiting to see what position the President … will take,” Muresan said after the result was announced.

His proposed cabinet was backed by the centre-right National Liberals, PNL, and two smaller former coalition partners, but the Social Democrats, PSD, the biggest party in parliament, rejected it.

The far-right Alliance for the Union of Romanians, AUR, the second-largest party in parliament, also declined to endorse Mureșan. Party leader George Simion said the AUR would not vote for any government until the far-right politician Calin Georgescu “is freed from prison”.

A court on Tuesday ordered 30 days’ detention for former presidential candidate Georgescu, who is accused of defrauding a businessman of more than 1 million euros.

President Nicusor Dan must now nominate another Prime Minister-designate, who will have ten days to put together a cabinet and seek parliament’s approval.

Under the law, the President may dissolve parliament and call an early election if two prime ministers-designate fail to secure parliamentary backing within 60 days. However, Dan has ruled out an early election, arguing that it would likely fail to produce a strong parliamentary majority.

Since May 5, Romania has been operating under an interim government, following the collapse of the previous cabinet. During this period, Dan has made two previous nominations for prime minister, both of whom failed to secure parliamentary support.

In June, independent Eugen Tomac, the first of them, withdrew before even facing a parliamentary vote. Three weeks later, parliament rejected the proposed programme and cabinet of liberal politician Adrian Vestea.

Romania’s political crisis stems from deep tensions among the parties that previously formed the pro-European governing coalition.

The coalition, formed in June 2025, brought together the centre-left PSD, the centre-right National Liberal Party, PNL, and two smaller centre-right parties. One of its main objectives was to curb the rise of the far-right AUR.

Its mandate included stabilising the economy, which is burdened by the largest budget deficit in the European Union, securing access to 11 billion euros in EU recovery funds and safeguarding Romania’s investment-grade credit rating.

But unpopular austerity measures introduced to cut the budget deficit placed growing strain on the coalition, particularly with the Social Democrats, who withdrew support in May.

World.title: In Serbia, ‘Fictitious’ Corruption Campaign Becomes Tool of Distraction
World.content:
Over the same period, Serbia has slid 11 places on Transparency International’s annual Corruption Perception Index, published in February. It now stands in 116th place out of 182 countries, the worst ranking of any country in the Western Balkans.

Last year, Transparency Serbia published a report showing that for the first time since the fall of Serbian strongman Slobodan Milosevic in October 2000, the Serbian public considers corruption the biggest issue in the country.

“Vucic came to power in 2012 on, among other things, a campaign of ‘zero tolerance for corruption’,” said Draskovic. “That zero tolerance has turned into absolute tolerance of corruption.”

Nemanja Nenadic, programme director of Transparency, questioned the very notion of an ‘anti-corruption campaign’, given fighting corruption is the day-to-day remit of special corruption departments within the public prosecution service.

“Based on what has been announced, it can be concluded that a large number of arrests presented as part of this campaign essentially have nothing to do with corruption, but with other criminal offences,” Nenadic told BIRN.

“For example, cases in which owners of private companies engage in schemes to avoid paying taxes, not in collusion with tax officials, but with other private business owners.”

“In 2025, the number of reported corruption cases and indictments did increase compared with the previous year. For four major criminal offences, the number of indictments was 52 per cent higher than a year earlier, but there were only nine per cent more first-instance judgments.”

Arrests are the least important indicators of success, Nenadic said.

“More important indicators include how quickly reports submitted by citizens are examined, which can encourage more people to report cases; the amount of benefit obtained through corruption offences or the level of damage caused to public property or the public interest; the number and seniority of those indicted; the speed of court decisions; and, finally, the value of unlawfully obtained assets that are confiscated.”

Draskovic said that long-running proceedings without final judgments risk weakening public confidence.

“It sends a signal that it is not worth fighting corruption,” he told BIRN.

World.title: Three Kosovo Serbs Plead Not Guilty Over 2022 Unrest in North
World.content:
Barricades set up by Kosovo Serbs on a road in Rudare leading to the Jarinje border crossing with Serbia, December 2022. Photo: Adelina Ahmeti/BIRN.

Three Kosovo Serbs, Dusan Maksimovic, Nemanja Jolovic and Srdjan Vucinic, pleaded not guilty at the Pristina Basic Court on Wednesday to violating the constitutional order by participating in setting up roadblocks in the north of the country in December 2022.

A fourth defendant, Nenad Orlovic, was not present in court. Judge Rrahman Beqiri said that “every effort has been made to secure his presence in the criminal proceedings but it appears that he is not in Kosovo”.

The charges relate to unrest in December 2022, when Serbs in northern Kosovo set up barricades at the two border crossings with Serbia, parking trucks, ambulances, diggers and other vehicles across access roads in what was cast as a spontaneous outpouring of popular anger after the arrest of a Kosovo Serb on suspicion of attacking election facilities.

Two Kosovo Serbs have already been convicted over the case. Dusan Dobrac and Milos Radosavlevic were given prison sentences of one year and nine months respectively on August 31, 2026, after pleading guilty to charges.

Dobrac was convicted of acts breaching the constitutional order and obstruction of an official in the performance of their duties, and Radosavlevic of violating the constitutional order.

The indictment charged six people – Maksimovic, Drobac, Radosavljevic, Jolovic, Orlovic and Vucinic – with staging violent activity to subvert the constitutional order by blocking roads to two border crossings with Serbia: Jarinje and Bernjak.

The prosecution file, seen by BIRN, claims the unrest endangered the lives of police and customs officers. Those involved also allegedly participated in creating “a tense security situation through the opening of fortified positions and the presence of uniformed and armed persons”, according to the prosecution.

The police discovered a Viber group named “Barricades December 2022” on Maksimovic’s phone, suggesting the incidents were organised and coordinated.

They obtained the phone in September 2023 after Maksimovic was arrested over the armed attack on police in the northern village of Banjska, in which one Kosovo Albanian police officer was killed and a cache of military-grade weaponry was seized. He was sentenced in the first instance to 30 years in prison over the Banjska incident.

The contents of his phone helped prosecutors investigating the unrest in Serb-majority municipalities and the setting up of the barricades of December 2022. The messages it contained included: “Today we’ll all receive ammunition” and, “In the afternoon we could try the weapons in Suvi Dol [local village] with two or three bullets each.”

Prosecutors said the phone evidence undermined claims that local Serbs spontaneously set up the barricades.

World.title: Dani Olmo Donates Two Percent of His Salary to Vukovar
World.content:
Dani Olmo has never hidden how much his time in Croatia meant to him, and now another detail has come to light, showing how attached he remains to the country where he took his first big steps in football.

Well-known Croatian agent Andy Bara, the man who brought Olmo from Barcelona to Dinamo, spoke about the Spanish international and his character. Especially striking is the story of Vukovar, a city that left a powerful impression on Olmo when he was a teenager playing for the Zagreb club.

Olmo donates 2 percent of his gross salary to Vukovar.

“Dani Olmo is extremely attached to Zagreb and Croatia. I’ll tell you something the public didn’t know until now, and I just hope Dani won’t hold it against me. Since leaving Dinamo, at every club he has played for, Olmo has donated two percent of his annual gross salary to Vukovar. Given that he earns serious money, these are large sums,” Andy Bara told Podcast Inkubator, adding:

“He did it while playing for RB Leipzig, and he still does it today at Barcelona, and he has never wanted to talk about it publicly. His big wish is to finish his career at Dinamo, and he hopes it will come true.”

Olmo arrived in Zagreb in 2014 as a 16-year-old from Barcelona’s La Masia, and a trip to a tournament in Vukovar was one of the key moments at the start of his Croatian story. After that tournament, he was promoted to Dinamo’s senior squad.

He later spoke about his Vukovar experience on several occasions. He explained that he talked with people who had lived through the war, began learning more about what had happened in Croatia, and felt a need to help, in some way, the people who still feel the consequences of the war today.

Olmo left Dinamo for RB Leipzig in early 2020 and returned to Barcelona four years later. He clearly never forgot Croatia, Dinamo, or Vukovar.

World.title: Global Event Industry Comes to Hvar: RSVP Symposium Croatia 2026.
World.content:
October 1, 2026 – The global event industry is coming to Hvar with RSVP Symposium Croatia 2026.

From October 5 to 8, Hvar will host leading professionals from the worlds of luxury events, destination weddings, creative design, and event production. The RSVP Symposium is being held with Sunčani Hvar Hotels acting as host and co-producer, supported by the Hvar Town Tourist Board and the Split-Dalmatia County Tourist Board.

From October 5 to 8, 2026, Hvar will become a meeting point for leading professionals in the global event industry. RSVP Symposium Croatia—part of the international RSVP community dedicated to the luxury events sector—brings together event organizers, wedding planners, designers, creatives, producers, and other professionals shaping the industry’s future.

This year’s edition is held under the theme “The Power of K(no)w,” a play on words combining the power of knowledge with the equally important ability to recognize when to say “no.” Two days of educational programming will feature discussions on knowledge, decision-making, professional relationships, and contemporary industry challenges, with a focus on exchanging experiences and networking among participants.

RSVP Symposium Hvar 2026 is being realized with Sunčani Hvar Hotels as the host and co-producer, supported by the Hvar Town Tourist Board and the Split-Dalmatia County Tourist Board, and in partnership with the Croatian planning team AMAVERA Collective. The collaboration between the hotel sector, destination tourism boards, and specialized partners shares a clear objective: to showcase Hvar and Central Dalmatia to an audience directly involved in selecting venues for international weddings, luxury private events, incentive programs, conferences, and corporate gatherings.

Joining Sunčani Hvar Hotels and AMAVERA Collective for this year’s edition are MihociStudios (photography and video production), The Bombay Lettering Company (stationery), Julie and Lisa—along with Camilla from CJC Hair & Makeup—(beauty services), The Collective (entertainment), Altera (rentals, furniture, linens, and tents), and Xcape (yacht experiences). This blend of international and local creatives, producers, and destination partners further demonstrates Hvar’s capacity to host complex events requiring high production values ​​and creative excellence.

The program is designed to ensure that Hvar is not merely a venue, but an integral part of the experience. Educational sessions will take place at the historic Hvar Theatre, while the social program will feature the Adriana, Palace Elisabeth, and Beach Club Hvar, as well as a maritime excursion. Local heritage and the island’s identity are woven into the concept of each evening—ranging from the atmosphere of a Dalmatian island to Hvar’s agave lace, which serves as the inspiration for the gala dinner at Palace Elisabeth.

The arrival of the RSVP Symposium is particularly significant for further positioning Hvar as a premium, year-round destination. The luxury events and MICE tourism segment naturally builds upon Hvar’s established international image—featuring high-quality hotel offerings, authentic cultural heritage, gastronomy, the sea, and a range of attractive locations within a compact area—while simultaneously creating opportunities for tourism activity outside the peak summer months. 1.

2. Statement from the Hvar Town Tourist Board

“Hvar may not be the largest destination in the MICE and premium events sector, but we see this as our very advantage. We boast unique locations, a strong city identity, and high-quality hotel and creative partners.

It is particularly valuable for the destination that, on this occasion, Hvar will be experienced not only by guests but also by professionals whose business decisions could lead to new events and visitor arrivals in the years to come.

We also value the fact that events like this involve local hoteliers, restaurateurs, transport providers, and production and creative event services, ensuring their impact remains within the local community.

The RSVP Symposium is an opportunity to showcase Hvar to the people who directly select and recommend destinations for international business and premium events. It is also a chance to highlight what makes the town and island of Hvar so special—where the location is not merely a backdrop but an integral part of the experience, lending the event something unique through its spaces, people, rhythm, and character—qualities that cannot be replicated elsewhere.

RSVP Symposium Croatia takes place in Hvar from October 5 to 8, 2026.

World.title: Zagreb Mayor Tomislav Tomašević: We Won’t Pay Workers for Their Strike
World.content:
October the 1st, 2026 – Zagreb Mayor Tomislav Tomašević has stated that the workers who went on strike from both ZET and Zagreb Holding won’t be paid.

After three days, the strike by ZET and Zagreb Holding workers has ended. Trams and buses are running again, and Čistoća has resumed regular waste collection. The County Court in Zagreb today declared the strikes at ZET and Holding illegal and ordered them to stop.

The unions then suspended the strike and announced they would appeal the rulings. Index reports that ZET has announced that from today onwards, all tram and bus traffic will again run according to the regular timetable.

what you need to know…

Mayor Tomislav Tomašević has stated that none of the workers who went on strike will be paid for the time they spent striking. A ZET union lawyer has stated that he received two drastically different rulings. Municipal workers and ZET workers have now formally ended the strike after the court banned the ZET workers’ strike and the municipal workers’ strike.

After three days, the strike of ZET and Zagreb Holding workers has ended. Trams and buses are running again, and Čistoća has continued regular waste collection. The County Court in Zagreb today declared the strikes at ZET and Holding illegal and ordered their termination. The unions then suspended the strike and announced appeals against the rulings. Mayor Tomislav Tomašević stated that workers will not be paid for the days spent on strike. ZET published that from tomorrow all tram and bus traffic will again operate according to the regular schedule.

The strike had caused significant disruption in Zagreb for three days, with no trams, buses or regular waste collection.

World.title: Butković: We’re Signing Largest Contract in History of Croatian Railways
World.content:
October the 1st, 2026 – Transport Minister Oleg Butković has stated that today the signing of the largest contract in the history of Croatian Railways will be signed.

Minister of Maritime Affairs, Transport and Infrastructure Oleg Butković announced the signing of a contract for the reconstruction and upgrading of the Dugo Selo – Novska railway line, worth almost 900 million euros. Index reports that this is the largest contract in the history of Croatian Railways.

The Dugo Selo – Novska line is part of one of the main corridors that runs through Croatia towards the east of the country. “This is truly the largest contract in the history of Croatian Railways – almost 900 million euros for 83 kilometres of track reconstruction and the construction of a second track. We’ve been working on this project for a long time, preparing it, a public tender was carried out and now the procedures are complete,” said Butković.

first cooperation with an indian company

After the realisation of this project, he added, the Okučani – Vinkovci section will still remain. “Then we will have a fully reconstructed and built railway line from the Slovenian border, because Savski Marof – Zagreb has been reconstructed, that is, from Zagreb to the border with Serbia,” the minister said. Butković confirmed that this is the first time a company from India has won a job in such a tender. “As far as we have inquired and according to the documentation they submitted, they have very good references. They have worked on one of the largest projects in India and the world, so I believe everything will be as it should,” he said.

The minister is aware that large projects also bring challenges. “Some things today you cannot predict and you cannot influence them. I hope there will be as few of them as possible,” he said. The start of works is planned for the first quarter of 2027 and they should last five and a half years. Butković expressed the hope that there will be no new major crises in the world that could, like previous ones, cause disruptions and price increases.

the lowland railway project

The minister also spoke about the lowland railway, a project that has been in preparation for a long time. “We have started with the Hrvatski Leskovac – Karlovac section. As for the reconstruction of the lines around Zagreb, mostly everything has been reconstructed: towards the west, towards Zagorje and towards Bjelovar. By the end of the year we are finishing Dugo Selo – Križevci, which is actually almost done, and Križevci – Koprivnica – Hungarian border,” he said.

He emphasised that it is now important to move towards Rijeka, where the most expensive section from Karlovac to Rijeka remains, whose value is estimated at more than 2.5 billion euros. “There has been an increase in prices due to all the disruptions I spoke about, but we have accelerated the entire project.

A tender for technical assistance is currently underway. We would go for the so-called Alliance model, in which design, obtaining building permits and execution of works would be in one package,” he explained. Under that model, the selected contractor would lead all procedures, which would shorten public procurement and appeal procedures, and the deadline for construction of the line would be five to six years.

another decade before any real change

Asked when passengers will feel real progress and get fast trains, Butković replied that passenger transport around Zagreb is already functioning well. “We’ve more than 70 new trains in passenger transport. Of those, 42 trains have been procured in the last four years. Contracts are constantly being signed and funds secured. This was also shown these days during the strike, when the trains helped a lot, especially in the suburban area,” he emphasised.

Nevertheless, the complete reconstruction of the railway network will still take time. “I always say that we have to be patient for another ten years or so. In those ten years we would manage to mostly reconstruct and build everything on the main corridors and reconstruct a large part of the regional lines. We have already spent around 900 million euros on the reconstruction of local and regional lines across Croatia,” he said.

the continuation of motorway construction

The minister also commented on motorway construction. He announced that the Istrian Y will be completed by the end of the year or the beginning of 2027. “We’re strongly and decisively going ahead with the construction of the Adriatic-Ionian Corridor, Križišće – Žuta Lokva. Two contracts have been signed there. Today we received the building permit for the first section and we are starting the works. That is around 400 million euros,” he said.

Bids have also been opened for the first section of the motorway towards Dubrovnik. Although the new bids are also above the estimated value, the tender will not be cancelled again. “We would not have cancelled the first one either if there had not been really large differences in price compared to the estimated values. The bids that arrived in the new tender are around 40 to 50 million euros lower compared to the previous tender,” Butković concluded. He said that they are decisively proceeding with the completion of the Adriatic-Ionian Corridor, that is, the motorway towards Dubrovnik and the Križišće – Žuta Lokva section.

World.title: Record Revenue from Foreign Tourists in Croatia in 1st 6 Months of 2026
World.content:
October the 1st, 2026 – Record revenue from foreign tourists in Croatia during the first 6 months of 2026 has amounted to incredible sums, amounting to well over 3 billion euros.

In the first six months of this year, 2.5 billion euros more revenue was generated than in the same period of 2016, said Tonči Glavina. As Novi list reports, according to the latest data from the Croatian National Bank (HNB), in the second quarter of 2026 revenues from foreign tourists amounted to 3 billion and 641.7 million euros, which represents growth of almost 4 percent compared to the same period in 2025, or 132.7 million euros more.

Overall, in the first half of 2026, revenues from foreign tourists amounted to 4 billion and 587 million euros, which represents growth of almost 5 percent compared to the same period in 2025, or 212.4 million euros more. In addition, strong growth in domestic tourism also contributed to the positive results of the tourist year.

In the first six months of 2026, a record 1.5 million arrivals and 4.2 million overnight stays by domestic tourists were recorded, which is 7 percent more arrivals and 6 percent more overnight stays than a year earlier.

“The excellent indicators in the pre-season are the result of strong strategic and promotional activities that we adapted to changes in the market, thereby continuing the positive trends of Croatian tourism even in this extremely challenging year. If we compare these financial results with those recorded back in 2016, revenues from foreign tourists have risen by 120 percent, both in the second quarter and in the first half of the year.

In the first six months of this year, 2.5 billion euros more revenue was generated than in the same period of 2016, while in the second quarter revenue was higher by two billion euros compared to the same period ten years ago. In line with all our strategic goals, we’re permanently changing Croatian tourism for the better in all segments,” emphasised Minister of Tourism and Sport Tonči Glavina.
