World.title: St. Jerome Exhibition Awaits Passengers at Split Airport
World.content:
October the 1st, 2026 – A brand new St. Jerome exhibition now awaits passengers coming and going from Split Airport.

The new exhibition brings together works by 24 prominent Croatian painters and sculptors created at the St. Jerome Art Colony on Marjan. Morski reports that the exhibition was officially opened by Split-Dalmatia County Prefect Blaženko Boban.

“On the occasion of the feast of Saint Jerome and Split-Dalmatia County Day, we organised an exhibition of our most eminent painters and sculptors, not only from our county but from the whole of the Republic of Croatia, who took part in the art colony on Marjan. We are presenting the exhibition for the third time, after the University Gallery and the National and University Library in Zagreb,” said Boban. He added that the exhibition at the Airport also opens the possibility for the story of Saint Jerome, Marjan and contemporary Croatian fine art to travel beyond Croatia’s borders.

“I’d like to thank all the artists and the director of Split Airport, and I congratulate him and all the staff on 60 years of very high-quality work by Saint Jerome Airport,” the Prefect said.

This year’s presentation of the exhibition has additional symbolism because Split Airport is marking the 60th anniversary of its founding. Its director Josip Čorić expressed satisfaction that such a cultural event is being held for the first time in the Airport premises.

The exhibition brings together works by Goran Balić, Duje Botteri, Nikola Džaja, Kažimir Hraste, Petar Jakelić, Kuzma Kovačić, Đani Martinić, Duje Matetić, Matko Mijić, Dijana Iva Sesartić, Ana Marija Botteri, Josip Botteri Dini, Željko Bubalo, Alma Čače, Vladimir Davidenko, Lili Gluić, Karin Grenc, Ivan Listeš, Zvonimir Mihanović, Tea Morić Šitum, Hrvoje Marko Peruzović, Vice Tomasović, Marko Gugić and Frane Šitum. The works were created at the St. Jerome Art Colony, held on the 22nd and 23rd of September 2023 on the occasion of the 30th anniversary of Split-Dalmatia County, organised by Split-Dalmatia County, the University of Split and the Parish of the Holy Cross, Veli Varoš.

World.title: HVARMONY, Celebrating Wellbeing on Croatia’s Premier Island
World.content:
September 30, 2026 – Famous for its sun, beaches, heritage and nightlife, a new initiative celebrates another of its gems – wellbeing. Meet HVARMONY.

Soon after I moved to the island of Hvar back in 2003, an island whose existence I had only become aware of two days before I bought my house, I realised that it was a very distinct island of two halves. The most famous, of course, was the tourism side, with its world famous beaches filled with tourists all over the world, as they also enjoyed the fine gastronomy, culture and endless sun.

But there was another side to Hvar, and one that I liked much better – the off-season. No longer warm enough to swim (although some did), devoid of tourists, most businesses closed for the season, but what a fantastic slice of nature to enjoy in peace and quiet. If Croatia made me realise that quality of life, lifestyle and wellbeing were the shortcut to happiness, it was the winters in Jelsa that first pointed the way.

Olive groves, vineyards, growing their own food, while loudly discussing olives and Hajduk Split over timeless coffees, I had never come across a place so contented with itself. And I quickly learned that I was not alone. All over the island, there were Austrians, Norwegians, Americans, Germans living in the hills or smaller villages, some with yoga studios, but all thrilled that they had found such a gem off the radar.

The digital nomad revolution came to Croatia in 2020, enabling a new breed of tourist to spend an extended period in Croatia. One of the first was an American couple who moved to Jelsa and did a great documentary for national tv on why life on a Dalmatian island in January was perfect. Some locals might have thought they were nuts, but I understood perfectly.

And as look around Hvar these days, in addition to the tourism, there is another undercurrent bubbling away – wellbeing. Yoga, pilates, energy healing, retreats – they are all increasing in number and diversity. It is for me an essential part of the Hvar DNA – this is, of course, the island that was nicknamed the Austrian Madeira for its temperate and healing climate, which resulted in it becoming the birthplace of organised tourism in Europe with the founding of the Hvar Health Society in 1868.

But there has been precious little official recognition of this wellbeing aspect. Until now.

Meet HVARMONY, an excellent initiative from the Hvar Tourist Board, which will take place for the first time from October 15-18. And before we get to the concept and programmes, the locations of the event set the tone – the oldest public theatre in Europe, the impressive Arsenal on the corner of the main square, the 1930s colonnade, Bonj les Bains, and the 5-star Maslina Resort, whose slogan is Mindful Luxury.

So what exactly is HVARMONY? An explanation from the dedicated website:

HVARMONY is a four-day gathering built around one simple question: how can we live better, longer and more fulfilling lives?

From 15 to 18 October in Hvar, talks, conversations, workshops and shared experiences will explore what wellbeing really means today, why we seem to need it more than ever, and whether somewhere along the way it has become yet another industry selling us health, happiness and longevity.

Over the four-day event, some 23 Croatian and international speakers will put on an excellent and diverse programme exploring key themes on health, happiness and longevity, with plenty of yoga, pilates and other energy food for the body. You can see the whole programme here.

I really like the direction that Hvar tourism is going these days, it is a much more pleasant experience, and I applaud the organisers of this initiative, which will not only bring together motivated like-minded people, but also showcase some of the magic I first discovered a quarter of a century ago.

Entrance and participation for events is free of charge (with the exception of a few sessions which are paid), although registration is required. You can do this on the official HVARMONY website.

World.title: Uber CEO Comes to Zagreb and Tries Out Rimac’s Robotaxi
World.content:
September the 30th, 2026 – Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi arrived in Zagreb and tried out Mate Rimac’s famed robotaxi without a safety driver.

Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi visited Verne and the Rimac Campus in Zagreb yesterday and rode in a robotaxi without a safety driver, Mate Rimac announced. “Uber is an investor and strategic partner in Verne. Dara tried out the robotaxi without a safety driver in Zagreb and was delighted with the experience. We talked about further cooperation and expanding Verne beyond Croatia with the ‘final’ Verne car without a steering wheel and pedals,” Rimac wrote on Facebook.

Index reports that Uber and Verne have otherwise been cooperating for months now on an autonomous taxi project. Back in March, Verne, China’s Pony.ai and Uber announced a strategic partnership to launch a robotaxi service in Europe, starting in Zagreb. Uber also announced an investment in Verne at that time.

driverless rides are already being tested out in zagreb

At the beginning of September, Verne and Pony.ai began testing rides with passengers in Zagreb without a safety driver or other staff in the vehicle. The tests are taking place on a 22-kilometre route connecting Verne’s headquarters with the area of Zagreb Airport. However, these are vehicles from the Chinese manufacturer BAIC with Pony.ai autonomous driving technology, not the final Verne vehicle without a steering wheel and pedals that Rimac mentions in today’s post. Since August, Uber has also enabled the ordering of autonomous rides via its app in Zagreb. In that phase a licensed operator was still behind the wheel, while fully driverless rides were introduced as separate tests.

the final report for the eu-funded project has been submitted

Mate Rimac’s announcement comes on the same day that Project 3 Mobility, the company developing Verne, submitted its final report to SAFU on the last day of the deadline for the robotaxi project financed from the National Recovery and Resilience Plan. According to what remains unofficial information, the company is not requesting recognition of the remaining part of the already paid advance in the final documentation. Verne had 179.5 million euros in non-repayable EU funds approved for the project, and back in July 2023 it received an advance of 89.75 million euros. SAFU earlier confirmed to Index that of that amount around 8.77 million euros had been justified so far, while around 80.98 million euros had not been justified.

The project formally ended on the 30th of August, after which a 30-day deadline for submitting the final documentation began. SAFU now has 60 days to check the reported costs and documentation, and during the procedure it may also request additional information. Only after the check is completed will it be known how much of the paid advance will be recognised and how much money, if any, Verne will have to return.

the primary contracted goal was not completed in time

The key problem of the EU-funded project remains the fact that by the deadline it was not confirmed that a fully autonomous Level 5 vehicle had been produced and homologated, which was one of the main contracted results of the project. Prime Minister Andrej Plenković said after the deadline expired that the project had not received final homologation from the competent institution in Germany and that it had not been completed by the end of August.

At the beginning of September, Verne revealed that it was ready to return the funds if the final evaluation showed that the contracted obligations had not been fully met. At the same time the company claimed that during the project test prototypes of fully autonomous electric vehicles had been confirmed and appropriate tests carried out. Mate Rimac’s meeting with Uber’s Dara Khosrowshahi therefore concerns the continuation of Verne’s commercial development and cooperation with Uber, while the final evaluation procedure for the EU-funded project continues separately.

World.title: Iraq emerges as India’s second-largest oil supplier
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq became the second-largest oil supplier to India in September, reflecting an increase in supplies to the Indian market compared to the previous month.

Data from Kpler, a leading data platform that tracks commodity flows and maritime shipping, indicates that India’s imports of Iraqi crude reached approximately 579,000 barrels per day between September 1 and September 27.

Iraq followed Russia, which was the largest oil supplier to India, with 1.74 million barrels per day. Saudi Arabia supplied 570,000 barrels per day, followed by the UAE with 483,000 barrels per day and Kuwait with 333,000 barrels per day.

India’s total crude oil imports during September reached approximately 5.25 million barrels per day, a 13 percent increase compared to the average of 4.65 million barrels per day in August.

India’s imports of Iraqi oil stood at 163,000 barrels per day in August, implying that Iraqi supplies increased by around 416,000 barrels per day throughout September.

Iraqi oil exports to India fell in the first half of 2026, as Indian refineries diversified their crude import sources to minimize the geopolitical risks associated with shipping difficulties through the Straits of Hormuz.

According to officials at Indian refining companies and the Indian Ministry of Petroleum, the goal of this measure is to improve supply security.

The drop in Iraqi supplies to India comes at a time when the global oil market is under increased pressure due to security worries along critical maritime routes. This pressure is causing consumers in Asia to split their purchases among many producing countries.

Iraqi oil remains a vital resource for India due to supply security and the high quality of Basra crude.

Experts anticipate that continuing instability in the Middle East will raise oil prices and pose new hurdles for Asian oil-importing countries.

World.title: Ghostly Kisses adds second Baghdad concert after first show sells out within hours
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Ghostly Kisses, a French-Canadian dream-pop duet, has added a second performance in Baghdad after the first sold out within hours of pre-sale, demonstrating Iraq’s tremendous desire for foreign live music.

Ghostly Kisses stated on X that the extra Baghdad show will take place on December 12, one day after the initial Dec. 11 event.

“Baghdad 🖤 due to incredible demand, we are adding a second show on Dec. 12,” the pair announced. Tickets for the extra date will go on sale on Friday, Oct. 2.

The news follows a previous post in which Ghostly Kisses said that their December 11 Baghdad show sold out in only a few hours during pre-sale, before regular ticket sales started.

The musicians said they had not anticipated the demand and were planning to add another concert in response.

The Baghdad performances are part of the Ghostly Kisses MENA Tour 2026, which also stops in Amman, Doha, Abu Dhabi, Cairo, and Kuwait City.

The journey will begin in Amman on November 26 and conclude in Baghdad in December.

Ghostly Kisses, a Quebec City-based duo consisting of vocalist Margaux Sauvé and composer and producer Louis-Étienne Santais, is recognized for its atmospheric sound, which combines dream-pop, techno, and cinematic elements.

The decision to stage two concerts in Baghdad is significant for Iraq’s burgeoning entertainment and cultural landscape.

Major worldwide tours have generally avoided Iraq, especially during the years of warfare and instability that followed the 2003 invasion and subsequent struggle against ISIS.

Baghdad’s improved security has provided more room for foreign cultural events, concerts, and entertainment, while the Iraqi city has witnessed increased investment in hotels, restaurants, retail malls, and other leisure ventures.

The inaugural Ghostly Kisses performance sold out quickly, demonstrating local interest for such events.

Baghdad joined established regional entertainment venues like Abu Dhabi, Doha, and Cairo on the group’s Middle East and North Africa tour.

For Iraq, the concerts have importance beyond the acts themselves. International musicians willing to include Baghdad on regional tours are unusual, but successful events may inspire other performers and promoters to explore the Iraqi market.

Two consecutive Ghostly Kisses performances in December will therefore represent another step in Baghdad’s gradual return to the international touring circuit, reflecting a city that is growing safer and more welcoming to foreign cultural and entertainment activities.

World.title: Iraq sets June 30 as deadline to bring arms under state control
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has set June 30, 2027, as the deadline to bring the weapons of armed factions under state control, announcing that October 1 marks a serious beginning to address the issue of unauthorized weaponry.

Al-Zaidi said in a statement that the Iraqi government is working according to a defined plan and agreed-upon timelines to resolve the arms issue, with the deadline set for no later than June 30, 2027, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

The prime minister’s remarks take place a day after the conclusion of the international coalition’s mission in Iraq and the withdrawal of its forces.

According to al-Zaidi, the Iraqi constitution limits war and peace choices to Iraqi authorities and prohibits any military activity outside of the national framework.

The Iraqi government would work to disarm all non-Iraqi armed groups present on Iraqi soil to maintain the country’s stability as well as border security, according to al-Zaidi.

Al-Zaidi noted that Baghdad is committed to preventing the use of Iraqi territory and airspace to launch attacks or threaten the security of neighboring countries.

The announcement is part of a phased plan to bring arms under state control, beginning with a 90-day preparatory period followed by the gradual handover of weapons, with the entire process scheduled for completion by June 30, 2027.

The prime minister stated that the conclusion of the international coalition’s mission marks the beginning of a new phase for Iraq, calling for state resources to be directed toward development and service improvements.

The plan to control weapons is part of Baghdad’s efforts to reorganize the relationship between armed factions and state institutions. This initiative is taking place amid ongoing discussions focused on transferring weapons and incorporating faction members into state security agencies.

World.title: Iraq weather: Autumn showers and temperature drop forecasted across country
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s General Authority for Meteorology and Seismic Monitoring issued a nationwide weather bulletin on Thursday, October 1, 2026, forecasting transitional autumn conditions characterized by moderate to warm daytime temperatures alongside a noticeable nocturnal and early-morning chill.

The agency noted that skies will remain partly cloudy to fair across most governorates, with localized chances of light convective rain showers accompanied by intermittent thunder and lightning across central and northern areas, extending into limited sectors of northern southern Iraq.

According to the meteorological report, unstable atmospheric conditions and scattered shower probabilities—ranging from light to moderate precipitation—are expected to persist intermittently through Monday, October 5.

Thermal readings across southern governorates continue to record seasonal highs, with Maysan, Dhi Qar, and Basra hovering around the 40°C threshold, whereas northern highlands in Duhok and Sulaymaniyah settle around a mild 29°C. The central and western provinces are recording daytime maximums within the mid-to-upper 30°C bracket.

While Thursday’s temperatures remain comparable to previous daily averages, the meteorological authority projected a nationwide slight thermal dip starting Friday, October 2. The modest cooling trend will continue into Saturday across central and southern provinces before temperatures register a slight upward rebound heading into Sunday and Monday.

World.title: US dollar dips to 157,500 IQD in Baghdad and Basra to open October
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The U.S. dollar extended its gradual downward drift across Iraq’s parallel currency markets on Thursday, October 1, 2026, recording modest dips across trading floors in Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra to kick off the new month. Despite the slight contraction, the market rate continues to hold a spread of over 20 percent against the Central Bank of Iraq’s statutory official peg of 131,000 dinars per $100.

Daily market figures released by the 964 Network indicated that currency bureaus in the capital city of Baghdad offered cash sales at 157,500 dinars per $100 against purchase bids of 156,950 dinars, shaving roughly 250 dinars off Wednesday’s close.

In Erbil, the primary financial trading hub of the Kurdistan Region, parallel exchange counters quoted selling rates at 157,100 dinars per $100, while buying bids settled at 156,750 dinars. In the southern port city of Basra, trading mirrored the capital’s selling price at 157,500 dinars per $100, alongside purchase bids posted at 156,750 dinars.

The easing trend reflects subdued speculative pressure on commercial bourses as local financial markets absorb recent announcements regarding upcoming foreign currency shipments to the Central Bank of Iraq.

While day-to-day liquidity demand from private merchants and commercial importers remains substantial, expectations of reinforced physical dollar reserves through official channels have helped temper sharp fluctuations and sustain relatively stable trading ranges across major provincial hubs.

World.title: PM Al Zaidi declares full sovereignty as coalition exits, sets 2027 arms deadline
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi unveiled a comprehensive security and political roadmap on Thursday, October 1, 2026, coinciding with the official and complete withdrawal of the U.S.-led International Coalition forces across land, air, and maritime domains.

Declaring the realization of full national sovereignty, Al-Zaidi pledged that the state will hold exclusive authority over decisions of war and peace, while initiating structured timelines to dismantle illicit arms and integrate paramilitary formations under constitutional command.

In a national address marking Iraqi Sovereignty Day, the Prime Minister commended the historic milestone, attributing the restoration of territorial independence to the sacrifices of the Iraqi people and the foundational role played by the Supreme Religious Authority’s fatwa of Sufficient Jihad.

He underscored the contributions of national armed forces and volunteer factions in defeating Daesh (ISIS), framing the coalition’s final exit not merely as a military milestone, but as the foundation for a sovereign state capable of managing its own defense.

A central pillar of the roadmap is the formal launch of a state campaign to resolve uncontrolled weapons. Al-Zaidi established a binding deadline of June 30, 2027, to reorganize factional armaments and integrate armed formations strictly under the command of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, while advancing legislation governing the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) within the statutory defense apparatus.

Concurrently, the Prime Minister affirmed that the federal government will systematically disarm all non-Iraqi armed groups present on national territory to safeguard domestic order and secure border regions.

To guarantee territorial and airspace integrity in the post-coalition era, Al-Zaidi announced that the government is initiating immediate procurement programs for a comprehensive national air defense system.

He reaffirmed Baghdad’s constitutional mandate barring Iraqi territory or airspace from serving as a launchpad or transit corridor for hostile actions against neighboring states, while rejecting any cross-border aggression against Iraq.

The Prime Minister concluded by asserting that October 1 initiates a new sovereign era focused on institutional law, civil peace, balanced foreign relations, and directing sovereign wealth toward infrastructure modernization and long-term socio-economic development.

World.title: Iraq’s Ibda’ Club wins 17th Arab Robotics and AI Championship in Alexandria
World.content:
Alexandria (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s “Ibda’ Club for Smart Skills” captured first place at the 17th Arab Robotics and Artificial Intelligence Championship held in Alexandria, Egypt, securing an unprecedented third consecutive continental title for the Iraqi team following previous championship victories in Jordan in 2024 and Tunisia in 2025.

Competing against more than 260 participants representing institutions across the Arab world, the delegation distinguished itself as an integrated family-led unit that combined technical training, project innovation, and accredited international adjudication.

The Iraqi delegation was led by senior software architect Firas Nizar Kareem, who served as head coach and project supervisor, directing a competitive team composed of his children: Maryam, Mohammed, and Ridha. Complementing the technical lineup, Alia Abdul-Hussein Lafteh and Zahra Firas Nizar participated in the regional tournament as certified international judges, creating a six-member delegation representing Iraq across the judging and competitive tiers.

Speaking to media agencies, Kareem traced the club’s championship trajectory back to the 13th edition of the competition in 2022, where the team earned its first international accolade in the ball-collection robotics challenge.

The club subsequently shifted its engineering focus toward the championship’s premier Innovation Category, clinching first place in Jordan in 2024, defending its crown in Tunisia in 2025, and completing the historic hat-trick with the 2026 victory in Alexandria.

While past campaigns were often self-funded by the family—supplemented intermittently by backing from Al-Ghadeer Real Estate Investment Company and the Holy Shrine of Imam Hussain—the Alexandria championship drive was sponsored by the Iraqi Syndicate of Programmers.

Building on the victory, the club is currently coordinating with the Syndicate to roll out youth training initiatives in coding, robotics, and applied artificial intelligence aimed at nurturing young Iraqi technical talent for future international competitions.

World.title: Man City scandal risks damage to Premier League’s booming brand
World.content:
Manchester – The Premier League has won a lengthy legal battle with Manchester City over financial impropriety, but the consequences could leave lasting damage for a league that has long since become the envy of world football.

City face severe sanctions after being found guilty of over 100 charges between 2009 and 2018, with an independent commission exposing “sham” contracts to artificially inflate the club’s revenues and reduce costs by more than £900 million ($1.2 billion).

A hefty points deduction resulting in relegation, stripped titles and even expulsion from the English top flight have been mooted as potential sanctions.

But the damage may not be limited to City alone with an entire era of the Premier League now under a cloud.

A takeover in 2008 by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan, the vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates, transformed City’s fortunes, but also the face of the Premier League.

The club’s first top-flight league title for 44 years was one of the most iconic moments in Premier League history when Sergio Aguero netted the winner against QPR in the 94th minute to deny Manchester United the title.

Some of City’s rivals have been quick to revel in their downfall.

“Another Premier League medal to be added to the cabinet,” posted former Manchester United defender Rio Ferdinand, who was part of the United team that finished second to City in the 2011/12 season.

Yet there could be more lingering collective consequences for a league that has become accustomed to flexing its financial muscle to hoover up the best talent from around the globe.

Italy’s Serie A once enjoyed that status in the 1990s.

Although it had lost some of its lustre by the time the Calciopoli scandal came about in 2006, Italian football has arguably never fully recovered in the two decades since.

That case surrounded club officials influencing which referees would officiate their games and led to Juventus being stripped of two titles and relegated to Serie B.

– Haaland exit inevitable?

The question is now whether fans will be turned away from the Premier League after feeling cheated over what they have witnessed over the past 18 years.

In total City have won eight titles in the last 15 seasons.

They rewrote the record books, becoming the first side to ever achieve 100 points and win the English top flight for four consecutive years.

All of those achievements are now labelled with an asterisk.

“If I was a player, I’d be 100 percent sticking those medals in the bin. Of course you would, it’s cheating,” said former Manchester United captain Roy Keane.

Despite the Premier League’s spending power, English clubs have still struggled to keep the world’s biggest superstars away from Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain.

City’s demise could also see the Premier League lose its marquee player in Erling Haaland.

“The Premier League is Britain’s greatest soft power cultural asset,” Simon Chadwick, professor of Afro-Eurasian sport, told AFP. “What happens when people start to question, ‘what have I been watching all these years?'”

By contrast, the Premier League has argued the City case is proof of strong governance.

The league pursued and persisted with an investigation which began in 2018 despite City’s best attempts to frustrate the process.

“This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history,” said the league’s chief executive Richard Masters.

“It is a key responsibility of the Premier League to ensure that the rules, approved by the clubs themselves, are upheld to protect the integrity of the competition.

“It is paramount that the league remains competitive and fair for all clubs and for the fans. We take that role extremely seriously.”

World.title: Full-body scanners at airports: Govt tests tech & algorithms to address privacy concerns before wider rollout
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India's aviation security regulator is collecting data from ongoing trials of full-body scanners at Bengaluru and Cochin airports before deciding on their wider deployment, with the technology's algorithms also being refined to account for objects commonly worn by passengers in India.

Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS) Director General Rajesh Nirwan told reporters on Thursday that full-body scanners have been mandated at eight airports, while trials are currently being conducted at Bengaluru and Cochin. Authorities are collecting data from the trials, including the number of alarms generated, which will be assessed before a decision is taken on introducing the scanners at airports.

However, Cochin is not among the eight airports where the scanners have been mandated.

The deployment of full-body scanners has been delayed for years, partly due to concerns over passenger privacy. Nirwan said newer scanners are being made âimage agnosticâ, meaning they do not produce an actual image of the passenger but instead display a model and identify the specific part of the body where a suspicious object may have been detected, reported PTI.





BCAS is also working with scanner vendors and original equipment manufacturers to refine the technology for Indian conditions, including concerns that jewellery and other commonly worn items could trigger alarms.

âWhat we are getting today in India is based on algorithms that have been designed for foreign markets. There are certain typical things that are on the body of Indian citizens or people living in India.

So, those algorithms are also being continuously refined,â Nirwan said.

The data collected during the ongoing trials will be used to further refine the algorithms, he added.

Meanwhile, the officials also addressed the recent Flydubai cockpit attack in which Indian pilot Smit Machchhar was injured, saying Indian aviation authorities are examining the incident and will hold internal deliberations on whether any aviation security advisory is required.

World.title: PM Modi urges UPSC to test aspirants’ motivation for joining civil services, not just academic knowledge
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Emphasising that the purpose of recruitment for govt jobs should be to bring people into public service rather than public office,

on Thursday asked recruitment agencies like Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) to adopt selection parameters that not only test an aspirant's academic knowledge but also their motivation to join the civil services.

Modi, while addressing UPSC's centenary celebrations here, explained that selecting individuals with the right inherent motivation makes it easier for the administration to adapt to rapidly changing public aspirations. Stating that the youths recruited today will simultaneously serve as the chief architects and the primary beneficiaries of the nation's future, he insisted that every selection process be rigorously tested against the dual criteria of prioritizing the nation and the citizen.

Modi said the archaic 'mai-baap' (supremacy) governance mindset of the past has made way for a modern administrative era built on the absolute principle of 'nagrik devo bhava' or 'citizen is king". Projecting India as an increasingly urbanized nation by 2047 with a narrowing rural-urban divide, he said the traditional service delivery models will need to evolve to match the speed of an instant-delivery world where citizens demand rapid, real-time solutions powered by AI.





âThis changing mindset demands new changes from our civil services as well,â noted Modi.

He demanded that selection processes for govt jobs at both national and state levels be meticulously designed to recruit professionals who proactively anticipate problems and operate without unnecessary pressure or influence. He emphasized the need for empathetic civil servants who find innovative solutions, proactively ease citizens' lives, and critically evaluate the impact of laws on the public.

Cautioning the future civil servants about having to navigate new-age threats like information warfare, deepfakes, algorithmic bias, and climate justice, the prime minister instructed the recruitment agencies to adapt to these global shifts by prioritizing candidates' foresight and complex problem-solving abilities.

He insisted that the examination agencies rapidly align with the nation's broader reform momentum by adopting the principle of time certainty to shorten exam cycles without lowering standards.

These would cut down the financial burden on account of coaching fees, rent, and transport, on the families, he said.

The prime minister proudly noted the dramatic rise in female candidates in civil services, from a mere 3% in 1952 to over 30%today, alongside the historic appointment of three out of four women UPSC chairpersons post-2014.

Pointing to the 45-fold increase in candidate participation since the institution's 50th anniversary in 1976, Modi reminded the commissions that the recruiting agencies are not merely picking candidates, but choosing individuals who will become the very face and representative of the government at the grassroots level.

Congratulating UPSC for having been in existence for 100 years, the prime minister praised the organisation's enduring credibility despite changing generations, governments, technologies, and syllabi. The celebrations were marked by the release of a commemorative postage stamp, a special coin, and a compilation of 100 significant case laws.

Recalling the monumental challenges faced after independence, Modi paid deep homage to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel for establishing the vital steel frame required not just to keep the country independent, but to actively govern the newly formed nation. He acknowledged that while the UPSC has excellently discharged its historical duties, the focus must now decisively pivot toward the critical next 25 years that await the country.

World.title: 'Show me one damaged vehicle': Nitin Gadkari's dare on ethanol blending, targets vested interests
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union minister

on Thursday talked about the Centre's ethanol-blending programme, rejecting claims that mixing ethanol with petrol damages vehicles and arguing that the policy has also opened a new avenue for farmers to diversify beyond food production.

Speaking at the inaugural session of the Bihar Investor Summit 2026, Gadkari said millions of vehicles had already been operating on ethanol-blended petrol since 2022 without, in his account, widespread complaints of damage.

"I challenge anybody to come up with the complaint that his or her vehicle has suffered damage on this account. Of course, those with vested interests may have some other story to tell," said Gadkari, who holds portfolios of Road Transport and Highways, as quoted by PTI.

Gadkari said the policy was designed not merely to reduce dependence on conventional fuel but also to create an additional market for agricultural produce. "We must understand that the decision to blend ethanol with petrol was taken with a view to diversification of agriculture towards energy and power sectors... Our farmers shall no longer remain 'anna data' (food producers) but also become 'urja data' (energy producers)," he said.





According to Gadkari, about 4 crore four-wheelers and 20 crore two-wheelers have been running on petrol blended with ethanol since 2022. He also claimed that major automobile manufacturers had tested vehicles using higher ethanol blends, including 100% ethanol.

"Of course, we are importing (conventional fuel) worth Rs 22 lakh crore, and those who feel that their business will get hit are bound to feel bad. But let me tell you, I am the minister in charge of the department concerned; all leading automobile brands have tried running their vehicles even on 100 per cent ethanol.

And there have been no complaints," he said.

The minister also linked ethanol production to higher farm incomes, saying the use of corn for ethanol had generated additional earnings for farmers in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.

"After the Union government took the decision to make ethanol out of corn and the same was used for the aforementioned purposes, it resulted in additional earnings of up to Rs 45,000 crore for farmers of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.

Is it not preferable to serve the interests of those from whom we import (fuel)," he asked.

Gadkari cited other examples of efforts to develop alternative fuels, including aviation fuel made using agricultural waste. "We have even made aviation fuel with rice straw. The future belongs to innovation, technology and research. And a state like Bihar has to play a key role in this direction," he said.
