World.title: Granting plea bargaining benefit to some accused during trial won’t prejudice others: Karnataka High Court
World.content:
The High Court of Karnataka has held that granting benefit of plea bargaining to a few accused persons under the Criminal Procedure Code (Cr.PC) will not affect the right of other accused persons to defend themselves in the same case.

Justice V. Srishananda made these observation upholding the decision of the special court for CBI cases, which in December, 2023, accepted the application for plea bargaining filed under Section 265B of the Cr.PC by four accused persons, three individuals and a company, in a 2016 bank fraud case.

Granting benefit of plea bargaining to K.T. Venkatesh, V.V. Vasantha Kumar, both directors of M/s Volton Agro Foods Products India Pvt Ltd, Bengaluru; Anil Kumar, a contractor, and the company, the special court had convicted for criminal conspiracy and cheating and sentenced the three individuals to undergo a simple imprisonment for only one day, till the raising of the court, and had imposed ₹1.25 lakh each as fine.

The special court had dropped charge of criminal breach of trust against them on noticing that they had repaid the borrowed amount utilising the One Time Settlement scheme.

However, petitioner R. Chittaranjan Das, the then manager of Central Bank of India and accused number-1 in the case, contended that grant of benefit of plea bargain to the three individuals and the company would affect his right as he is also facing criminal conspiracy along with them under Section 120B of the Indian Penal Code.

Rejecting his plea, the High Court said that his apprehension that the co-accused’s admission of guilt would affect his defence was “hypothetical and cannot be countenanced in law.”

Also, the High Court emphasised that the prosecution must independently establish the guilt of the remaining accused, including the petitioner, through cogent evidence.

Burden or proof

The admission of guilt by one set of accused does not relieve the prosecution of its burden to prove charges against others, the High Court said.

The laudable object of plea bargaining in the Cr.PC is to lessen the prosecution’s burden and grant leniency to those who admit guilt, the High Court pointed out.

The High Court remarked that a person who wants to become an approver by resorting to Section 306 of the Cr.PC, stands on a different footing than a person who wants to avail the benefit of plea bargaining under the provisions of the Cr.PC.

What is plea bargaining?

Plea bargaining is a lawful negotiation in which an offender is allowed to confess his guilt in court voluntarily in certain types of criminal cases and in exchange bargain for a lighter punishment than the one actually prescribed for offences alleged against him.

World.title: Dharwad Chamber of Commerce and Industries seek withdrawal of MDR on UPI transactions
World.content:
The Dharwad Chamber of Commerce and Industries has urged the government to withdraw Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) charges on specified UPI transactions, saying the levy would increase the burden on traders and could eventually raise prices for consumers.

In a memorandum to the Finance Minister, submitted through the Deputy Commissioner of Dharwad, the chamber welcomed the promotion of digital payments but sought deletion of the MDR-related provisions from the Act.

It questioned the rationale for imposing MDR on transactions above ₹2,000 and termed the proposed ₹300 cap discriminatory. Shifting the burden from the payer to the merchant, it said, was against the principle of ease of doing business.

The chamber said the additional cost could particularly affect traders dealing in goods with printed MRP and operating on thin margins. They might have to absorb the cost until stocks carrying revised MRPs reached the market, it said.

It also cautioned that the MDR could encourage consumers to opt for cash, undermining efforts to promote digital payments and increasing the government’s currency-management costs.

The chamber said the UPI, as a government-backed payment infrastructure, should not attract charges for merchants and suggested that the government bear the cost, as it does for currency printing and distribution.

It also proposed a Merchant Service Recognition Fund, financed by earmarking a small portion of taxes collected through merchants, including GST. The fund, it said, could recognise the role of merchants in tax collection, employment generation and service delivery.

World.title: State govt. nominates new chief to SUDA in Shivamogga
World.content:
The State government on Thursday nominated Congress leader C.G. Madhusudan as chairperson of the Shivamogga-Bhadravathi Urban Development Authority (SUDA), replacing H.S. Sundaresh, who recently made allegations against several party leaders, including School Education Minister Madhu Bangarappa.

The order was issued on Thursday, by the under secretary of the Urban Development Department. The newly nominated chairperson took the charge of his office in the afternoon.

Mr. Madhusudan, 40, has been associated with the Congress for years and has served as an office-bearer of the Youth Congress. He was recently appointed State coordinator of the Youth Congress committee, with the responsibility of constituting Bharat Joto Yuva Sanghas in 11 districts.

Mr. Sundaresh, a former president of the District Congress Committee, was appointed SUDA chairperson in February 2024. He recently held a press conference in Shivamogga, where he made allegations against several Congress leaders, including Mr. Bangarappa, who is also the Minister in-charge of the district.

He is also said to have used expletives while criticising party leaders, following which the Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) issued him a notice on September 24, asking him to respond within seven days. The government’s decision to appoint a new chairperson came within a week of the notice.

World.title: CITU welcomes SC order lifting ban on manufacturing joined crackers
World.content:
Virudhunagar District CITU - Fireworks Matches Workers Association has welcomed the Supreme Court judgement on Wednesday lifting the ban on manufacturing and bursting of next generation joined green crackers.

In a statement the association president, P. N. Deva and its general secretary, M. C. Pandian, said that joined crackers was a popular fireworks goods in festivals, victory celebrations and in some places even during funerals.

The joined crackers are used by people from all religions and it constitutes around 40% of the total production of fireworks, the association said.

After its ban by the Centre, the CITU had conducted a series of protest against banning joined crackers and also Barium Nitrate which was an important chemical in fireworks production.

“We conducted protests by organising gruel centres, wait in protest, human chain, black flag protest and also a mega protest of laying siege to the Collectorate in December 2018,” the association said.

The CITU-affiliated association, then led by its president, M. Mahalakshmi, impleaded itself in the case against banning joined crackers and barium nitrate before the Supreme Court.

The association had fought against the ban both on the streets and also in the court. Welcoming the court order, the association said that the Centre should also recommend to lift the ban on barium nitrate before the Supreme Court.

World.title: Association wants Rajapalayam railway station to be upgraded as secondary terminal
World.content:
The Rajapalayam Rail Users’ Association has demanded that Rajapalayam railway station be upgraded as secondary terminal for train services on Madurai-Sengottai section.

A resolution to this effect was passed at the fifth general body meeting of the association held on Sunday. Association president Ramakrishnan, presided over the meeting in the presence of its secretary, Vijay and treasurer, Jegath Sankar.

The association demanded that the shelter be provided for the full length of the first platform in the railway station. Similarly, the development works under Amrit Bharat Scheme in the railway station should be expedited and retiring room facility be provided.

Construction work for Sholapuram railway station should be commenced soon and a MEMU rail workshop should be set up at Madurai railway junction. Advance ticket booking facility should be provided at Rajapalayam railway station from 8 a.m. till 8 p.m., the statement added.

The association sought several train services which benefit rail users of Rajapalayam, including operation of Silambu Express daily, new overnight express train between Kollam and Erode connecting Rajapalayam with Coimbatore and Tiruppur; a new daily express train to Bengaluru via Rajapalayam.

The association also wanted to augment the coaches in Mayiladurai-Sengottai express to 20 coaches with ticket reservation facility and to restore the departure time of Pothigai Express at Chennai to 8.50 p.m.

Tambaram-Tenkasi day-time special train service should be resumed. Convenient link should be provided for Train number 56771 Madurai-Sengottai passenger with Mysuru-Thoothukudi Express.

World.title: Minister seeks public cooperation to keep Kurnool clean
World.content:
Industries and Commerce Minister T.G. Bharath Gupta on Thursday said that the onus of keeping the city clean rests not only with sanitation staff but with every person, urging students and voluntary organisations in Kurnool to come forward and raise awareness among citizens about the importance of cleanliness.

Mr. Bharath, along with Kurnool Municipal Corporation (KMC) Commissioner Challa Obulesu and staff, took part in the 'Ek din - ek gantha - ek saath’ (One day - One hour - Together) initiative, aimed at creating awareness about cleanliness as part of Swacchtha hi Seva - 2026. Along with the municipality staff, the Minister swept the roads at Sankalbagh on the banks of the Tungabhadra River.

Commissioner Obulesu said the civic body is taking various steps to keep the city clean and pointed out that the participation of the public is crucial. He urged people not to throw garbage on the streets and to segregate dry and wet waste. He asked people to keep their surroundings clean and also to educate others about the importance of cleanliness.

Pedala Sevalo programme

Meanwhile, Mr. Bharath along with Collector Dr. A. Siri disbursed pension to the beneficiaries in the Birlagadda area as part of ‘Pedala Sevalo’ programme.

Speaking on the occasion, the Minister expressed happiness about Kurnool Assembly constituency securing 8th rank at the State level for positive public perception of government services. He said that Kurnool constituency holds first position at the district level.

Mr. Bharath urged officials and public representatives to work in coordination and put in greater effort to reach the top spot at the state level. He noted that feedback is being systematically collected from the public on whether pensions are reaching them on time and if they are facing any challenges.

The Minister stated that a positive perception is formed based on the public’s feedback regarding the government services they receive.

World.title: Officials step up vigil to check functioning of quarries
World.content:
The Departments of Revenue and Geology and Mines, and the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board have stepped up vigil to monitor the functioning of stone quarries in the district.

According to sources, there are about 70 quarries in the district. Except for a few, most of them are are functioning in private landholdings. Some quarries, which were given conditional lease licences by the Geology and Mines Department, have been inoperative.

Collector C. Muthukumaran made surprise visits recently to various quarries in the district to check whether they were following the rules and regulations stipulated by the Department of Geology and Mines and the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board. He checked whether the quarries mined beyond the permitted level. Similarly, he reviewed the adherence of safety rules and environmental regulations.

He told The Hindu that some quarries were found to have been detected for committing licence violations. They would be imposed penalties on violations. No quarries would be allowed to violate the conditions. Strict action would be taken against the violators. The process of levying penalties on the quarries, which were found to have violated the conditions of the licence, had been initiated.

Mr. Muthukumaran said the officials of Revenue, Geology and Mines and others had been instructed to step up vigil on the functioning of stone quarries. They would carry out periodic visits to quarries. He had been making surprise inspections. The quarries would have to strictly follow all rules and regulations.

World.title: Telangana fine-tunes Hyderabad policing map with new zones, divisions
World.content:
Nine months after a major reorganisation of policing jurisdictions across Hyderabad and its suburbs, the Telangana government has fine-tuned the map again, creating a new Uppal Law and Order Zone along with three new divisions, while revising police station, traffic and Women Safety Wing jurisdictions across Hyderabad, Malkajgiri and Cyberabad commissionerates.

The Home Department issued three government orders on September 30, modifying parts of the reorganisation notified in December 2025. The fresh exercise was taken up in view of the restructuring of GHMC, with the government citing the need for better policing efficiency, supervision, response time and law and order management.

Malkajgiri sees biggest reshuffle

The most substantial structural changes are in Malkajgiri Commissionerate, where the Begumpet Law and Order zone has been officially absorbed under Malkajgiri zone and a new Uppal Zone created.

Three new Law and Order divisions, Alwal, Uppal and Medipally, have been created. Alwal Division is formed by reorganising areas of the earlier Tirumalagiri Division and Alwal police station jurisdiction.

The new arrangement also reshuffles jurisdictions involving Kushaiguda, Cherlapally, Nagole, Tukaramgate and Vanasthalipuram. Addagutta ward will remain with Tukaramgate police station. Vanasthalipuram police station will additionally cover wards 41 and 42, Hastinapuram and B.N. Reddy Nagar, which were earlier under Meerpet police station.

The government has reconsidered an earlier jurisdictional change concerning Secunderabad Railway Station, deciding to retain it with Gopalapuram police station of Malkajgiri Commissionerate. Begumpet police station will similarly retain the road leading to the old airport and the area adjacent to the airport.

Traffic policing has also been recast. A new Uppal Traffic Division has been created comprising Uppal, Kushaiguda and Ghatkesar Traffic Police Stations.

Hyderabad’s internal structure recast

In Hyderabad, the latest order primarily reorganises the internal structure following the earlier territorial changes.

The Khairatabad side is reorganised into Khairatabad-I and Khairatabad-II zones, with police stations and divisions across Banjara Hills, Jubilee Hills, Film Nagar, S.R. Nagar, Borabanda, Nampally, Abids, Khairatabad, Lake, Saifabad, Narayanguda and Sultan Bazar realigned under the revised structure.

Changes have also been made on the Secunderabad side, while Santosh Nagar Division has been renamed Charminar Division.

The Law and Order changes are accompanied by a corresponding reshuffle of traffic jurisdictions. Begumpet, Tirumalagiri and Gopalapuram Traffic Police Stations move from Hyderabad City Police to Malkajgiri Commissionerate.

The Women Safety Wing has also been realigned with the reorganised zones, while the Women Police Station attached to the erstwhile North Zone moves to Malkajgiri Commissionerate. Hyderabad’s zonal cyber units are similarly aligned with the revised zonal structure.

Cyberabad boundaries adjusted

The changes in Cyberabad are largely at the police station and neighbourhood level, particularly around Ameenpur-IDA Bollaram, Patancheru, Kollur, Ramachandrapuram, Narsingi and Mokila.

Parts of the existing Ameenpur police station jurisdiction, including areas in Bollaram, are shifted to IDA Bollaram police station under Ramachandrapuram Division of the Serilingampally Zone.

Edulanagulapally moves from Patancheru police station to Kollur police station under Narsingi Division.

The order also redraws jurisdictions around Kollur, Osmannagar, Tellapur and several BHEL and Ramachandrapuram neighbourhoods. The Narsingi boundary has been further clarified, with Hydershakote, Gandamguda, Bayragiguda and Pirancheru, including the RBVRR Telangana Police Academy and Army firing range, falling under Rajendranagar police station rather than Narsingi.

Meanwhile, in Future City, areas listed in the Narsingi-Mokila-Chevella belt include Janwada, Mirjaguda, Maharajpet, Donthanpally, Gopularam and Pilligundla, with the notification specifying their revised police station and commissionerate jurisdictions.

World.title: ‘Why the need for all this drama’: DG ISPR lampoons India's 'neutralised Pakistani terrorist' claims, presents him before media
World.content:
Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry lampooned India’s claims of “neutralising” a “terrorist” allegedly linked to the Pakistani military, presenting the individual during a press conference on Thursday.

The press conference comes after Indian media reported that an individual wanted in connection with the April 22 Pahalgam terrorist attack last year had been killed during an “encounter” in Indian Illegally Occupied Kashmir’s Korag area.

Addressing the media, the DG ISPR said he would talk “about a so-called terrorist incident, a false flag that has been staged by the Indian political military”.

He presented a five-point timeline, showing that the whole scenario began on Sept 29.

“On the night of Sep 29, the Indian corps deployed in IIOK made a tweet, claiming that, based on joint intelligence reports, the Indian Army, police and CRPF launched an operation in general area of Korag, Yousmarg,” he read from a social media post by Chinar Corps.

The DG ISPR then referred to another post by Chinar Corps on Sept 30 morning that claimed the Indian forces had found the body of a “Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist”.

The military spokesperson noted that later, India’s ANI news outlet claimed that the deceased had been identified as Mohammad Asif, who had been inducted into the Special Services Group (SSG).

The DG ISPR went on to say that India’s home affairs ministry and Press Information Bureau also reiterated the supposed details.

India’s home affairs ministry said the neutralisation of “Musa alias Asif Fauji” was part of an “ongoing long-sustained Operation Sheruwali” that was launched in May.

“After six months of hard work, Musa alias Asif Fauji has been neutralised. Congratulations, applause,” Lt Gen Chaudhry retorted.

He then read out India’s claims of Asif’s alleged involvement in various attacks, including Halan attack August 23, DKG attack December 23, Kandi attack May 2023, Shah Sitar attack May 2024, Shiv Khori attack June 2024, Gagangeer attack October 2024, Boota Pahari attack October 2024, and Basira attack April 2025.

The DG ISPR then noted that the Indian government also claimed to have neutralised three other “members of the group”.

“After this [press conference], the shameful characters will have at least the shame to delete this,” he remarked.

The DG ISPR also read out the Indian PIB’s narrative, which said their forces had killed “four senior LeT commanders”.

He took a jibe at Indian media too for highlighting the claims: “Now they said, ‘Let’s jump in’.

“So there comes News18, Statesman, India Today, Hindustan Times, ABP Live, Indian Express,” he said, as he displayed the screengrabs of these outlets’ reports on the matter.

The DG ISPR then called Asif to join him during the presser, who said he was a resident of Attock district.

“So here is that superman. You can see this superman. Please, come, my brother. Tell us about these achievements of yours, what all you have been doing,” Lt Gen Chaudhry quipped.

‘Here, alive and healthy’

Speaking before the media, Asif narrated: “Yesterday, some friends called me and told me there were reports on social media that I had been martyred by the Indian army in Kashmir.

“To their concerns, I responded that I was here, alive and healthy.”

Asif said he also received calls from the Indian numbers, asking him for his personal information, identity and whereabouts and his connection with the claims.

“Through ANI on social media, I became aware of the reports that Indian media, using my personal data, had named me as a martyr in an operation in Kashmir,” Asif said.

“I was surprised by whatever was happening as I was sitting in my home,” he remarked.

Following the reports, Asif said that he informed his unit about the reports to clarify his position, and the unit asked him to block all the numbers calling from India and said that ISPR officials would contact him.

Sharing details about himself, Asif said that he joined the Pakistan Army in the year 2000. “In 2005, I joined the SSG, performed my duty with courage for 18 years, and retired in 2023.”

Asif added that he had also worked for a private security company for three years. “For the past three or four months, I have been living with my family in our home in Rawalpindi.”

He termed the Indian allegations as “false, ignominious and disreputable”.

“I condemn this. By the grace of God, I am alive and present before you.“

He further affirmed that he performed his duties with courage and that Pakistan responds face to face, not from behind.

‘Six reasons behind such dramas’

Taking on the mic, the DG ISPR maintained that there were “six reasons” behind “such dramas” by India against Pakistan.

“It is a very shameful and embarrassing thing. No self-respecting nation does this.”

Explaining the first reason, Lt Gen Chaudhry said that India did those theatrics to “cover its own track of terrorism”. “So, there has to be some good reason,” he added.

“India is the biggest sponsor of terrorism and a terrorist state in the world,“ the DG ISPR declared.

“And its implication, involvement, direct and indirect terrorism in the region goes back decades,” he added.

“Whether it’s Mukti Bahini or LTT, and now the TTP, BLA, and their funding, sponsorship and planning. It (India) has now become a victim of its own trait.”

The military spokesperson highlighted that this terrorism was also “now taking on an internal dimension”.

He elaborated: “They are not just terrorising the region or countries around the region; they are terrorising the Muslims inside India, and also the Kashmiris, Sikhs, Dalits, Christians, [residents of] Manipur, and tribals.

“Some country which lives and breathes terrorism is at the same time very afraid that their dark face will be exposed, so they have to cover their tracks. What better way to cover their tracks than to start calling everyone else a terrorist?”

Lt Gen Chaudhry then played a video clip on the “decades of lies that they have been feeding to their own people as well as to the world at large”.

He accused India of jailing Muslim Kashmiris, adding: “They take them out, kill them, and stage that as a false flag operation, portraying it as a terrorist act.”

The DG ISPR quipped: “This time they went ahead; they said this is not very spicy, let’s take an army soldier of Pakistan and portray him as one that we have killed.”

He then brought attention to India’s involvement in transnational killings, saying, “This habit of false flag operations has further encouraged India to go for transnational killings.”

He added, “Everyone whom they don’t like, they start calling terrorists, because they see their image.”

The military spokesperson then played a video containing a clip of an Afghan minister saying “our DNA is one” as he referred to India.

“That is the illegitimate child of this terrorism, which is on our western border,” Lt Gen Chaudhry said, referring to Afghanistan.

“Because what better opportunity than to give this dirty work to someone who is ready to do it for certain coins and dollars and money,” he retorted.

The DG ISPR then identified the second reason for the claims as the developments in occupied Jammu and Kashmir, describing it as the “biggest garrison of the world”.

“What’s happening in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir plays a big role in the psyche and in the cognitive domain of these Indians,” he asserted.

“For every 10th Kashmiri, there is an Indian soldier or a security person. There are nearly 1 million military, security, and intelligence CRPF and law enforcement there,” he pointed out, noting other acts such as arrests and demolition of houses.

“And you cannot subside them; you cannot take out their desire to be counted. It’s a simple desire,” Lt Gen Chaudhry said, mentioning the United Nations Security Council resolution on self-determination for Kashmiris.

He stated that New Delhi had to stage such incidents to “portray that Kashmiris have no problem”, whereas the reality was otherwise due to the “oppression” being committed against them.

Indian claims

Indian media had claimed that the supposedly slain individual was affiliated with the banned Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) and a soldier of the Pakistan military. The claim, attributed to “sources”, named the individual as Mohammad Asif.

It may be recalled that Indian media and authorities have made several allegations regarding Pakistani involvement in the April Pahalgam incident in the past, but failed to substantiate them. The Pakistan government and security forces have yet to respond to this most recent allegation.

“Mohammad Asif alias Hashim Moosa was born on 07 March 1980. He joined the Pakistan Army in 2000 under service number PA-3106947 and retired with the rank of Havildar,” India’s Asian News International (ANI) reported on Thursday.

It also provided a detailed profile of the slain man. “In 2005, Mohammad Asif was inducted into the Special Services Group (SSG). He served with 4 Commando ‘Yalgar’ Battalion and was posted to Balochistan from 2006 onward. During his deployment in Balochistan, he reportedly participated in approximately 10 operations against Baloch insurgents and is credited with 13 personal kills,” the ANI news report stated, adding that Asif was also part of the security detail of former president Pervez Musharraf.

It was stated by ANI that Asif was “wanted in the Pahalgam terror attack”, and the claim was repeated by the Indian Army’s Chinar Corps — part of the Northern Command and headquartered in occupied Kashmir. The corps primary area of responsibility is the Kashmir area of operations.

In May 2025, a four-day conflict between Pakistan and India was sparked by an attack on tourists in occupied Kashmir’s Pahalgam, which New Delhi, without evidence, linked to Pakistan.

Islamabad had strongly denied responsibility while calling for a neutral investigation .

After New Delhi launched deadly air strikes in Punjab and Azad Kashmir on May 7, Pakistan said it downed at least six Indian aircraft in air-to-air combat, later raising the tally to eight .

After tit-for-tat strikes on each other’s airbases, it took American intervention on May 10 for both sides to finally reach a ceasefire .

During that conflict, Indian media had been heavily criticised for beating the war drums and regurgitating fake news fed by Indian government sources. Many mainstream Indian channels had also aired inflammatory anti-Pakistan and anti-Muslim content.

India’s ranking in the Reporters Without Borders’ World Press Freedom Index has deteriorated sharply over the past decade. The country ranked 122nd in 2010 but fell to 157th out of 180 countries in 2026.

In April, on the first anniversary of the Pahalgam attack, Pakistan had rejected a renewed Indian propaganda campaign linking it to the attack, deploring that the neighbouring country was focusing on “weaponising its false narrative” in the midst of a regional crisis sparked by the US-Israel war on Iran.

World.title: Ready to sit under any tree but no talks at PM House, Office or speaker's chamber, says Achakzai
World.content:
Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly Mehmood Khan Achakzai did not explicitly rule out talks with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday but said he was not ready to hold parleys at the Prime Minister’s House or Office or the Speaker’s Chamber.

“The prime minister is illegitimate. The mandate of millions of Pakistanis … Harsh words are rising to my lips; that is why I am silent.

“I am ready to sit anywhere in Pakistan, under any tree. I am ready to visit the house of any party [leader]. But I will not go to the speaker house [sic], the Prime Minister’s House or the prime minister’s chamber,” he said while speaking to the media at Parliament House after a meeting of the opposition leaders.

Achakzai’s remarks were in response to a question about the prime minister’s adviser, Rana Sanaullah, inviting him and PTI Chairperson Barrister Gohar to hold a sitting with the premier. The reporter asked him why the meeting was not taking place.

In a video clip shared by the opposition alliance Tehreek-i-Tahaffuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan (TTAP), Achakzai also said the meeting with the prime minister would take place after a meeting with jailed former premier and PTI founder Imran Khan.

The possibility of a meeting between the prime minister and Achakzai is being seen as a means to defuse the current political crisis in the country, with the PTI’s planned Oct 4 protest march to demand Imran’s release becoming the new bone of contention between the party and the Centre.

The TTAP, which is headed by Achakzai and also includes the PTI, has announced that it would join the protest. And as the PTI remains resolute to go ahead with the march, federal ministers have warned that the Centre would have no other option but to impose the governor’s rule or emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa — where Imran’s party is in the government — in light of the security situation in the province and the PTI’s protest call on Oct 4.

For its part, the opposition party has warned the government of dire consequences if such a decision is imposed.

PM Shehbaz had also extended an invitation to the NA opposition leader to sit together for consultations on the issues of national impor­tance and those related to the PTI before leaving for the US. Earlier, the premier also invited Achakzai on Sept 11 for mandatory consultation on the appointment of a new chief election commi­ssioner.

Opposition leaders’ meeting

Achakzai and other opposition leaders held a meeting in the Senate opposition leader’s chamber earlier in the day.

The meeting was also attended by Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, Barrister Gohar, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, former senator Mustafa Nawaz Khokhar, former NA speaker Asad Qaiser, NA Chief Whip Aamer Mahmood Kamboh, TTAP spokesperson Akhundzada Hussain Ahmad Yusufzai, and other opposition leaders.

The consultations regarded the country’s overall political situation, the long march, and constitutional and parliamentary affairs.

Opposition ready for dialogue but ‘without conditions’: Senate opposition leader

Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas called for reconciliation and dialogue to resolve the country’s political crisis, saying his side was ready for talks, but without preconditions.

Speaking to the media today, he said, “This judiciary is ours, all these matters are ours, and we are ready to discuss them.”

He also stressed that the protest in KP would be peaceful even when met with violence, and that “no false narrative” should be created against the protest.

“I have said before as well that when we leave from there, there will be no weapons in our hands … We will carry the Quran in our pockets,” he said. “We know the value of human life.”

“An official of the administration or a member of the security forces is also our brother. Who would want to shed the blood of his own brothers?”

He also rejected claims of cowardice, saying that the “cowards” were those who had placed containers and dug up roads.

Abbas called for a move towards reconciliation and dialogue in order to improve the country, saying, “Let’s return people their rights and, God willing, make Pakistan a truly constitutional and legal country. Make it a country of the people and a representative of their aspirations.”

“We are fully prepared to hold dialogue and correct the situation, but this will be without any conditions. If anyone thinks that they will hold a dagger of conditions at our necks, then, such a thing will never be accepted,” he said.

Regarding the proposed protest, Abbas said the people of KP had “decided to adopt a democratic approach by staging peaceful protests and a long march”.

He said the government should have “assured the protesters of the protection of their lives and property, provided them with facilities, and, while recognising the right to peaceful protest, designated the routes”.

“But, on the contrary, what did the government do? Even before the protests began, containers were placed to seal Islamabad, roads were dug up and nails were hammered into the routes,” he said, claiming that this was the behaviour of “scared people”.

Stressing that the Constitution guaranteed the rights of the Pakistani people, Abbas said peaceful protests, sit-ins and long marches were part of democratic politics.

“Protests can have many forms and objections can also have many methods. It can be in the form of a press conference, a seminar, a demonstration, a sit-in or a long march. This is prevalent throughout the world,” he said.

“When you talk about protests, objections, sit-ins or long marches, some people call it an attack. No, this is not an attack,” he added.

The opposition leader also criticised the arrests of protesters under the Maintenance of Public Order law, terming it a completely illegal practice.

He alleged that the country was facing worsening political, economic and law-and-order crises.

“Unrest is increasing day by day and the law and order situation has become extremely poor, which proves that the government has completely failed to establish peace,” he said.

“The country’s economic situation is also extremely bad and the rulers have proved incapable of managing the economy. Similarly, the political crisis is continuously intensifying and the government does not have the ability to resolve political issues. In short … the current system, judiciary and all other state institutions have completely collapsed,” he added.

Abbas also criticised that “bloodshed is being carried out in the name of peace”, stressing that peace could not be established through bullets.

On Imran Khan, Abbas said, “The only personality who can take Pakistan out of the current crisis is Imran Khan, whom the people trust.”

“He will go to Balochistan, where Akhtar Mengal and other leaders will be with him. He will sit with the people and talk to them and convince them. What you cannot do through the force of bullets can be done through dialogue because the people trust him,” he added.

Abbas said the welfare of the people should be the state’s top priority.

“Full attention should be given to the state’s agreement with the people that it will protect their lives, property and honour,” he said, also stressing the need to provide people with rights, services and protection of their interests.

In the morning, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said that the federal government and PTI were engaged in “off-the-record talks” regarding PTI’s planned protest on Oct 4.

Sanaullah made the remarks while appearing in Geo News’ morning show “Geo Pakistan”.

Sanaullah said that the decision on the proposed march rested with PTI’s senior leadership, “with whom off-the-record consultation is ongoing”.

“So let us see, even if they do not postpone it, we have arrangements in place to stop them,” Sanaullah warned.

He likened the PTI’s march to a “provincial government attacking the capital” in an apparent reference to the PTI-led government in KP.

“If a political party or a private organisation stages a protest, […] but for a government to attack […] it cannot be tolerated under any circumstances,” he held.

“The law will be enacted in full force, and they (PTI) will be barred from entering Islamabad,” he added.

Responding to a question about governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Sanaullah on Thursday said that the option was “on the table”.

Sanaullah further clarified that the federal government was in talks with coalition parties about imposing governor’s rule in KP. He added that the final decision rested upon the federal government and the Senate, adding that it would only come into effect with parliament’s approval.

Sanaullah alleged that the KP chief minister had not been performing his functions as the province’s chief executive.

“For the past two months, he has not done anything, nothing about development or counter-terrorism efforts or for the welfare of people […] in fact, all he has done is talk about marching to Islamabad and toppling the federal government.

“They want to take ladders to Islamabad to secure the release of a certain someone,” he added.

Sanaullah reiterated that if a province is “engaged in such illegal and unconstitutional activities, then the Centre has the right to declare emergency or governor rule and assume power”.

World.title: ‘Calibrated’ air strikes target terrorist hideouts at two locations in Afghanistan: info ministry
World.content:
Pakistan carried out “well-planned and calibrated” air strikes against terrorist hideouts in Afghanistan, the information ministry said on Thursday.

In a post on X, the ministry said the strikes were carried out in continuation of Operation Ghazab lil Haq and Pakistan’s resolve to eliminate terrorists, their networks and supporters.

It said the aerial strikes targeted the hideouts and safe havens of terrorist organisations it referred to as Fitna al Khwarij and Fitna al Hindustan, and resulted in the deaths of “multiple terrorists”.

The state uses the term Fitna al Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and refers to designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna al Hindustan to highlight India’s role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

The statement added, “Based on credible intelligence, selective targeting of terrorist camps and hideouts at two locations belonging to Fitna al Khawarij, Fitna al Hindustan and their affiliates has been carried out in Afghanistan with precision and accuracy.”

The ministry said the targets were destroyed, with initial reports suggesting that 22 terrorists had been killed.

“Large quantities of weapons and ammunition stored at these hideouts were also destroyed,” it said.

The ministry added that Pakistan had always stressed regional peace and stability, but held that the safety of Pakistani citizens remained the “foremost priority”.

The statement expressed concern that Afghanistan “continues to remain a hub of terrorism. The threat to Pakistan emanates from Afghanistan”, adding that, keeping in view the fact, the strikes had targeted terrorist hubs and “maximum precaution” was taken to ensure “no collateral damage”.

It added that Pakistan’s counter-terrorism campaign Ghazab lil Haq will continue at “full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country”.

Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned TTP, that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded.

According to a UN Security Council-mandated monitoring report — covering the period from Dec 16, 2025, to June 9, 2026 — Afg­han Taliban’s continued support for TTP has contributed to a rise in the frequency and lethality of terrorist attacks in Pakistan, even as Kabul has taken some initial steps to rein in the group.

The report also pointed to growing operational and facilitation linkages among the TTP, Al Qaeda, Islamic State-Khorasan (ISIL-K) and the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA).

Pak-Afghan tensions

Ties between the two neighbours have been strained in the past few years as Islamabad continues to voice its concern over cross-border terrorism.

September witnessed another bout of conflict between Pakistan and Afghanistan.

On Sept 21, in response to recent major terrorist attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan conducted “calibrated” airstrikes in the border region with Afghanistan against terrorist hideouts, with the government saying more than 28 terrorists were killed.

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar described the action as part of Operation Ghazab lil Haq, which was launched on the night of Feb 26 in response to unprovoked cross-border firing by the Afghan Taliban.

Days later, Pakistan shot down eight drones launched from across the border that had entered Pakistani airspace near the Torkham border and Kohat. It was also reported that the Afghan Taliban engaged in unprovoked firing the night before near Kurram as security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to cross into Pakistan.

In retaliation to the drone incursion, Pakistan conducted “precision aerial and drone strikes” in 10 locations across Afghanistan.

On Sunday, the Foreign Office (FO) said a demarche was also delivered to the Afghan side on account of airspace violation by drones on Sept 23.

The demarche was delivered on Sept 26, the FO spokesperson said in a statement.

World.title: Consumer inflation eases to 10.3pc in September from 11.1pc in August, official data shows
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Consumer inflation eased to 10.3 per cent in September from 11.1pc a month earlier, mainly due to a sharp slowdown in food inflation, the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics said on Thursday.

The slight deceleration in the inflation rate, measured by the Consumer Price Index, reversed the sharp increase recorded in August, when higher food and energy prices pushed the annual rate to 11.1pc from 9.2pc in July.

The easing was more pronounced in rural areas, where inflation fell to 10.5pc from 12.2pc, while urban inflation edged down to 10.1pc from 10.4pc.

The September reading was also within the Ministry of Finance’s projection of 10pc to 11pc for the month in its Monthly Economic Update and Outlook for September 2026.

However, despite the decline in the annual rate, prices rose 1.3pc month-on-month in September. The annual inflation rate was 5.8pc in September last year.

The easing was largely driven by food prices. Food inflation dropped to 8.1pc in urban areas in September from 12.1pc in August. The decline was much sharper in rural areas, where food inflation fell to 7.7pc from 13.2pc a month earlier.

However, non-food inflation moved in the opposite direction, indicating continued pressure on household expenses. Urban non-food inflation accelerated to 11.5pc from 9.4pc in August, while rural non-food inflation increased to 13.1pc from 11.3pc.

The finance ministry had warned in its September 2026 outlook that inflationary pressures were concentrated in food and energy following the impact of higher global oil prices on domestic energy, transport and food costs.

In August, food, housing and utilities, and transport together contributed 8.2 percentage points, or about three-quarters of headline inflation. Food alone contributed 4.9 percentage points.

The latest data show that the composition of inflation shifted in September. While food inflation slowed sharply, electricity and transport costs continued to rise. Electricity charges increased by 15.28pc from the previous month, while motor fuel prices rose by 10.76pc in urban areas.

At the national level, transport costs increased by 5.75pc during September and were 27.43pc higher than in the same month last year. Housing, water, electricity, gas and fuels increased by 3.05pc during the month and by 12.39pc on an annual basis.

Core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy components, also eased slightly. It stood at 8.6pc in urban areas in September, compared with 8.8pc in August, while the rural rate declined to 8.1pc from 8.5pc.
